# Skill Author

Helps you write **new agent skills** that follow the best-practices documented at
https://agentskills.io/skill-creation/ — without you having to re-read those pages
every time. Pairs with `skill-creator` (which handles eval/iterate/optimize loops
once a draft exists).

## When to use this vs `skill-creator`

| Task | Use |
|---|---|
| "I want to make a new skill for X" | **skill-author** (scaffold + author) |
| "Scaffold the SKILL.md / a reference / a script" | **skill-author** |
| "Lint this skill draft" | **skill-author** |
| "My skill isn't triggering when I want it to" | `skill-creator` (description optimization) |
| "Run test cases against my skill, benchmark it" | `skill-creator` (eval loop) |
| "Compare two versions of my skill" | `skill-creator` (blind comparison) |

If both apply, start here, then hand off to `skill-creator` once the draft is solid.

## Workflow

### 1. Capture intent (1 minute)

Before scaffolding, get four answers — usually just by asking the user:

1. **What does it do?** (one sentence)
2. **When should it trigger?** (specific user phrases / contexts)
3. **What does it output?** (file, command result, plan, prose)
4. **Is the output objectively verifiable?** (decides whether `skill-creator` evals are worth the effort later)

Write these four down before touching files. They become the seeds for the
description, the workflow body, and the future eval set.

### 2. Scaffold

Use `scripts/new-skill.sh` to produce the directory layout. The script
auto-detects **scope** (where to put the skill) and fans out discovery
symlinks for non-universal agents so the skill is loadable immediately.

```bash
bash skills/local/skill-author/scripts/new-skill.sh <skill-name>
```

Three scopes (auto-detected; override with `--local` / `--project` / `--global`):

| Scope | Canonical dir | Symlinks created |
|---|---|---|
| **LOCAL** (this publishing repo: vendor.yaml / skills/local/ found walking up) | `<repo>/skills/local/<name>/` (or `skills/vendor/<name>/` with `--vendor`) | `.agents/skills/<name>` + `.claude/skills/<name>` -> `../../skills/{local,vendor}/<name>` |
| **PROJECT** (inside another git repo) | `<repo>/.agents/skills/<name>/` (universal agents — Cursor / Codex / OpenCode / Warp — pick this up directly) | `.claude/skills/<name>` -> `../../.agents/skills/<name>` (+ any already-present non-universal agent dir at the repo root) |
| **GLOBAL** (no git repo found) | `~/.agents/skills/<name>/` | `~/.claude/skills/<name>` -> `../../.agents/skills/<name>` (+ any detected non-universal agent dir under `$HOME`) |

The template's frontmatter has placeholders that lint will reject — this is on
purpose so the agent can't forget to fill them in.

> **Important**: When the user's intent is ambiguous (they're inside a git repo
> but haven't said whether the skill should live with the project or be
> available everywhere), **ask** "system-wide (`--global`) or just this
> project (`--project`)?" before running the script. The script is
> non-interactive — once you've picked a scope, files land and symlinks fan
> out without further prompting.

After running, the script emits a single JSON object on stdout with
`{skill, mode, canonical, symlinks[], next_steps[]}` so you can chain
follow-up actions deterministically.

### 3. Author the SKILL.md

Read `references/authoring-patterns.md` before writing the body. The patterns
that matter most:

- **Description must be "pushy"** and include concrete trigger contexts. Naive
  descriptions cause undertriggering — the #1 failure mode of new skills. Keep
  this within the cross-agent budget: 120-500 chars is the preferred range,
  501-900 is valid but context-heavy, 901-1024 is valid but close to hard
  loader limits, and >1024 is invalid for Codex/Cursor/spec-aligned skills.
- **Gotchas section** — environment-specific facts that defy reasonable
  assumptions. The single highest-value section in most skills.
- **Output templates** — agents pattern-match against concrete structures more
  reliably than they follow prose descriptions of formats.
- **Calibrated specificity** — be prescriptive only where the task is fragile;
  give the agent freedom (and explain *why*) where multiple approaches are valid.
- **Defaults, not menus** — pick one tool/approach and mention alternatives as
  escape hatches.

Keep `SKILL.md` under 500 lines. If you blow past that, move detail into
`references/<topic>.md` and tell the agent **when** to load it ("Read X if Y
happens"), not just that it exists.

### 4. Design any scripts

Before writing a script, read `references/script-design.md`. Skills script
design is meaningfully different from "regular" CLI script design because the
caller is an LLM reading your stderr to decide what to do next. The non-obvious
requirements:

- No interactive prompts, ever (agents run in non-interactive shells)
- `--help` is the primary interface documentation — keep it concise but complete
- Errors must say *what was expected* and *what to try*, not just *what failed*
- Structured stdout (JSON/CSV/TSV), prose diagnostics to stderr — separate them
- `--dry-run` for any destructive operation
- Pin versions for `uvx` / `npx` / `pipx` invocations

For Python helpers, prefer **PEP 723 inline dependencies** + `uv run` over
`requirements.txt` — the script becomes self-contained and the agent doesn't
have to set up an environment first.

### 5. Lint

Run the linter before committing or handing off to `skill-creator`:

```bash
bash skills/local/skill-author/scripts/lint-skill.sh skills/local/<skill-name>
```

It checks three things:

1. **Frontmatter & length** — `name` and `description` exist; name is
   hyphen-case and <=64 chars; description has a "use when" trigger phrase,
   respects the 1024-char hard limit, and SKILL.md is under 500 lines.
2. **Script hygiene** — every `scripts/*.sh` has a shebang, is executable, and
   responds to `--help` (presence of the flag handler, not necessarily a working
   script).
3. **Reference reachability** — every file in `references/` is mentioned at
   least once from `SKILL.md` (no dead reference docs).

Fix every error. Warnings are advisory but usually worth addressing.

### 6. (Optional) Hand off to skill-creator

Once lint passes and the skill *looks* right, the next questions are
quantitative: does it trigger reliably? does it produce good output? That's
`skill-creator` territory. Tell the user: "skill-author got the structure
right. If you want to validate it works on real prompts, the `skill-creator`
skill runs test cases and benchmarks."

## Available scripts

- **`scripts/new-skill.sh <name>`** — Scaffold the canonical skill dir
  (SKILL.md, references/, scripts/, assets/) and add discovery symlinks for
  non-universal agents. Auto-detects scope (LOCAL / PROJECT / GLOBAL); see
  table in step 2.
  - Scope flags (mutually exclusive): `--local` (force this repo's
    `skills/local/`), `--project` (force `<repo>/.agents/skills/`),
    `--global` (force `~/.agents/skills/`).
  - Other flags: `--vendor` (LOCAL only — `skills/vendor/<name>/` instead of
    `skills/local/`; rare, vendored skills normally come via `vendor.yaml`);
    `--root DIR` (override walk-up); `--no-symlinks` (skip the fan-out);
    `--dry-run`; `--force` (overwrite existing canonical dir + replace
    symlinks).
- **`scripts/lint-skill.sh <skill-dir>`** — Run frontmatter, script hygiene,
  and reference reachability checks. Exit non-zero on any error.
  - Flags: `--strict` (treat warnings as errors); `--quiet` (only print failures).

## Bundled assets

Templates that `new-skill.sh` copies and that you can reference manually:

- `assets/SKILL.md.template` — Frontmatter + workflow skeleton with placeholders.
- `assets/reference.md.template` — Reference doc skeleton (TOC + sections).
- `assets/script-bash.template` — Bash 3.2 compatible script with `set -euo pipefail`,
  `--help` / `--dry-run` flag handler, structured-output friendly logging
  (data → stdout, prose → stderr).
- `assets/script-python.template` — Python script with PEP 723 inline-deps
  block, argparse with help/examples, dry-run support.

## Reference files

- `references/authoring-patterns.md` — The agentskills.io "best practices"
  page condensed: gotchas, templates, validation loops, calibrated specificity,
  defaults-not-menus, procedures-over-declarations, plan-validate-execute.
- `references/script-design.md` — The agentskills.io "using scripts" page
  condensed: agentic CLI design, structured output, error message style,
  PEP 723, uvx/npx/pipx version pinning, dry-run patterns.
- `references/this-repo-conventions.md` — Conventions specific to *this*
  repository: where to put local vs vendor skills, how the 5-level skill
  search works, AGENTS.md ↔ CLAUDE.md sync, where mirrored scripts live.

## Gotchas

- **AGENTS.md is a symlink to CLAUDE.md** — edit either one; never replace the
  symlink with a real file.
- **Skill discovery is one level deep first, then recursive up to 5 levels.**
  `skills/local/<name>/SKILL.md` works because of the recursive fallback. Don't
  nest skills more than 5 deep or they become invisible.
- **`bash 3.2` compatibility** is required for any script that might run on
  stock macOS. No `mapfile`, no `${var,,}` lowercasing, no `[[ -v var ]]`.
  See `references/script-design.md` for the safe subset.
- **`description` is always-on context and has agent-specific hard limits.**
  Put concrete trigger phrases in frontmatter, but keep local skills in the
  120-500 char preferred range when possible. Treat >1024 chars as invalid:
  Codex and Cursor/spec-aligned validators can skip the skill entirely.
- **Don't write a skill that wraps something the agent already does well.**
  If a stock Claude session handles the task in one turn without help, a skill
  adds context-window cost for no gain. Test the no-skill baseline before
  investing in authoring.
- **Scope auto-detect can surprise you.** `new-skill.sh` walks up looking for
  a publishing-repo anchor (`vendor.yaml` / `skills/local/` /
  `skills/.claude-plugin/`) *first*, then a `.git`. If you ran it from inside
  a clone of this repo while meaning to add a skill to your *other* project,
  it'll silently land in `skills/local/`. Pass `--project` or `--global`
  explicitly when intent isn't obvious, and prefer asking the user
  system-wide-vs-project-wide before running.
- **Discovery symlinks must be `../../`-relative**, not repo-root-relative —
  POSIX resolves symlink targets relative to the link's own directory. The
  script enforces this and verifies each link with `test -e <link>/SKILL.md`;
  if you ever hand-create one, see
  [`pitfalls/symlink-target-relative-to-symlink-not-cwd.md`](../../../pitfalls/symlink-target-relative-to-symlink-not-cwd.md).

## When the user is updating an existing skill (not creating new)

Same workflow, but skip step 2 (scaffold). Read the existing SKILL.md first,
identify which patterns from `references/authoring-patterns.md` are missing or
weakly applied, and propose edits one section at a time so the user can sanity
check. After edits, run lint, then offer the `skill-creator` handoff for
quantitative validation.

```text
Selected short quotations (each <125 chars):

- "The ChordPro file format is a simple text file format."
- "The directives play an important part in how the printed output will look like."
- "As you can see, the lyrics of the song are interspersed with chords written between brackets `[` and `]`."

Concise extraction of ChordPro basics (paraphrased)

- File type and editing
  - ChordPro files are plain text and can be created/edited with any text editor or word processor.
  - Common filename extensions: .cho, .crd, .chopro, .chord, .pro ( recommendation: use .cho ).

- Inline chords and annotations
  - Chords are written inline between square brackets: use [ and ] around chord symbols.
  - Chords are placed in front of the syllable they belong to; when rendered they are printed above that syllable.
  - Annotations (text placed above lyrics similar to chords) use the syntax [*text].
  - Markup for styling text (size, color, font, etc.) follows a Pango-like markup language; available from ChordPro v6.

- Directives (structure and syntax)
  - Directives are lines that begin with { and end with }.
  - Directives control presentation (title, structure, comments, chorus blocks, etc.).
  - Examples of directive forms:
    - Key:value form, e.g. {title: ...} to set the song title.
    - Block markers with just a name, e.g. {start_of_chorus} and {end_of_chorus} to mark chorus sections.
    - Comment-style directive with text, e.g. {comment: ...} to show an inline indicator in output.
  - Directives affect how the printed/processed output is formatted.

- Other file-structure rules
  - Lines that start with # are ignored (used for maintainer remarks).
  - Empty lines are significant (separate verses/blocks) and are part of the format.
  - The format consists essentially of: lyrics with inline chords, directives, empty lines, and # remarks.

Notes / limits
- This summary is strictly drawn from the provided content; exact song lyrics from the source were not reproduced.
```

1	# CLAUDE.md
2	
3	This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.
4	
5	## Project Overview
6	
7	A personal agent skills collection installable via `npx skills@latest add daviddwlee84/agent-skills`. Contains custom-authored skills (`skills/local/`) and cherry-picked 3rd-party skills (`skills/vendor/`) synced from upstream repos.
8	
9	The skills CLI discovers skills by checking `skills/` one level deep for `SKILL.md`, then falls back to recursive search (up to 5 levels). The nested `local/`/`vendor/` structure works because of this fallback behavior — including vendor `series` subdirs (e.g. `skills/vendor/fullstack-nextjs/<name>/SKILL.md` at depth 4).
10	
11	## Commands
12	
13	```bash
14	# Sync all vendored skills from upstream
15	make sync
16	
17	# Check for upstream updates (dry-run)
18	make sync-check
19	
20	# Validate and render the repo backlog board
21	make kanban
22	
23	# Validate skills/.claude-plugin/marketplace.json (the catalog manifest
24	# that drives the grouped install UI of `npx skills add ...`).
25	make marketplace
26	
27	# Add a new vendored skill (auto-syncs)
28	./scripts/add-vendor.sh owner/repo/path/to/skill
29	./scripts/add-vendor.sh https://github.com/owner/repo/tree/branch/path/to/skill
30	# Group under a series subdir (skills/vendor/<series>/<name>/)
31	./scripts/add-vendor.sh --series fullstack-nextjs vercel/vercel-plugin/skills/nextjs
32	
33	# Add a structured TODO entry (preferred over editing TODO.md by hand)
34	./scripts/add-todo.sh --priority P3 --effort M \
35	  --title "Title" --description "Description"
36	
37	# Triage backlog/inbox.md (loose captures) into TODO.md
38	./scripts/sweep-inbox.sh             # interactive
39	./scripts/sweep-inbox.sh --batch     # only formalize parseable key=value lines
40	
41	# Move an active TODO item to ## Done with the right syntax
42	./scripts/promote-todo.sh --title "<substring>" --summary "<shipped summary>"
43	
44	# Create a new local skill
45	cd skills/local && npx skills@latest init [skill-name]
46	
47	# Docs site (MkDocs Material + llmstxt + copy-to-llm)
48	uv sync --extra docs
49	make docs-serve     # http://127.0.0.1:8000/
50	make docs-build     # produces ./site/
51	```
52	
53	## Vendor System
54	
55	- `vendor.yaml` — manifest of upstream skill sources with `last_sync` tracking (date + commit SHA). Optional per-entry `series:` field groups skills under `skills/vendor/<series>/<name>/`; entries without `series` stay flat at `skills/vendor/<name>/`
56	- `scripts/sync-vendor.sh` — downloads skill files via GitHub API (`gh` + `yq` required); honors the `series` field for nested destinations, and skips any entry carrying a `frozen:` block (see below)
57	- `scripts/add-vendor.sh` — adds entries to `vendor.yaml`, verifies upstream exists, deduplicates; pass `--series <name>` to group into a series subdir
58	
59	Sync uses the git trees API to recursively download skill directories (SKILL.md + references/ etc.) and updates `vendor.yaml` with the latest commit SHA.
60	
61	Active series in this repo:
62	- `fullstack-nextjs` — Next.js + Supabase + shadcn/ui + Tailwind + design/testing skills (9 skills from vercel/vercel-plugin, vercel-labs/agent-skills, supabase/agent-skills, anthropics/skills)
63	
64	### When an upstream skill is renamed or removed
65	
66	Upstream repos reorganize; `make sync` fails hard if a tracked
67	`upstream.path` no longer exists (the download step finds no files).
68	Handle the two cases explicitly in `vendor.yaml`:
69	
70	- **Renamed upstream** — update `name` + `upstream.path` to the new
71	  values, `git mv` the vendored dir, fix that skill's `skills[]` path in
72	  `marketplace.json`, and add a `renamed_from: <old-name>` field so the
73	  history stays greppable. Renaming changes the *downstream* install id:
74	  the `npx skills` CLI has no lockfile, so users who installed the old
75	  name won't auto-map on `npx skills update`.
76	- **Removed upstream** — freeze it with a `frozen:` block (`reason:` +
77	  `since:`). `sync-vendor.sh` then skips the entry in both `make sync`
78	  and `make sync-check` while keeping the last-synced copy and its
79	  `marketplace.json` entry. Don't delete a vendored copy just because
80	  upstream did — unless you also mean to stop shipping it.
81	
82	Live examples in `vendor.yaml`: `diagnosing-bugs` (`renamed_from: diagnose`)
83	and `zoom-out` (`frozen:`), both from the 2026-07-05 mattpocock/skills reorg.
84	
85	## Marketplace Catalog
86	
87	`skills/.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` defines the user-facing plugin
88	groupings shown by `npx skills@latest add daviddwlee84/agent-skills/skills`.
89	Located under `skills/` (not repo root) because the `/skills` subpath in
90	the install command makes the CLI read the manifest from
91	`<repo>/skills/.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` — see
92	[`docs/reference/npx-skills-metadata.md`](docs/reference/npx-skills-metadata.md)
93	for the full mechanism.
94	
95	When adding a new skill (local or vendored), also append its path to the
96	matching plugin's `skills[]` array in the manifest, or accept that it
97	will fall through to the **Other** group. Run `make marketplace` after
98	editing — the validator catches broken paths, duplicates, and reserved
99	marketplace names. Path format is `./local/<name>` or
100	`./vendor/<name>` (relative to `skills/`, not repo root).
101	
102	**Picker ordering is alphabetical-only.** `npx skills` sorts groups by
103	`plugins[].name` (A→Z) and skills within a group by their `SKILL.md`
104	`name` — the `plugins[]` / `skills[]` array order is ignored. To pin a
105	frequently-used group to the top, prefix its `name` with two digits: this
106	repo pins `01-project-memory`, `02-skill-authoring`, `03-infra-and-docs`,
107	`04-ml-workflow`, `05-notebooks`; the rest stay alphabetical. **These
108	`NN-` prefixes are deliberate — don't strip them.** Full mechanism +
109	within-group caveat in
110	[`docs/reference/npx-skills-metadata.md`](docs/reference/npx-skills-metadata.md).
111	
112	## SKILL.md Format
113	
114	Each skill is a directory containing a `SKILL.md` with YAML frontmatter (`name`, `description`) and markdown body with instructions, conventions, and examples. Vendored skills may include `references/` subdirectories.
115	
116	## Local Skill Discovery Symlinks (`.agents/skills/`, `.claude/skills/`)
117	
118	The `.agents/skills/<name>` and `.claude/skills/<name>` entries are
119	**discovery symlinks** that make a skill active in *this* repo's own agent
120	context (Cursor and Claude Code load whatever resolves under those dirs).
121	They are unrelated to distribution — downstream users get skills via
122	`npx skills add ...` + `marketplace.json` regardless of these links.
123	
124	`scripts/new-skill.sh --local` (run by the `skill-author` skill) creates
125	both links automatically. **Only keep them for skills that are genuinely
126	useful while working _on this repo_** — e.g. `skill-author`,
127	`mkdocs-site-bootstrap`. Skills authored here purely for downstream use
128	(e.g. `fastapi-ai-*`, `dvc-ml-workflow`, `mlflow-tracking`) should **not**
129	be symlinked: they would load into every in-repo agent session and just
130	bloat/pollute context without ever being exercised here. The canonical copy
131	under `skills/local/<name>/` is all that's needed for distribution.
132	
133	To author a downstream-only skill without the links, either:
134	
135	```bash
136	# Skip the symlinks at creation time
137	bash skills/local/skill-author/scripts/new-skill.sh --local --no-symlinks <name>
138	
139	# …or remove them afterward
140	rm .agents/skills/<name> .claude/skills/<name>
141	```
142	
143	## Project Memory Workflow
144	
145	### Long-term backlog -> `TODO.md` + `backlog/`
146	
147	When work is explicitly deferred, add it to [`TODO.md`](TODO.md) using the
148	fixed section order `P1`, `P2`, `P3`, `P?`, `Done`.
149	
150	- Active items must use `- [ ] **[Effort] Title** — description`
151	- `P?` items must use `- [ ] **[?/Effort] Title** — description`
152	- Non-trivial research should be linked as `→ [research](backlog/<slug>.md)`
153	
154	`TODO.md` is parsed by [`scripts/todo-kanban.sh`](scripts/todo-kanban.sh), so
155	do not invent alternate headings, nested bullets, or ad hoc checkbox formats.
156	
157	#### Three ways to add a TODO entry (preferred order)
158	
159	1. **Structured CLI — `scripts/add-todo.sh`** (default):
160	
161	   ```bash
162	   ./scripts/add-todo.sh --priority P3 --effort M \
163	     --title "Title" --description "Description"
164	   # add --backlog to also scaffold backlog/<slug>.md
165	   ```
166	
167	   This inserts a canonically-formatted line into the right `## P*` lane
168	   and re-runs the validator. Refuses to write a malformed entry.
169	
170	2. **Quick capture — `backlog/inbox.md`** (when priority/effort unclear):
171	
172	   ```bash
173	   echo "- maybe add docs versioning with mike" >> backlog/inbox.md
174	   ```
175	
176	   When the user asks "sweep the inbox" or "clear inbox.md", run
177	   [`./scripts/sweep-inbox.sh`](scripts/sweep-inbox.sh). It prompts for
178	   priority/effort/title/description per loose line and calls
179	   `add-todo.sh`. Use `--batch` for non-interactive runs that only
180	   formalize lines with parseable `key=value` pairs.
181	
182	3. **Direct edit of `TODO.md`** — fine if the format is fresh in your
183	   head; run `make kanban` (or `./scripts/todo-kanban.sh --validate-only`)
184	   afterwards to catch drift.
185	
186	#### Promote a TODO when implementing it
187	
188	When implementing a TODO item, in the same commit run:
189	
190	```bash
191	./scripts/promote-todo.sh --title "<substring>" --summary "<one-line shipped summary>"
192	```
193	
194	That moves the matched active item into `## Done` with the dated `Done`
195	syntax and re-validates the file. If a `backlog/<slug>.md` exists for the
196	item, also mark it as shipped (don't delete — keep it as historical record).
197	
198	Keep `## Done` as the recent history buffer. Prune it into `CHANGELOG.md` only
199	when it contains items from a previous calendar year or grows past 20 entries.
200	
201	### External skill / MCP / domain catalog -> `docs/catalog/`
202	
203	`docs/catalog/` is the vendoring decision log + external-awareness
204	registry, separate from `Skills` (what we ship) and `Reference` (our
205	own conventions). It has three subareas:
206	
207	- `docs/catalog/domains/` — per-domain hub pages (one per professional
208	  domain: Finance, Quant Research, AI/ML Research, Web & Fullstack,
209	  Knowledge Work, Agent Harness). Each hub aggregates local + vendored
210	  + external skills + MCPs relevant to that domain. New hubs copy
211	  [`docs/_snippets/domain-hub-template.md`](docs/_snippets/domain-hub-template.md).
212	- `docs/catalog/skill-collections.md` — single curated index of all
213	  upstream skill collections (Anthropic, Vercel, Supabase, marimo,
214	  Warp Oz, Orchestra-Research, etc.) with status per entry. Replaces
215	  the historical `Collections.md` (kept as a stub).
216	- `docs/catalog/mcp/` — MCP wiki, modeled after Karpathy's
217	  [LLM Wiki pattern](docs/reference/llm-wiki-pattern.md). One markdown
218	  file per MCP with required YAML frontmatter
219	  (`name / slug / upstream_url / transport / auth / hosting / domain /
220	  status / license / last_verified`).
221	
222	Every external entry carries a status enum (single source of truth in
223	`docs/_snippets/external-install.md`):
224	
225	| Status | Meaning |
226	|---|---|
227	| `vendored` | In `vendor.yaml` — link to the entry. |
228	| `deferred` | Open `TODO P?` item — link to it. |
229	| `skipped` | Looked at, chose not to vendor — inline reason required. |
230	| `evaluated` | Read but no decision — 1-line note. |
231	| `wishlist` | Surfaced but not yet evaluated — default for fresh discoveries. |
232	
233	Status changes trigger existing scripts:
234	`wishlist → deferred` runs `add-todo.sh`; `deferred → vendored` runs
235	`add-vendor.sh` + optionally `promote-todo.sh`. Full recipe in
236	[`docs/workflows/adding-catalog-entries.md`](docs/workflows/adding-catalog-entries.md).
237	
238	Every published catalog page is bilingual (`*.md` + `*.zh-TW.md`).
239	Snippets and `_template.md` are EN-only by convention.
240	
241	### Past pitfalls -> `pitfalls/`
242	
243	When a debugging session uncovers a non-obvious trap that could realistically be
244	hit again, write `pitfalls/<slug>.md` with:
245	
246	1. The verbatim symptom or error text
247	2. The root cause
248	3. The workaround
249	4. Prevention guidance or the hard invariant that supersedes it
250	
251	Use symptom-first titles so future agents can grep the failure they see, not
252	the explanation they do not know yet.
253
```

```text
Below I list every ChordPro directive shown on the page you supplied, give the exact syntax form used in ChordPro files, and note short (abbreviated) names when the page shows them. I only use wording from the page inside quotation marks; other phrasing is paraphrased.

General syntax rules (quoted)
- "{...}": directives are written inside braces.
- "the arguments are separated from the directive name by a colon `:` and/or whitespace." 

Form and examples
- Basic directive form:
  - {name: argument}
  - {name attribute="value" attr2='v2'} (attributes allowed)
  - {name argument} (single-argument may be given without colon)
  - Example from the page: {title: Swing Low Sweet Chariot}

Preamble
- new_song (short: ns)
  - Syntax: {new_song: [optional-args]} or {ns: ...}

Metadata directives
- title (short: t)
  - Syntax: {title: text} or {t: text}
- sorttitle
  - Syntax: {sorttitle: text}
- subtitle (short: st)
  - Syntax: {subtitle: text} or {st: text}
- artist
  - Syntax: {artist: text}
- sortartist
  - Syntax: {sortartist: text}
- composer
  - Syntax: {composer: text}
- lyricist
  - Syntax: {lyricist: text}
- copyright
  - Syntax: {copyright: text}
- album
  - Syntax: {album: text}
- year
  - Syntax: {year: YYYY}
- key
  - Syntax: {key: C} (or other key)
- time
  - Syntax: {time: 4/4} (or other meter)
- tempo
  - Syntax: {tempo: 120} (or text)
- duration
  - Syntax: {duration: value}
- capo
  - Syntax: {capo: n}
- tag
  - Syntax: {tag: name}
- meta
  - Syntax: {meta: name="value"} (used for arbitrary meta items)

Formatting and comments
- comment (short: c)
  - Syntax: {comment: text} or {c: text}
- highlight (document links to comment)
  - Syntax: {highlight: text}
- comment_italic (short: ci)
  - Syntax: {comment_italic: text} or {ci: text}
- comment_box (short: cb)
  - Syntax: {comment_box: text} or {cb: text}
- image
  - Syntax (attributes style): {image: src="myimage.jpg" scale="50%"} (single or double quotes allowed)

Environments (paired directives)
- start_of_chorus (short: soc) / end_of_chorus (short: eoc)
  - Syntax: {start_of_chorus: [label]} or {soc: label}  ...  {end_of_chorus}
- chorus
  - Syntax: {chorus: [label]}  (single directive form)
- start_of_verse (short: sov) / end_of_verse (short: eov)
  - Syntax: {start_of_verse: Verse 1} or {start_of_verse label="Verse 1"}  ...  {end_of_verse}
- start_of_bridge (short: sob) / end_of_bridge (short: eob)
  - Syntax: {start_of_bridge: label}  ...  {end_of_bridge}
- start_of_tab (short: sot) / end_of_tab (short: eot)
  - Syntax: {start_of_tab: [label]}  ...  {end_of_tab}
- start_of_grid (short: sog) / end_of_grid (short: eog)
  - Syntax: {start_of_grid: [label]}  ...  {end_of_grid}

Delegated environments (paired)
- start_of_abc / end_of_abc
  - Syntax: {start_of_abc} ... {end_of_abc}
- start_of_ly / end_of_ly (Lilypond embedding)
  - Syntax: {start_of_ly} ... {end_of_ly}
- start_of_svg / end_of_svg
  - Syntax: {start_of_svg} ... {end_of_svg}
- start_of_textblock / end_of_textblock
  - Syntax: {start_of_textblock} ... {end_of_textblock}

Chord diagrams
- define
  - Syntax example: {define: Name base-fret n frets f1 f2 ...}  
  - Conditional example from page: {define-guitar:  Am base-fret 1 frets 0 2 2 1 0 0}
- chord
  - Syntax: {chord: Name fingering...}

Transposition
- transpose
  - Syntax: {transpose: +1} (or other transpose value)

Font / size / colour (formatting directives)
- chordfont (short: cf), chordsize (short: cs), chordcolour
  - Syntax: {chordfont: name}, {chordsize: size}, {chordcolour: color}
- chorusfont, chorussize, choruscolour
  - Syntax: {chorusfont: ...}, etc.
- footerfont, footersize, footercolour
- gridfont, gridsize, gridcolour
- tabfont, tabsize, tabcolour
- labelfont, labelsize, labelcolour
- tocfont, tocsize, toccolour
- textfont (short: tf), textsize (short: ts), textcolour
  - Syntax: {textfont: ...}, {textsize: ...}, {textcolour: ...}
- titlefont, titlesize, titlecolour

Output / page control
- new_page (short: np)
  - Syntax: {new_page}
- new_physical_page (short: npp)
  - Syntax: {new_physical_page}
- column_break (short: colb)
  - Syntax: {column_break} or {colb}
- pagetype
  - Syntax: {pagetype: name}

Legacy output directives (from old `chord`)
- diagrams
  - Syntax: {diagrams: ...}
- grid (short: g) / no_grid (short: ng)
  - Syntax: {grid}, {no_grid}, or {g}, {ng}
- titles
  - Syntax: {titles: ...}
- columns (short: col)
  - Syntax: {columns: n} or {col: n}

Custom extension prefix
- Any directive beginning with x_
  - Syntax: {x_appname_directive: ...}
  - Note from page: these should be ignored by programs that do not handle them.

Conditional selectors (postfixed selectors)
- Selector syntax:
  - {directive-selector: args} — directive name is followed by a hyphen and selector.
  - Selection checks instrument, then user, then meta item; append "!" to reverse selection.
  - Examples from the page:
    - {define-guitar:  Am base-fret 1 frets 0 2 2 1 0 0}
    - {define-ukulele: Am base-fret 1 frets 2 0 0 0}
    - {comment-alto:  Very softly!}
    - Section example:
      {start_of_verse-soprano}
      ...content...
      {end_of_verse}
    - Note: "the section end must not include the selector."

Concise examples (exact syntax forms)
- Single argument (colon or whitespace):
  - {title: My Title}
  - {start_of_verse Verse 1}
  - {start_of_verse label="Verse 1"}
- Attribute pairs:
  - {image: src="myimage.jpg" scale="50%"}
- Paired environment:
  - {start_of_chorus: Chorus}
    ...lyrics/chords...
    {end_of_chorus}

Notes and constraints from the page (quoted short lines)
- "Many directives have long and short names."
- "It is always best to use the variant with explicit attributes."
- "To facilitate using custom extensions ... any directive with a name starting with `x_` should be completely ignored"

If you want, I can reformat this into a one-line cheat sheet per directive or produce a machine-readable list (JSON) of directive names, accepted attributes, and short names.
```
</details></tool-use>

<tool-use data-tool-type="read" data-tool-name="WebFetch"><details>
<summary>Tool use: **WebFetch**</summary>
 `https://www.chordpro.org/chordpro/using-chordpro/`

```text
Summary of chordpro CLI usage (concise, from provided docs)

Key actions and examples
- Render to PDF (choose output by filename extension or explicit generator)
  - By output filename (PDF selected from extension):
    chordpro --output=song.pdf MySong.cho
    chordpro -o song.pdf MySong.cho
    (Quoted description: "Designates the name of the output file where the results are written to.")
  - By explicit generator:
    chordpro --generate=PDF --output=song.pdf MySong.cho
    (You may also use --output out.html and --generate=HTML)

- Other output formats (examples)
  - ChordPro (functional ChordPro output):
    chordpro --generate=ChordPro --output=song.cho MySong.cho
  - Text inspection:
    chordpro --generate=Text --output=song.txt MySong.cho
  - HTML (experimental):
    chordpro --generate=HTML --output=song.html MySong.cho

- Transpose options (global CLI transpose)
  - Basic transpose up 2 semitones:
    chordpro --transpose=2 MySong.cho
    chordpro -x 2 MySong.cho
  - Transpose down 3 semitones, prefer flats:
    chordpro --transpose=-3f MySong.cho
  - Transpose up 1 semitone, force sharps:
    chordpro --transpose=1s MySong.cho
  - Quoted guidance: "Transposes all songs by the given number of semi-tones."

- Capo handling alternative
  - If you want capo removed and chords transposed instead:
    chordpro --decapo MySong.cho
    (Docs: use when you want transpose applied rather than showing capo.)

Config / configuration control
- Specify JSON config file(s):
  chordpro --config=layout.json --output=song.pdf MySong.cho
  (Option may be repeated; later files override earlier ones.)
- Avoid default configs (start from only explicit configs):
  chordpro --no-default-configs --config=layout.json ...
- Per-user / system config selection:
  chordpro --userconfig=user.json --sysconfig=/etc/chordpro.json ...
- Print or convert configs:
  chordpro --print-template-config        (prints template and exits)
  chordpro --print-final-config          (prints final calculated config and exits)
  chordpro --convert-config=cfgfile.json  (converts to RRJSON and exits)
  (Quoted: "This option may be specified more than once. Each additional config file overrides the corresponding definitions that are currently active.")

Info, version, help
- Version / about:
  chordpro --about
  chordpro -A
  chordpro --version
  chordpro -V
  (Quoted: "Prints version information about the ChordPro program.")
- Help and manual:
  chordpro --help
  chordpro -h
  chordpro --manual

Validation / strictness (lint-like behavior)
- Strict mode (default) enforces the standard; unknown directives raise warnings:
  chordpro --strict MySong.cho
  (Quoted: "Enforces strict interpretation of the input with regard to the ChordPro standard.")
- Liberal / lenient processing (suppress warnings for unknown directives):
  chordpro --no-strict MySong.cho
  (Quoted: "Enables liberal interpretation of the input with regard to the ChordPro standard.")

Other useful flags briefly
- Table of contents (PDF):
  chordpro --toc --output=song.pdf many_songs/*.cho
- Suppress CSV generation (PDF backend otherwise also writes CSV):
  chordpro --no-csv --output=song.pdf MySong.cho
- Generate chord diagrams in output:
  chordpro --diagrams=all --output=song.pdf MySong.cho
- Read list of input files from a file:
  chordpro --filelist=myfiles.txt

Minimal example workflows
- Single-song PDF with transpose and user config:
  chordpro --config=ukulele.json -x 2 --output=MySong.pdf MySong.cho
- Batch PDF with filelist and TOC:
  chordpro --filelist=songlist.txt --toc --output=Songbook.pdf

Quoted snippets (<=125 chars each)
- "Designates the name of the output file where the results are written to."
- "Transposes all songs by the given number of semi-tones."
- "Enforces strict interpretation of the input with regard to the ChordPro standard."
- "This option may be specified more than once. Each additional config file overrides..."

Notes / constraints
- The docs list PDF, Text, ChordPro (cho) and HTML generators; use output extension or --generate.
- Capo behavior can be replaced by transposition via --decapo.
- Strict vs no-strict controls how warnings for unknown directives are handled (use for lint-like tolerance).

If you want, I can produce a short cheat-sheet with 6–10 common one-line commands tailored to your typical workflow.
```

```text
1	---
2	name: slurm-hpc
3	description: Generic Slurm/HPC know-how for any cluster. Use when the user writes or debugs sbatch/srun batch scripts, requests resources (--mem/--cpus-per-task/--gres/--time/partitions), reads job state with squeue/sacct/sinfo/scontrol, cancels jobs, or reasons about resource isolation — cgroup CPU/RAM limits and GPU GRES (gpu vs shard vs mps vs MIG) and which of them actually fence VRAM so a misbehaving job fails alone.
4	---
5	
6	# slurm-hpc — generic Slurm workload-manager know-how
7	
8	Portable Slurm reference for authoring batch jobs and reasoning about resource
9	isolation on any cluster. Not tied to a specific site — for a specific repo's
10	recipes and layout, prefer that project's own skill.
11	
12	## When to use
13	
14	- Writing or fixing an `sbatch` script, or an `srun` command line.
15	- Choosing resource requests (CPUs, memory, GPUs, time, partition).
16	- Reading job/queue/node state (`squeue`, `sacct`, `sinfo`, `scontrol`).
17	- Reasoning about what isolates jobs (cgroups) and what fences GPU VRAM.
18	
19	## When NOT to use
20	
21	- Operating a specific project's cluster with its own recipes → use that repo's skill.
22	- Designing cluster provisioning/config from scratch → that's admin work, not this.
23	
24	## Batch script skeleton
25	
26	```bash
27	#!/bin/bash
28	#SBATCH --job-name=train
29	#SBATCH --partition=<partition>       # see `sinfo`
30	#SBATCH --gres=gpu:1                  # GPUs (see GPU section)
31	#SBATCH --cpus-per-task=8
32	#SBATCH --mem=32G                     # per-node; enforced as a hard cgroup cap
33	#SBATCH --time=02:00:00               # job killed at this wall-clock limit
34	#SBATCH --output=logs/%x_%j.out       # %x=name %j=jobid
35	srun python train.py
36	```
37	
38	Submit `sbatch script.sh`; inspect `squeue -j <id>`; after it ends,
39	`sacct -j <id> --format=JobID,State,ExitCode,Elapsed,MaxRSS,ReqTRES,AllocTRES`.
40	Cancel `scancel <id>`. `--start` on squeue estimates a pending job's start.
41	
42	## Resource requests
43	
44	- `--mem=<N>G` / `--mem-per-cpu=<N>G` — real memory; with cgroups this is a
45	  **hard cap** (see below). `--cpus-per-task` + `--ntasks` set core count.
46	- `--gres=gpu:N` or `--gres=gpu:<type>:N` (e.g. `gpu:a100:2`).
47	- `--time` is mandatory discipline on most clusters; jobs are killed at it.
48	- `--exclusive` gives the whole node. Partitions (`sinfo`) gate limits/priority.
49	
50	## Isolation: what actually fences a misbehaving job
51	
52	**CPU/RAM (cgroups, if the site enables `task/cgroup` + `ConstrainCores/RAMSpace`):**
53	a job is pinned to its cores (cpuset) and hard-capped at `--mem`. Exceeding
54	`--mem` triggers the **kernel cgroup OOM killer inside that job's cgroup only**
55	— the job dies alone; neighbours and the host are untouched. A thread-bomb
56	only saturates its own cores. This is real isolation and is the norm.
57	
58	**GPU VRAM — the gap.** Allocating a GPU does NOT cap its memory:
59	
60	| Method | VRAM isolation | Misbehaving job fails alone? |
61	|---|---|---|
62	| `--gres=gpu:N` (whole card) | n/a (owns it) | — |
63	| `--gres=shard:N` | **none** — accounting only | ❌ can OOM the whole card |
64	| `--gres=mps:N` (plain) | none | ❌ |
65	| `--gres=mps:N` + `CUDA_MPS_PINNED_DEVICE_MEM_LIMIT` | enforced cap | ✅ OOMs at its cap |
66	| **MIG** (`--gres=gpu:1g.5gb:1`) | **hardware slice** | ✅ strongest |
67	
68	Read `references/gpu-isolation.md` when the task is specifically about capping
69	or partitioning GPU VRAM, or choosing between shard/mps/MIG.
70	
71	## Reference files
72	
73	- `references/gpu-isolation.md` — read when capping/partitioning GPU VRAM or
74	  choosing shard vs mps vs MIG; has the config snippets and enforcement details.
75	
76	## Gotchas
77	
78	- **`--gres=shard:N` and plain `--gres=mps:N` do NOT fence VRAM.** Sharing a
79	  GPU ≠ isolating it. Only MPS *with a pinned memory limit set*, or MIG,
80	  enforces a per-job VRAM ceiling. A job with a wrong batch size otherwise OOMs
81	  the whole card and takes down its neighbours.
82	- **MIG needs a datacenter GPU** (A100/A30/H100…); GeForce/RTX cards can't do it.
83	- **`--mem` is a hard cap under cgroups, not a hint.** A job that needs more
84	  gets OOM-killed; bump `--mem`, don't expect bursting into idle RAM.
85	- **`sacct` needs accounting (`slurmdbd`) configured.** Without it use
86	  `scontrol show job <id>` (live only — gone after the job ages out).
87	- **A failing site `Prolog`/`Epilog` drains the node**, showing jobs as
88	  `PENDING` with a node `Reason=`. Check `scontrol show node`.
89	- **`srun --oversubscribe` is ignored under consumable resources** — you can't
90	  opportunistically grab more than you requested.
91

5	
6	# DVC ML Workflow
7	
8	DVC turns a git repo into a full ML lab: data and model files are versioned out-of-band (in a cache + remote), pipelines are declared in `dvc.yaml`, and experiments are run as ephemeral git commits with metrics and plots attached. No tracking server, no separate database — everything lives in your existing git history.
9	
10	This skill is opinionated about **the parts of DVC that matter for production ML work**: pipelines, queued experiments, metrics/commit binding, and remotes. It defers to the official docs at https://dvc.org/doc for everything else and links them inline so the agent always pulls the latest guidance.
11	
12	## When to use
13	
14	- User wants reproducible ML pipelines without a tracking server (`mlflow`, `wandb`, etc.)
15	- User mentions `dvc.yaml`, `params.yaml`, `dvc exp run`, `dvc queue`, `dvc push`, `.dvc/cache`
16	- User wants to do a hyperparameter sweep / grid search and have each run land as a separate commit with metrics
17	- User wants to version a dataset or model file too large for git
18	- User asks "how do I make my training reproducible" and is already on git
19	- User wants `mlflow ui`-style experiment comparison but **doesn't want to run a server** (DVC's `dvc exp show` + VS Code extension fills that role)
20	
21	## When NOT to use
22	
23	- User wants a hosted experiment dashboard with multi-user collaboration → use `mlflow-tracking` skill
24	- User wants LLM trace observability (spans, prompts, token costs) → DVC has no story here; use `mlflow-tracking`
25	- User just needs `git lfs` for a few large files → DVC is overkill; recommend `git lfs`
26	- User has an existing `mlflow` workflow and is happy with it → don't push DVC unless they ask
27

29	
30	- Docs root: https://dvc.org/doc
31	- Command reference: https://dvc.org/doc/command-reference
32	- User guide: https://dvc.org/doc/user-guide

34	- PyPI: https://pypi.org/project/dvc/
35	
36	When you're unsure of a flag, syntax, or behavior, **fetch the relevant doc page** rather than guessing — DVC's CLI surface changes between minor versions.
37	
38	## Core mental model
39	
40	Three orthogonal things, often confused:
41	
42	| DVC concept | Analogy | What it does |
43	|---|---|---|
44	| `dvc add <file>` | `git lfs track` | Snapshots a single file/dir into the cache, writes a `.dvc` pointer file (which **is** committed to git) |
45	| `dvc.yaml` (stages) | `Makefile` | Declares pipeline stages with dependencies and outputs; `dvc repro` re-runs only stages whose inputs changed |

40	MLflow ships a release roughly every 4–6 weeks. **Fetch the docs page** before answering version-specific questions (especially anything about LLM tracing, which is the fastest-moving area).

# Domains

Per-domain hub pages. Each hub is a single-page entry point that pulls
together the local skills, vendored skills, external (manual-install)
skills, MCP servers, and backlog items relevant to a professional
domain.

## Hubs

| Hub | Coverage | Status |
|---|---|---|
| [Finance](finance.md) | Banking, capital markets, equity research, wealth management, fund admin. | Populated |
| [Quant Research](quant-research.md) | Quant trading, factor research, backtesting, live execution. | Populated |
| [AI/ML Research](ai-ml-research.md) | Experiment tracking, model lifecycle, fine-tuning, agent frameworks. | Populated |
| [Web & Fullstack](web-fullstack.md) | Next.js / React / Tailwind / Supabase / Vercel / browser automation / web quality audits. | Populated |
| [Knowledge Work](knowledge-work.md) | Sales / legal / customer support / product / marketing / data / etc. | Mostly template |
| [Agent Harness](agent-harness.md) | SDD frameworks + agent harnesses (the layer above skills). | Template only |

"Mostly template" / "Template only" hubs are honest about being mostly
empty — they exist so the structure is in place when content arrives.

## How to add a new domain hub

1. Copy [`docs/_snippets/domain-hub-template.md`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/agent-skills/blob/main/docs/_snippets/domain-hub-template.md) to `docs/catalog/domains/<slug>.md`.
2. Fill in the elevator pitch + the 4 tables (Local / Vendored / External / MCP) — leave `_none yet_` for empty rows.
3. Add the new page to `mkdocs.yml` nav under `Catalog → Domains`.
4. Translate to `docs/catalog/domains/<slug>.zh-TW.md` (every catalog page is bilingual).
5. Cross-link from related hubs (`See also` section) and from any
   relevant reference landscape pages.
6. Run `make docs-build` (strict mode catches missing translations and
   broken links).

For the workflow on adding individual entries to an existing hub
(skills, MCPs, status changes), see
[Adding catalog entries](../../workflows/adding-catalog-entries.md).

## 1. Existing local content-skill structure

**Assets** — dvc uses `assets/*.template` files; mlflow vendors a whole `assets/docker-compose-stack/` dir.

## 3. Registering a new local skill

Canonical rules are in `/Users/david/Documents/Program/agent-skills/CLAUDE.md` (§ "Local Skill Discovery Symlinks" lines 116–141, § "Marketplace Catalog" lines 85–110).

- **Canonical dir:** `skills/local/<name>/` — this copy alone is what ships downstream.
- **Discovery symlinks (`.agents/skills/<name>`, `.claude/skills/<name>`):** For a **downstream-only** skill (which ChordPro is — it isn't useful while working *on this repo*), you should **NOT** keep the symlinks. Per CLAUDE.md, symlinked skills load into every in-repo agent session and just bloat context. Keep symlinks only for repo-dogfooding skills like `skill-author`, `mkdocs-site-bootstrap`. Two ways to author without them:
  - `bash skills/local/skill-author/scripts/new-skill.sh --local --no-symlinks <name>`
  - or create with links, then `rm .agents/skills/<name> .claude/skills/<name>`
- **Also append** `"./local/<name>"` to a plugin's `skills[]` in `marketplace.json` (or accept "Other"), then run `make marketplace`.

**What `new-skill.sh` scaffolds** (`/Users/david/Documents/Program/agent-skills/skills/local/skill-author/scripts/new-skill.sh`):
- Auto-detects scope (this repo → LOCAL) or force with `--local`.
- Creates `skills/local/<name>/` with `SKILL.md` (seeded from `assets/SKILL.md.template`, placeholders substituted) plus `references/`, `scripts/`, `assets/` each holding a `.gitkeep`.
- Unless `--no-symlinks`, fans out discovery symlinks: `.agents/skills/<name>` and `.claude/skills/<name>` → `../../skills/local/<name>`, plus any other already-present non-universal agent config dirs.
- Prints a single JSON object on stdout (`skill, mode, canonical, symlinks[], next_steps[]`); prose to stderr. Supports `--dry-run`, `--force`, `--vendor`, `--root`, `--help`. (Note: docs mention `lint-skill.sh` as the follow-up verify step.)

The seed template (`skills/local/skill-author/assets/SKILL.md.template`) already encodes the section skeleton observed in §1: When to use / When NOT to use / Workflow / Available scripts / Bundled assets / Reference files / Gotchas, and instructs a 120–500 char "Use when…" description.

CLAUDE.md line 45 also documents an alternative: `cd skills/local && npx skills@latest init [skill-name]` — but that won't apply this repo's template or symlink policy; `new-skill.sh --local` is the repo-native path.

```text
Here are extracted details about chord diagrams/grids from the provided ChordPro text.

1) {define} directive — syntax and purpose
- The directive defines a chord. Example syntaxes given:
  - "{define: name base-fret offset frets pos pos … pos}"
  - "{define: name base-fret offset frets pos pos … pos fingers pos pos … pos}"
  (each shown above as an exact example)

- The directive may also be written for keyboards:
  - "{define: name keys note … note}"

2) base-fret (offset)
- Called the offset or base-fret; it "defines the offset for the chord, which is the position of the topmost finger."
- Must be 1 or higher.
- When printing diagrams, the top row corresponds to the actual row at that position (so base-fret shifts which fret row is shown as the top).

3) frets (string/fret positions)
- "frets pos pos … pos defines the string positions."
- Strings are listed left (lowest) to right (highest).
- Positions are relative to (base-fret minus one). With base-fret 1 the topmost fret position is 1.
- Use 0 for open string; use -1, N, or x for a non-sounding (muted) string.
- There must be exactly as many positions as strings (6 by default).

4) fingers (finger assignments)
- "fingers pos pos … pos defines finger settings."
- This part is optional.
- For fingers, values corresponding to open or damped strings are ignored.
- Finger values may be numeric 1–9 or uppercase letters A–Z; other values ignored.
- For fingers there must be exactly as many positions as strings.

5) Keyboard chord diagrams
- For keyboards the keys list notes relative to the root (0 = root, 7 = fifth, 11 = dominant seventh, etc.).
- Root-position chords start with 0; first inversion commonly starts with 4 (major) or 3 (minor); second inversion starts with 7.

6) Whether diagrams are shown / diagram option
- A define may include "diagram off" to prevent a diagram from being included. Possible values: "on", "off", or a colour name; a colour value causes the diagram to be shown in that colour.
  - Exact quoted fragment used above: "diagram off"
- If a define supplies diagram properties (frets/base_fret/etc.) then a chord diagram will be included in output; if only name/properties exist but no diagram properties are provided, no diagram is included.

7) Copying/boilerplate behavior relevant to diagrams
- "{define: A copy B …}" copies diagram properties (base_fret, frets, fingers, keys) from B; you may then override some properties.
- "{define: A copyall B …}" also copies display and format properties from B.

8) Format strings for chord name/diagram display
- ChordPro uses a format string (metadata-style substitutions) to control displayed chord text; the default uses chord properties root, qual, ext, bass or name as fallback.
- When using a format string inside a define directive, backslashes must escape "%{" to avoid early substitution (example shown in text).

9) Grid environments
- The provided document does not define or mention a separate "grid environment" term beyond the chord diagram/grid examples and diagram options already summarized above.

Notes on quoting and source wording
- Exact quoted fragments from the source are enclosed in quotation marks and kept short (under 125 characters) as requested (examples above: "{define: name base-fret ...}", "{define: name keys ...}", "frets pos pos … pos defines the string positions.", "diagram off").

- show how base-fret affects a printed diagram with two small examples. Which would you prefer?

I searched for yt-dlp usage examples and docs for extracting the best audio and converting to WAV/MP3 (including Bilibili and SoundCloud). Below are concise, ready-to-run commands and short notes + sources.

Prerequisites
- ffmpeg (or ffprobe) must be installed for extraction/conversion. ([man.archlinux.org](https://man.archlinux.org/man/extra/yt-dlp/yt-dlp.1.en))
- yt-dlp supports Bilibili, SoundCloud and many other sites. ([github.com](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp))

Common commands
- Best audio → WAV (highest quality):
  yt-dlp -f "bestaudio" -x --audio-format wav --audio-quality 0 -o "%(title)s.%(ext)s" "URL"
  Explanation: -f "bestaudio" forces the audio-only format, -x (or --extract-audio) extracts audio, --audio-format wav converts to WAV, --audio-quality 0 requests best quality. ([mankier.com](https://www.mankier.com/1/yt-dlp))

- Best audio → MP3 (high quality):
  yt-dlp -f "bestaudio" -x --audio-format mp3 --audio-quality 0 -o "%(title)s.%(ext)s" "URL"
  (Same flags; change --audio-format to mp3.) ([mankier.com](https://www.mankier.com/1/yt-dlp))

Site-specific tips
- Bilibili (public videos): the same commands above work. For some Bilibili content (higher-res or member-only) you may need to provide cookies / login; use --cookies-from-browser chrome (or export cookies) if you need authenticated access. ([notes.hongdou.host](https://notes.hongdou.host/categories/technology/yt-dlp))
  Example (with browser cookies and output template including uploader):
  yt-dlp --cookies-from-browser chrome -f "bestaudio" -x --audio-format wav --audio-quality 0 -o "%(uploader)s - %(title)s.%(ext)s" "https://www.bilibili.com/video/…"

- SoundCloud: most public tracks are downloadable as audio; the same -f "bestaudio" + -x + --audio-format flags work. Example (MP3):
  yt-dlp -f "bestaudio" -x --audio-format mp3 --audio-quality 0 -o "%(title)s.%(ext)s" "https://soundcloud.com/artist/track" ([github.com](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp))

Extra options you may find useful
- --add-metadata to write metadata, --embed-thumbnail to embed cover art (when available). See yt-dlp docs/man for more flags and templates. ([github.com](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp))
- If you just want to list available formats before downloading: yt-dlp -F "URL". ([mankier.com](https://www.mankier.com/1/yt-dlp))

Sources (docs & examples)
- yt-dlp official repo / README (usage, supported sites). ([github.com](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp))
- yt-dlp man / examples (format selection, --extract-audio, --audio-format). ([mankier.com](https://www.mankier.com/1/yt-dlp))

---

# ChordPro Format & CLI — Reference for Skill Authoring

## 1. File format basics

**File extensions** (from the official intro): `.cho` is the *recommended* extension. Also recognized: `.crd`, `.chopro`, `.chord`, `.pro`. Files are plain UTF-8 text, editable in any editor.

**Inline chords**: chords go in square brackets immediately before the syllable they sit above — `[C]lyric`. When rendered, the chord prints above that syllable.
- Annotations (non-chord text placed like a chord): `[*text]` (e.g. `[*softly]`).
- Text markup (size/color/font, Pango-like) available from ChordPro v6.

**Directive syntax**: a directive is a line wrapped in braces `{ }`. Arguments are separated from the name by a colon and/or whitespace. All three forms are valid:
- `{title: My Title}` (colon)
- `{start_of_verse Verse 1}` (whitespace)
- `{start_of_verse label="Verse 1"}` (attributes — the docs note the explicit-attribute form is safest)

**Other structural rules**:
- Lines starting with `#` are comments (ignored by the parser).
- Empty lines are significant — they separate verses/blocks.
- Many directives have long and short forms (below).

**Core metadata directives** (all `{name: value}`):
`title`/`t`, `sorttitle`, `subtitle`/`st`, `artist`, `sortartist`, `composer`, `lyricist`, `copyright`, `album`, `year`, `key`, `time` (e.g. `4/4`), `tempo` (e.g. `120`), `duration`, `capo` (integer), `meta` (arbitrary: `{meta: name="value"}`).

**Formatting / comment directives**:
`comment`/`c`, `comment_italic`/`ci`, `comment_box`/`cb`, `highlight`, `image` (`{image: src="x.jpg" scale="50%"}`).

**Environment (paired) directives** — short forms in parens:
- Chorus: `{start_of_chorus}`/`{soc}` … `{end_of_chorus}`/`{eoc}`; recall a chorus with `{chorus}` (optionally `{chorus: label}`).
- Verse: `{start_of_verse}`/`{sov}` … `{end_of_verse}`/`{eov}`.
- Bridge: `{start_of_bridge}`/`{sob}` … `{end_of_bridge}`/`{eob}`.
- Tab (monospaced, chords not parsed): `{start_of_tab}`/`{sot}` … `{end_of_tab}`/`{eot}`.
- Grid: `{start_of_grid}`/`{sog}` … `{end_of_grid}`/`{eog}`.
- Delegated: `{start_of_abc}`, `{start_of_ly}` (Lilypond), `{start_of_svg}`, `{start_of_textblock}` — each with matching `end_of_*`.
- All environment starts accept an optional label; **the matching `end_of_*` must NOT repeat any selector**.
- Instrument/meta selectors are appended with a hyphen: `{comment-alto: Very softly!}`, `{define-guitar: ...}`, `{start_of_verse-soprano}`; append `!` to negate.
- Page/layout: `{new_song}`/`{ns}`, `{new_page}`/`{np}`, `{column_break}`/`{colb}`, `{columns: n}`/`{col: n}`, `{transpose: +n}`.
- Custom extensions: any directive named `x_...` (e.g. `{x_myapp_foo: ...}`) must be ignored by conformant programs — safe namespace for tool-specific data.

**Complete, well-formed example** (usable as an output template):

```
{title: Swing Low Sweet Chariot}
{subtitle: Traditional Spiritual}
{artist: Traditional}
{key: G}
{tempo: 90}
{time: 4/4}
{capo: 2}

# This is a comment line, ignored by the parser
{comment: Intro}
[G] [C] [G] [D]

{start_of_chorus: Chorus}
Swing [G]low, sweet [C]chari[G]ot,
Comin' for to carry me [D]home.
Swing [G]low, sweet [C]chari[G]ot,
Comin' for to [D]carry me [G]home.
{end_of_chorus}

{start_of_verse: Verse 1}
I [G]looked over Jordan, and [C]what did I [G]see,
Comin' for to carry me [D]home.
A [G]band of angels [C]comin' after [G]me,
Comin' for to [D]carry me [G]home.
{end_of_verse}

{chorus}

{start_of_tab: Outro riff}
e|-----0-----|
B|---0---0---|
G|-0-------0-|
{end_of_tab}
```

## 2. The official `chordpro` CLI

It is a Perl program, distributed on CPAN as **`App::Music::ChordPro`**, which installs two commands: **`chordpro`** and **`a2crd`**.

**Installation (most reliable path per platform):**

- **macOS (CLI — recommended):** use Homebrew's Perl, then CPAN:
  ```
  brew install perl cpanminus
  cpanm App::Music::ChordPro
  ```
  There is **no official Homebrew `chordpro` formula**. For a GUI, download the ad-hoc-signed `.dmg` (macOS 10.15+) from GitHub Releases — read the bundled README, since it is not signed by an approved Apple Developer.
- **Linux:** `cpanm App::Music::ChordPro` (canonical). The project ships an official package only for **Fedora**; an AppImage is also published on Releases.
- **Windows:** use the native installer from GitHub Releases, or Strawberry Perl + `cpanm App::Music::ChordPro`.
- **CPAN bootstrap anywhere:** `curl -L https://cpanmin.us | perl - App::Music::ChordPro`.
- Official install hub: https://www.chordpro.org/chordpro/chordpro-installation/. There is no emphasized official Docker image; CPAN is the canonical cross-platform route.

**Key command-line usage:**

```
# Render to PDF (format inferred from output extension)
chordpro --output=song.pdf MySong.cho
chordpro -o song.pdf MySong.cho

# Explicit generator
chordpro --generate=PDF  --output=song.pdf  MySong.cho
chordpro --generate=HTML --output=song.html MySong.cho     # experimental
chordpro --generate=Text --output=song.txt  MySong.cho
chordpro --generate=ChordPro --output=song.cho MySong.cho  # normalized round-trip

# Batch songbook with table of contents
chordpro --toc --output=Songbook.pdf songs/*.cho
chordpro --filelist=songlist.txt --toc --output=Songbook.pdf

# Config files (JSON; repeatable, later overrides earlier)
chordpro --config=layout.json --output=song.pdf MySong.cho
chordpro --no-default-configs --config=layout.json ...
chordpro --print-final-config        # dump the computed config, then exit

# Info
chordpro --about       # or -A
chordpro --version     # or -V
chordpro --help        # or -h ; chordpro --manual
```

Available generators: **PDF** (default backend), **Text**, **ChordPro**, **HTML** (experimental). A **LaTeX** backend exists historically but is experimental/limited — prefer PDF/HTML for the skill. Output to stdout with `--output=-`.

**Validation / lint / round-trip.** There is no dedicated `--lint` subcommand, but the intended mechanisms are:
- **Strict mode** (default): `chordpro --strict` enforces the ChordPro standard and emits warnings for unknown/malformed directives on stderr. `--no-strict` is the lenient/liberal mode.
- **Round-trip normalization**: `chordpro --generate=ChordPro -o out.cho in.cho` reparses and re-emits canonical ChordPro — the practical way to normalize a file.
- **How an agent should verify a generated file**: run it through the parser and check for warnings/nonzero exit, e.g.
  ```
  chordpro --strict --generate=Text --output=- MySong.cho
  ```
  If it parses without warnings on stderr and exits 0, the file is syntactically valid. Using `--generate=ChordPro` additionally shows how the canonical form differs from the input.

## 3. Transposition & chord handling

- **Transpose** all songs by semitones: `--transpose=N` or `-x N`.
  ```
  chordpro --transpose=2  MySong.cho      # up 2 semitones
  chordpro --transpose=-3f MySong.cho     # down 3, prefer flats
  chordpro --transpose=1s  MySong.cho     # up 1, force sharps
  ```
  Suffix `s`/`f` forces sharp/flat spelling. There is also a per-song `{transpose: +n}` directive.
- **Capo**: `--decapo` removes a `{capo}` and transposes the chords accordingly (instead of printing a capo instruction).
- **Chord parsing/normalization**: ChordPro parses chord roots/qualities/extensions/bass and re-spells them on transpose; it knows the difference between chords and annotations (`[*...]`). Chord display can be reformatted via a format string using properties `root`, `qual`, `ext`, `bass`, falling back to `name`.
- **Chord diagrams/grids**: defined with `{define: Name base-fret N frets p p p p p p [fingers p p …]}`.
  - `base-fret` = offset of the topmost shown fret (≥ 1); `frets` lists positions low→high string, `0` = open, `-1`/`N`/`x` = muted; there must be exactly one value per string (6 by default). `fingers` (optional) uses `1–9` or `A–Z`.
  - Keyboard chords: `{define: Name keys note … note}` (0 = root, 4/3 = third, 7 = fifth, 11 = maj7).
  - Instrument-specific: `{define-guitar: ...}`, `{define-ukulele: ...}`. Suppress a single diagram with `diagram off`; copy from another with `{define: A copy B ...}` / `copyall`.
  - Control diagram output globally with `--diagrams=` (e.g. `all`, `none`; the CLI accepts `--diagrams=all`).

## 4. Ecosystem tools

- **`a2crd` — the official "chords-above-lyrics → ChordPro" converter.** This is the answer to your converter question: yes, it ships with the CLI. It reads legacy chords-over-lyrics ("crd") text and emits ChordPro with inline `[..]` chords.
  ```
  a2crd input.txt                 # writes ChordPro to stdout
  a2crd input.txt -o output.cho
  chordpro --a2crd input.txt -o output.cho   # same via the main binary
  ```
  Note `--a2crd` (ASCII→crd) is distinct from `--generate=ChordPro`. It uses heuristic classifiers (e.g. `pct_chords`, `classic`) to distinguish chord lines from lyric lines; these are tunable and the output usually needs light manual cleanup. Config docs: https://www.chordpro.org/chordpro/chordpro-configuration-a2crd/ ; man page: https://manpages.ubuntu.com/manpages/stonking/man1/a2crd.1.html
- **Official editor/validator**: chordpro.org does **not** host an official online editor or validator. The official GUI is the desktop **ChordPro GUI** (wxWidgets), bundled in the macOS/Windows installers. There is no "try it online" demo on the site.
- **Third-party web converters** (chords-over-lyrics / Ultimate-Guitar-style → ChordPro): Band Central's ChordPro Converter (https://www.bandcentral.com/tools/chordpro-converter), Fretlist, obicreo, and various GitHub community projects. OnSong and SongBook apps also import/export ChordPro.
- **Reference material**: MetaCPAN distribution page https://metacpan.org/dist/App-Music-ChordPro (POD for `chordpro`, `a2crd`, `A2Crd`, config).

### Practical recommendations for the skill
- Emit `.cho` files with metadata block → `{comment}`/environments → verses/choruses; use `{soc}`/`{sov}`/`{sot}` long forms for readability and `{chorus}` to recall.
- Reserve `{x_yourskill_...}` for any tool-specific metadata (guaranteed to be ignored by conformant parsers).
- Verify generated files with `chordpro --strict --generate=Text -o - file.cho` (exit 0 + no stderr warnings), and offer `chordpro --generate=ChordPro` to auto-normalize.
- Offer transpose via `chordpro -x N[s|f] -o out.pdf in.cho` and import via `a2crd`.

**Sources:**
- [ChordPro format introduction](https://www.chordpro.org/chordpro/chordpro-introduction/)
- [ChordPro directives reference](https://www.chordpro.org/chordpro/chordpro-directives/)
- [Using the ChordPro CLI](https://www.chordpro.org/chordpro/using-chordpro/)
- [Installation](https://www.chordpro.org/chordpro/chordpro-installation/) · [macOS native install](https://www.chordpro.org/chordpro/install-macos-native/) · [Install on macOS](https://www.chordpro.org/chordpro/chordpro-install-on-macos/)

# ChordPro Format &amp; CLI — Reference for Skill Authoring

## 1. File format basics

**File extensions** (from the official intro): `.cho` is the *recommended* extension. Also recognized: `.crd`, `.chopro`, `.chord`, `.pro`. Files are plain UTF-8 text, editable in any editor.

**Inline chords**: chords go in square brackets immediately before the syllable they sit above — `[C]lyric`. When rendered, the chord prints above that syllable.
- Annotations (non-chord text placed like a chord): `[*text]` (e.g. `[*softly]`).
- Text markup (size/color/font, Pango-like) available from ChordPro v6.

**Directive syntax**: a directive is a line wrapped in braces `{ }`. Arguments are separated from the name by a colon and/or whitespace. All three forms are valid:
- `{title: My Title}` (colon)
- `{start_of_verse Verse 1}` (whitespace)
- `{start_of_verse label="Verse 1"}` (attributes — the docs note the explicit-attribute form is safest)

**Other structural rules**:
- Lines starting with `#` are comments (ignored by the parser).
- Empty lines are significant — they separate verses/blocks.
- Many directives have long and short forms (below).

**Core metadata directives** (all `{name: value}`):
`title`/`t`, `sorttitle`, `subtitle`/`st`, `artist`, `sortartist`, `composer`, `lyricist`, `copyright`, `album`, `year`, `key`, `time` (e.g. `4/4`), `tempo` (e.g. `120`), `duration`, `capo` (integer), `meta` (arbitrary: `{meta: name="value"}`).

**Formatting / comment directives**:
`comment`/`c`, `comment_italic`/`ci`, `comment_box`/`cb`, `highlight`, `image` (`{image: src="x.jpg" scale="50%"}`).

**Environment (paired) directives** — short forms in parens:
- Chorus: `{start_of_chorus}`/`{soc}` … `{end_of_chorus}`/`{eoc}`; recall a chorus with `{chorus}` (optionally `{chorus: label}`).
- Verse: `{start_of_verse}`/`{sov}` … `{end_of_verse}`/`{eov}`.
- Bridge: `{start_of_bridge}`/`{sob}` … `{end_of_bridge}`/`{eob}`.
- Tab (monospaced, chords not parsed): `{start_of_tab}`/`{sot}` … `{end_of_tab}`/`{eot}`.
- Grid: `{start_of_grid}`/`{sog}` … `{end_of_grid}`/`{eog}`.
- Delegated: `{start_of_abc}`, `{start_of_ly}` (Lilypond), `{start_of_svg}`, `{start_of_textblock}` — each with matching `end_of_*`.
- All environment starts accept an optional label; **the matching `end_of_*` must NOT repeat any selector**.
- Instrument/meta selectors are appended with a hyphen: `{comment-alto: Very softly!}`, `{define-guitar: ...}`, `{start_of_verse-soprano}`; append `!` to negate.
- Page/layout: `{new_song}`/`{ns}`, `{new_page}`/`{np}`, `{column_break}`/`{colb}`, `{columns: n}`/`{col: n}`, `{transpose: +n}`.
- Custom extensions: any directive named `x_...` (e.g. `{x_myapp_foo: ...}`) must be ignored by conformant programs — safe namespace for tool-specific data.

**Complete, well-formed example** (usable as an output template):

```
{title: Swing Low Sweet Chariot}
{subtitle: Traditional Spiritual}
{artist: Traditional}
{key: G}
{tempo: 90}
{time: 4/4}
{capo: 2}

# This is a comment line, ignored by the parser
{comment: Intro}
[G] [C] [G] [D]

{start_of_chorus: Chorus}
Swing [G]low, sweet [C]chari[G]ot,
Comin' for to carry me [D]home.
Swing [G]low, sweet [C]chari[G]ot,
Comin' for to [D]carry me [G]home.
{end_of_chorus}

{start_of_verse: Verse 1}
I [G]looked over Jordan, and [C]what did I [G]see,
Comin' for to carry me [D]home.
A [G]band of angels [C]comin' after [G]me,
Comin' for to [D]carry me [G]home.
{end_of_verse}

{chorus}

{start_of_tab: Outro riff}
e|-----0-----|
B|---0---0---|
G|-0-------0-|
{end_of_tab}
```

## 2. The official `chordpro` CLI

It is a Perl program, distributed on CPAN as **`App::Music::ChordPro`**, which installs two commands: **`chordpro`** and **`a2crd`**.

**Installation (most reliable path per platform):**

- **macOS (CLI — recommended):** use Homebrew's Perl, then CPAN:
  ```
  brew install perl cpanminus
  cpanm App::Music::ChordPro
  ```
  There is **no official Homebrew `chordpro` formula**. For a GUI, download the ad-hoc-signed `.dmg` (macOS 10.15+) from GitHub Releases — read the bundled README, since it is not signed by an approved Apple Developer.
- **Linux:** `cpanm App::Music::ChordPro` (canonical). The project ships an official package only for **Fedora**; an AppImage is also published on Releases.
- **Windows:** use the native installer from GitHub Releases, or Strawberry Perl + `cpanm App::Music::ChordPro`.
- **CPAN bootstrap anywhere:** `curl -L https://cpanmin.us | perl - App::Music::ChordPro`.
- Official install hub: https://www.chordpro.org/chordpro/chordpro-installation/. There is no emphasized official Docker image; CPAN is the canonical cross-platform route.

**Key command-line usage:**

```
# Render to PDF (format inferred from output extension)
chordpro --output=song.pdf MySong.cho
chordpro -o song.pdf MySong.cho

# Explicit generator
chordpro --generate=PDF  --output=song.pdf  MySong.cho
chordpro --generate=HTML --output=song.html MySong.cho     # experimental
chordpro --generate=Text --output=song.txt  MySong.cho
chordpro --generate=ChordPro --output=song.cho MySong.cho  # normalized round-trip

# Batch songbook with table of contents
chordpro --toc --output=Songbook.pdf songs/*.cho
chordpro --filelist=songlist.txt --toc --output=Songbook.pdf

# Config files (JSON; repeatable, later overrides earlier)
chordpro --config=layout.json --output=song.pdf MySong.cho
chordpro --no-default-configs --config=layout.json ...
chordpro --print-final-config        # dump the computed config, then exit

# Info
chordpro --about       # or -A
chordpro --version     # or -V
chordpro --help        # or -h ; chordpro --manual
```

Available generators: **PDF** (default backend), **Text**, **ChordPro**, **HTML** (experimental). A **LaTeX** backend exists historically but is experimental/limited — prefer PDF/HTML for the skill. Output to stdout with `--output=-`.

**Validation / lint / round-trip.** There is no dedicated `--lint` subcommand, but the intended mechanisms are:
- **Strict mode** (default): `chordpro --strict` enforces the ChordPro standard and emits warnings for unknown/malformed directives on stderr. `--no-strict` is the lenient/liberal mode.
- **Round-trip normalization**: `chordpro --generate=ChordPro -o out.cho in.cho` reparses and re-emits canonical ChordPro — the practical way to normalize a file.
- **How an agent should verify a generated file**: run it through the parser and check for warnings/nonzero exit, e.g.
  ```
  chordpro --strict --generate=Text --output=- MySong.cho
  ```
  If it parses without warnings on stderr and exits 0, the file is syntactically valid. Using `--generate=ChordPro` additionally shows how the canonical form differs from the input.

## 3. Transposition &amp; chord handling

- **Transpose** all songs by semitones: `--transpose=N` or `-x N`.
  ```
  chordpro --transpose=2  MySong.cho      # up 2 semitones
  chordpro --transpose=-3f MySong.cho     # down 3, prefer flats
  chordpro --transpose=1s  MySong.cho     # up 1, force sharps
  ```
  Suffix `s`/`f` forces sharp/flat spelling. There is also a per-song `{transpose: +n}` directive.
- **Capo**: `--decapo` removes a `{capo}` and transposes the chords accordingly (instead of printing a capo instruction).
- **Chord parsing/normalization**: ChordPro parses chord roots/qualities/extensions/bass and re-spells them on transpose; it knows the difference between chords and annotations (`[*...]`). Chord display can be reformatted via a format string using properties `root`, `qual`, `ext`, `bass`, falling back to `name`.
- **Chord diagrams/grids**: defined with `{define: Name base-fret N frets p p p p p p [fingers p p …]}`.
  - `base-fret` = offset of the topmost shown fret (≥ 1); `frets` lists positions low→high string, `0` = open, `-1`/`N`/`x` = muted; there must be exactly one value per string (6 by default). `fingers` (optional) uses `1–9` or `A–Z`.
  - Keyboard chords: `{define: Name keys note … note}` (0 = root, 4/3 = third, 7 = fifth, 11 = maj7).
  - Instrument-specific: `{define-guitar: ...}`, `{define-ukulele: ...}`. Suppress a single diagram with `diagram off`; copy from another with `{define: A copy B ...}` / `copyall`.
  - Control diagram output globally with `--diagrams=` (e.g. `all`, `none`; the CLI accepts `--diagrams=all`).

## 4. Ecosystem tools

- **`a2crd` — the official "chords-above-lyrics → ChordPro" converter.** This is the answer to your converter question: yes, it ships with the CLI. It reads legacy chords-over-lyrics ("crd") text and emits ChordPro with inline `[..]` chords.
  ```
  a2crd input.txt                 # writes ChordPro to stdout
  a2crd input.txt -o output.cho
  chordpro --a2crd input.txt -o output.cho   # same via the main binary
  ```
  Note `--a2crd` (ASCII→crd) is distinct from `--generate=ChordPro`. It uses heuristic classifiers (e.g. `pct_chords`, `classic`) to distinguish chord lines from lyric lines; these are tunable and the output usually needs light manual cleanup. Config docs: https://www.chordpro.org/chordpro/chordpro-configuration-a2crd/ ; man page: https://manpages.ubuntu.com/manpages/stonking/man1/a2crd.1.html
- **Official editor/validator**: chordpro.org does **not** host an official online editor or validator. The official GUI is the desktop **ChordPro GUI** (wxWidgets), bundled in the macOS/Windows installers. There is no "try it online" demo on the site.
- **Third-party web converters** (chords-over-lyrics / Ultimate-Guitar-style → ChordPro): Band Central's ChordPro Converter (https://www.bandcentral.com/tools/chordpro-converter), Fretlist, obicreo, and various GitHub community projects. OnSong and SongBook apps also import/export ChordPro.
- **Reference material**: MetaCPAN distribution page https://metacpan.org/dist/App-Music-ChordPro (POD for `chordpro`, `a2crd`, `A2Crd`, config).

### Practical recommendations for the skill
- Emit `.cho` files with metadata block → `{comment}`/environments → verses/choruses; use `{soc}`/`{sov}`/`{sot}` long forms for readability and `{chorus}` to recall.
- Reserve `{x_yourskill_...}` for any tool-specific metadata (guaranteed to be ignored by conformant parsers).
- Verify generated files with `chordpro --strict --generate=Text -o - file.cho` (exit 0 + no stderr warnings), and offer `chordpro --generate=ChordPro` to auto-normalize.
- Offer transpose via `chordpro -x N[s|f] -o out.pdf in.cho` and import via `a2crd`.

**Sources:**
- [ChordPro format introduction](https://www.chordpro.org/chordpro/chordpro-introduction/)
- [ChordPro directives reference](https://www.chordpro.org/chordpro/chordpro-directives/)
- [Using the ChordPro CLI](https://www.chordpro.org/chordpro/using-chordpro/)
- [Installation](https://www.chordpro.org/chordpro/chordpro-installation/) · [macOS native install](https://www.chordpro.org/chordpro/install-macos-native/) · [Install on macOS](https://www.chordpro.org/chordpro/chordpro-install-on-macos/)
- [Chord `{define}` directive](https://www.chordpro.org/chordpro/directives-define/)
- [a2crd configuration](https://www.chordpro.org/chordpro/chordpro-configuration-a2crd/) · [a2crd man page](https://manpages.ubuntu.com/manpages/stonking/man1/a2crd.1.html) · [A2Crd POD](https://metacpan.org/dist/App-Music-ChordPro/view/lib/ChordPro/res/pod/A2Crd.pod)
- [App-Music-ChordPro on MetaCPAN](https://metacpan.org/dist/App-Music-ChordPro) · [GitHub repo](https://github.com/ChordPro/chordpro) · [Releases](https://github.com/ChordPro/chordpro/releases)
- [Band Central ChordPro Converter](https://www.bandcentral.com/tools/chordpro-converter)

One caveat to double-check before shipping: the exact set of `--diagrams=` accepted values and whether the current LaTeX generator is still present vary slightly by release — confirm against `chordpro --help` on the installed version.</result>
