130	## Verify loop — never hand back an unvalidated `.cho`
131	
132	Every generated or edited file goes through the parser before you present it:
133	
134	```bash
135	scripts/validate-cho.sh song.cho          # wraps the command below; PASS/FAIL + warnings
136	# equivalently:
137	chordpro --strict --generate=Text -o - song.cho   # exit 0 + no stderr warnings = valid
138	```
139	
140	To auto-normalize to canonical form (fix spacing, round-trip directives):
141	`chordpro --generate=ChordPro -o song.cho song.cho`. If `chordpro` isn't
142	installed, the script prints the install one-liner — say so and offer to proceed
143	without rendering (the format is still human-checkable).
144	
145	## Finding existing chord charts (the usual first move)
146	
147	For a named/popular song, a human-made chart almost always already exists online
148	and beats audio extraction on accuracy. Search chart sites, pull the
149	**chords-over-lyrics** block, run it through `chordpro --a2crd`, then validate:
150	
151	```bash
152	# 1. search (中文: 吉他谱/和弦/弹唱谱; EN: chords / ultimate guitar)
153	# 2. WebFetch the best hit, copy the chords-over-lyrics into chart.txt
154	chordpro --a2crd chart.txt -o song.cho   # 3. convert
155	scripts/validate-cho.sh song.cho          # 4. validate
156	```
157	
158	Caption the result with a `{comment:}` naming the source and "published
159	arrangement — verify against the recording (capo/key may differ)". This is *not*
160	machine ACR, so don't use the `AUTO-GENERATED` header — but a web chart is still
161	one person's arrangement, not ground truth. Site catalog (91譜/Chord4/Ultimate
162	Guitar/…), format taxonomy, and legality → read `references/chord-tab-sources.md`.
163	
164	## Generating from audio / links — the fallback when no chart exists
165	
166	This is the shakiest path — reach for it only when no existing chart is available.
167	
168	**Set expectations first**: open automatic chord recognition tops out around **78–80% on simple major/minor pop**
169	and drops sharply on 7ths, extended/jazz chords, key changes, and quiet or dense
170	mixes; inversions/slash chords are unreliable; and it cannot know the capo a
171	guitarist used. Treat the result as a **draft to correct**, not a transcription.
172	
173	```bash
174	# Best-effort turnkey: link or local file -> draft ChordPro
175	uv run scripts/audio-to-chords.py --dry-run "https://youtu.be/..."   # show the plan first
176	uv run scripts/audio-to-chords.py -o draft.cho "https://youtu.be/..."
177	```
178	
179	The script downloads audio with `yt-dlp` (YouTube/Bilibili/SoundCloud) and runs
180	`chord-extractor`/Chordino. Its output **must** carry the
181	`{comment: AUTO-GENERATED — verify chords/key/timing}` header. On macOS the
182	Chordino Vamp plugin often isn't installed; the script detects that and prints
183	exact install guidance + manual alternatives instead of crashing — relay that to
184	the user rather than silently failing. Tool comparison, beat/key detection, and
185	commercial escape hatches (Moises/Songsterr have APIs; Chordify/Chord AI/Ultimate
186	Guitar don't) → read `references/audio-to-chords.md`.
187	
188	**Legal**: only process content the user owns or has the right to use, for
189	personal use, locally; downloading copyrighted audio can violate a platform's
190	ToS. Surface this — don't bury it.
191	
192	## Lyrics sources
193	
194	Default to **LRCLIB** — free, no API key, returns time-synced `.lrc`:
195	
196	```bash
197	uv run scripts/fetch-lyrics.py --artist "Adele" --track "Hello" --duration 295
198	uv run scripts/fetch-lyrics.py --plain --artist "..." --track "..."   # plain text
199	```
200	
201	| Source | Access | Synced `.lrc`? |
202	|---|---|---|
203	| **LRCLIB** | free, no key | **yes** |
204	| Musixmatch | API key; full/synced is paid | yes (paid) |
205	| NetEase / QQ Music | unofficial community APIs | yes (Chinese catalog) |
206	| Genius (`lyricsgenius`) | API token; lyrics scraped from page | no (plain) |
207	| Mojim / 魔鏡 | scrape-only | no (plain) |
208	| KKBOX | partner-gated | n/a |
209	
210	Full comparison, legality, and the LRCLIB API → read `references/lyrics-sources.md`.
211	
212	## Available scripts
213	
214	- **`scripts/validate-cho.sh <file.cho>`** — verify a file parses cleanly
215	  (`chordpro --strict`); PASS/FAIL to stdout, warnings to stderr. Guides install
216	  if `chordpro` is missing. Flags: `--help`.
217	- **`scripts/fetch-lyrics.py`** — fetch lyrics from LRCLIB (synced `.lrc` default,
218	  `--plain` for text). Self-contained via `uv run`. Flags: `--artist`, `--track`,
219	  `--duration`, `--album`, `--plain`, `--help`, `--dry-run`.
220	- **`scripts/audio-to-chords.py`** — best-effort link/audio → draft ChordPro
221	  (`yt-dlp` + `chord-extractor`). Degrades gracefully when the ACR backend is
222	  unavailable. Flags: `-o/--output`, `--lrc`, `--help`, `--dry-run`.

225	
226	Ready-to-open examples + a template under `assets/` (all songs are **public

241	## Reference files
242	
243	- `references/chordpro-format.md` — Read **when** hand-authoring or you need a
244	  directive beyond the cheat-sheet (`{define}` diagrams, `{transpose}`, markup,
245	  ABC/LilyPond, `x_` custom namespace).
246	- `references/chord-tab-sources.md` — Read **when** you need chords for a named
247	  song and have none: where to find existing charts (91譜/Chord4/Ultimate
248	  Guitar/…), how to adapt them, and the legality.
249	- `references/cli-and-rendering.md` — Read **when** installing, rendering,
250	  transposing, converting with `a2crd`, or validating/normalizing.
251	- `references/audio-to-chords.md` — Read **when** the user wants chords from an
252	  audio file or a link (ACR tool choice, beat/key, limits, escape hatches).
253	- `references/lyrics-sources.md` — Read **when** fetching lyrics (source table,
254	  synced-vs-plain, API-vs-scrape, legality, LRCLIB API).
255	
256	## Gotchas
257	
258	- **macOS has no official Homebrew `chordpro`** — install via CPAN
259	  (`brew install perl cpanminus && cpanm App::Music::ChordPro`). A signed `.dmg`
260	  GUI exists on GitHub Releases but the CLI is the CPAN route.
261	- **`Can't locate ChordPro.pm in @INC` after cpanm** — cpanm installed into a
262	  `local::lib` (`~/perl5`) that isn't on Perl's path. Activate it:
263	  `eval "$(perl -I"$HOME/perl5/lib/perl5" -Mlocal::lib)"` (persist in `~/.zshrc`).
264	- **No standalone `a2crd` in ChordPro 6.x** — use `chordpro --a2crd input.txt`.
265	  Its output needs a human pass (heuristic, column-based chord placement); always
266	  validate and eyeball before rendering.
267	- **Angle brackets `< >` are text markup in ChordPro v6.** Don't put `<...>`
268	  placeholders in lyrics/chords — the parser reads `<b>`/`<i>`-style markup and
269	  floods warnings. Use plain-text placeholders (see `assets/template-song.cho`).
270	- **No official online validator.** chordpro.org hosts docs + a desktop GUI, not
271	  a "try it online" box. Validate locally with the CLI (`validate-cho.sh`).
272	- **Chord accuracy from audio is ~80% at best** on simple pop, worse otherwise.
273	  Never present a machine-extracted sheet without the `AUTO-GENERATED` header and
274	  a "verify chords/key/timing" caveat.
275	- **Auto-generated chart sites are ACR in disguise.** Chordu / Chordify /
276	  GuitarTuna charts are machine-derived (~80%, same caveat) — treat them as drafts,
277	  unlike human-made charts on 91譜 / Chord4 / Ultimate Guitar.
278	- **Detected key is a suggestion.** ACR outputs absolute pitches; key detection
279	  confuses relative major/minor and keys a fifth apart, and enharmonic spelling
280	  (Gb vs F#) is ambiguous. Confirm with the user before committing `{key:}`.

```text
1	# Finding existing chord charts online
2	
3	Read this when the user wants chords for a **known/popular song** (by title, by
4	lyrics, or from a link) and hasn't pasted chords or supplied audio. For most
5	songs people ask about, **a human-made chart already exists on the web** — and it
6	is usually *more accurate* than machine audio→chord extraction (`audio-to-chords.py`,
7	~80%). So the reliable first move is: search chart sites → adapt the chart to
8	ChordPro → validate. Fall back to audio ACR or interactive fill only when no
9	chart is found.
10	
11	This is the router's highest-value path for "make me a chord sheet for `<song>`",
12	and it's what actually happens in practice — treat existing charts as the
13	default source of chords, not an afterthought.
14	
15	## The workflow
16	
17	1. **Search.** `WebSearch` for the song + a chart keyword in the right language:
18	   - EN: `"<artist> <title>" chords`, `... ultimate guitar`, `... chordpro`
19	   - 中文: `<歌手> <歌名> 吉他谱`, `... 和弦`, `... 弹唱谱`, `... 简谱`
20	2. **Fetch.** `WebFetch` the most promising result and pull the **chords-over-lyrics**
21	   block (chord symbols on their own line above each lyric line).
22	3. **Adapt.** If it's chords-over-lyrics text, run it through `chordpro --a2crd`
23	   (see `cli-and-rendering.md`) — that's exactly its input format. If it's already
24	   inline or a chart, transcribe it into the ChordPro template.
25	4. **Validate + caption.** Run `scripts/validate-cho.sh`. Add a `{comment:}` noting
26	   the source and that it's a *published arrangement to verify against the
27	   recording* (capo/key can differ between charts). Do **not** stamp the
28	   machine-extraction `AUTO-GENERATED` header — this isn't ACR — but do stay honest
29	   that a web chart is one person's arrangement, not ground truth.
30	
31	## Where the charts live
32	
33	Coverage and format vary; try a couple. **Text (chords-over-lyrics)** sites feed
34	straight into `a2crd`; **image** charts (many 吉他谱/简谱 scans) need manual
35	transcription (no reliable OMR). Auto-generated sites are effectively ACR — same
36	~80% caveat.
37	
38	**Chinese / Taiwan (great for C-pop like the 落葉歸根 case):**
39	- **91譜 / 91pu** — `91pu.com.tw` — large Taiwan library of ready 吉他谱/弹唱谱; often the fastest hit for Mandarin songs.
40	- **Chord4 / 和弦网** — `chord4.com` — chords-over-lyrics, capo/key noted (used by the eval runs).
41	- **弹唱谱 / 简谱 hubs** — `kanpu8`, `qupu123`, `中国曲谱网 (qupu.com)`, `17jita (17吉他网)`, `jitaba/jitapu` — mix of text and image; simplified-character search often finds more.
42	- **魔鏡歌詞 / Mojim** — `mojim.com` — mostly lyrics, some chords; good for confirming lyrics.
43	
44	**Western / global:**
45	- **Ultimate Guitar** — `ultimate-guitar.com` — the largest; use the **"Chords"** tab (chords-over-lyrics) not "Tab". No official API; scrape the page.
46	- **e-chords**, **Chordie**, **AZChords** — chords-over-lyrics.
47	- **Songsterr** — public API for tabs/chords (`songsterr.com/a/wsa/api-tabs-a26570`).
48	- **Chordu / Chordify / GuitarTuna** — **auto-generated from audio** → treat as ACR-quality (~80%, verify), not human-checked.
49	
50	## Format taxonomy (what you'll get back)
51	
52	| Format | How to use it | Reliability |
53	|---|---|---|
54	| Chords-over-lyrics text | `chordpro --a2crd` → clean up → validate | High (human-made) |
55	| Inline / chord chart | transcribe into the ChordPro template | High |
56	| Guitar tab (6-line) | embed in a `{start_of_tab}` block; or use for riffs only | High for riffs |
57	| 简谱 (numbered) / image scan | manual transcription; no reliable OMR | Low (tedious) |
58	| Auto-generated (chordu/chordify) | same as ACR — a draft to verify | ~80% |
59	
60	## Legality (surface it, don't bury it)
61	
62	These charts are user-contributed arrangements; the underlying songs are usually
63	copyrighted. Keep it **personal-use and local**, don't redistribute the fetched
64	chart or lyrics commercially, and cite the source in a `{comment:}`. Prefer this
65	route over downloading audio — it avoids the platform-ToS problem entirely — but
66	the copyright of the song itself still applies to any lyrics you embed.
67
```
</details></tool-use>

12	paste, bare lyrics, an audio file, or just a song title) and every path ends by
13	**validating** the output. It is honest about the one hard part — extracting
14	chords from raw audio is an ~80%-accurate *draft*, never an oracle — and falls
15	back to interactive, fill-in-the-gaps assistance instead of pretending otherwise.
16	
17	## When to use
18	
19	- User names **ChordPro** / `.cho` / `.crd` / `.chopro` / `.pro`, inline
20	  `[C]lyric` chords, or `{title:}` / `{start_of_chorus}` / `{soc}` directives.
21	- Convert an existing sheet: **chords-over-lyrics** text (Ultimate Guitar, OnSong,
22	  a lyric with chord letters on the line above) → ChordPro.
23	- Render / transpose / validate a `.cho` with the **`chordpro`** or **`a2crd`** CLI.
24	- "Make a chord sheet for <song>" starting from **lyrics only**, or from a
25	  **YouTube / Bilibili / SoundCloud link** or an **mp3 / wav** file.
26	- Ask about **lyrics sources** (Mojim/魔鏡, KKBOX, Musixmatch, LRCLIB, Genius,
27	  NetEase, QQ Music) — which give time-synced `.lrc` vs plain text.
28	
29	## When NOT to use
30	
31	- **Engraving staff notation** (notes on a staff, MusicXML / MIDI / LilyPond /
32	  MuseScore output) — ChordPro is lyrics+chords, not a score. Hand off to a
33	  notation tool. (ChordPro *can* embed ABC/LilyPond fragments — see the format
34	  reference — but it is not an engraver.)
35	- **OMR from a scanned score image** (photo/PDF of printed sheet music → notes)
36	  is out of scope; there is no reliable open path. Offer manual transcription
37	  into ChordPro instead, and say so plainly.
38	
39	## Authoritative sources
40	
41	- Format + directives + CLI: **https://www.chordpro.org/** (link, don't
42	  paraphrase from memory — the directive set evolves).
43	- Source / releases: **https://github.com/ChordPro/chordpro**.
44	
45	## The router — pick the workflow by what the user has
46	
47	| User has… | Do this | Reliability |
48	|---|---|---|
49	| A `.cho`/`.crd`/`.pro` file | Render / transpose / **validate** via `chordpro` CLI | High |
50	| **Chords-over-lyrics** text (UG/OnSong) | `a2crd` → light manual cleanup → validate | High |
51	| A **known song** (title / lyrics / a link) and no chords yet | **Search existing chord charts online** → adapt to ChordPro (often via `a2crd`) → validate. See `references/chord-tab-sources.md` | Med–High (**best first move**) |
52	| **Lyrics only**, no chart found | Fetch/confirm lyrics → **interactively** fill chords (propose from key, ask the user to confirm/correct) | Medium (human-in-loop) |
53	| An **audio file or link**, want a machine draft | `scripts/audio-to-chords.py` → *draft* with `AUTO-GENERATED` header → human correction | ~80% (last resort) |
54	
55	Prefer the highest row that fits. Two rules that matter: don't jump to the audio
56	pipeline when the user already pasted chords (`a2crd` is faster and correct); and
57	for a **named/popular song, search for an existing human-made chart first** — it's
58	usually more accurate than audio ACR and sidesteps the download-ToS problem
59	entirely.
60	
61	**Before charting a named song, confirm it exists as described** — user-supplied
62	artist/album is sometimes wrong, and searching a bad artist can grab a mislabeled
63	chart; a quick Wikipedia/LRCLIB match prevents shipping a misattribution.
64	**Non-interactive/batch runs** can't use the "ask the user" rows — instead produce a
65	best-effort chart from the published chord vocabulary, caption every uncertainty in
66	a `{comment:}`, and omit unknown metadata rather than fabricate it.
67	
68	## ChordPro cheat-sheet + output template
69	
70	- **Extensions**: `.cho` (recommended), also `.crd` `.chopro` `.chord` `.pro`.
71	  Plain UTF-8. `#` starts a comment line; blank lines separate blocks.
72	- **Inline chords**: `[C]` immediately before the syllable it sits over —
73	  `Swing [G]low, sweet [C]chari[G]ot`. Annotations (non-chords): `[*softly]`.
74	- **Metadata**: `{title:}`/`{t:}`, `{subtitle:}`/`{st:}`, `{artist:}`,
75	  `{composer:}`, `{album:}`, `{year:}`, `{key:}`, `{tempo:}`, `{time:}`, `{capo:}`.
76	- **Environments** (long / short): chorus `{start_of_chorus}`/`{soc}` …
77	  `{end_of_chorus}`/`{eoc}`; verse `{sov}`…`{eov}`; bridge `{sob}`…`{eob}`;
78	  tab (monospaced, chords NOT parsed) `{sot}`…`{eot}`. Recall a chorus with
79	  `{chorus}`. Comments: `{comment:}`/`{c:}`.
80	- **Key vs capo**: `{key:}` is the *written/fingering* key of the shapes shown;
81	  `{capo:}` is the capo used. If charts disagree, prefer the one whose chord
82	  vocabulary is internally consistent, and caption the *sounding* pitch.
83	- **Chorus recall**: `{chorus}` reprints the most-recently-defined chorus (showing
84	  only a "Chorus" label by default). With 2+ distinct recurring sections, label
85	  them — `{start_of_chorus: name}` … `{chorus: name}` — or expand the repeat.
86	
87	Emit this shape — metadata block → environments/comments → verses/choruses:
88	
89	```
90	{title: Swing Low Sweet Chariot}
91	{artist: Traditional}
92	{key: G}
93	{tempo: 90}
94	{time: 4/4}
95	
96	{comment: Intro}
97	[G] [C] [G] [D]
98	
99	{start_of_chorus: Chorus}
100	Swing [G]low, sweet [C]chari[G]ot,
101	Comin' for to carry me [D]home.
102	{end_of_chorus}
103	
104	{start_of_verse: Verse 1}
105	I [G]looked over Jordan, and [C]what did I [G]see,
106	Comin' for to carry me [D]home.
107	{end_of_verse}
108	
109	{chorus}
110	```
111	
112	Full directive set (chord `{define}` diagrams, `{transpose}`, markup, ABC/LilyPond
113	blocks, `x_` custom namespace) → read `references/chordpro-format.md`.
114	
115	## The `chordpro` / `a2crd` CLI (essentials)
116	
117	The official tool is a Perl program (CPAN dist **`App::Music::ChordPro`**). Current
118	6.x releases install the **`chordpro`** command; the chords-over-lyrics importer
119	is `chordpro --a2crd` (a standalone `a2crd` binary shipped in older releases and
120	may be absent — prefer `chordpro --a2crd`).
121	
122	```bash
123	# Install (macOS — there is NO official Homebrew formula; use CPAN)
124	brew install perl cpanminus && cpanm App::Music::ChordPro
125	# If `chordpro` then errors "Can't locate ChordPro.pm", activate local::lib once:
126	eval "$(perl -I"$HOME/perl5/lib/perl5" -Mlocal::lib)"   # add to ~/.zshrc to persist
127	
128	# Render
129	chordpro -o song.pdf song.cho          # PDF (format inferred from extension)
130	chordpro --generate=HTML -o song.html song.cho
131	
132	# Transpose (N semitones; suffix s/f forces sharp/flat spelling)
133	chordpro -x 2  -o up.pdf   song.cho
134	chordpro -x -3f -o down.pdf song.cho
135	
136	# Convert chords-over-lyrics text -> ChordPro (the official importer)
137	chordpro --a2crd input.txt -o song.cho
138	```
139	
140	Install-per-platform, generators, config JSON, songbook `--toc`, and `a2crd`
141	heuristic tuning → read `references/cli-and-rendering.md`.
142	
143	## Verify loop — never hand back an unvalidated `.cho`
144	
145	Every generated or edited file goes through the parser before you present it:
146	
147	```bash
148	scripts/validate-cho.sh song.cho          # wraps the command below; PASS/FAIL + warnings
149	# equivalently:
150	chordpro --strict --generate=Text -o - song.cho   # exit 0 + no stderr warnings = valid
151	```
152	
153	To auto-normalize to canonical form (fix spacing, round-trip directives):
154	`chordpro --generate=ChordPro -o song.cho song.cho`. If `chordpro` isn't
155	installed, the script prints the install one-liner — say so and offer to proceed
156	without rendering (the format is still human-checkable).
157	
158	**Producing a PDF? Verify it *renders*, not just parses.** `validate-cho.sh` only
159	checks that the file parses — it can't see a broken PDF. `chordpro`'s default
160	fonts have **no CJK glyphs**, so a Chinese/Japanese/Korean song renders as blank
161	tofu while still exiting 0 and passing validation. Use `scripts/render-cho.sh
162	song.cho` — it auto-detects a CJK font, renders, and glyph-checks the PDF (fails
163	loudly on tofu).
164	
165	## Finding existing chord charts (the usual first move)
166	
167	For a named/popular song, a human-made chart almost always already exists online
168	and beats audio extraction on accuracy. The realistic recipe (WebFetch's
169	summarizer strips copyrighted lyrics, and `a2crd`'s column logic mis-aligns
170	full-width CJK — so neither is the happy path it looks like):
171	
172	```bash
173	# 1. search (中文: 吉他谱/和弦/弹唱谱; EN: chords / ultimate guitar)
174	# 2. fetch the RAW html (WebFetch drops the lyrics) and parse chords from the
175	#    site's markup — e.g. Chord4 parenthesized-syllable, UG js-store data-content.
176	curl -sL "<chart-url>" -o chart.html
177	# 3. lyrics come SEPARATELY from LRCLIB (reliable, synced):
178	uv run scripts/fetch-lyrics.py --artist "…" --track "…" -o song.lrc
179	# 4. align the chart's chords onto the lyric syllables by phrase, NOT by column
180	#    (CJK chars are 2 display cells). For pure-Latin chords-over-lyrics you can
181	#    still use:  chordpro --a2crd chart.txt -o song.cho
182	scripts/validate-cho.sh song.cho && scripts/render-cho.sh song.cho   # 5. validate + render (CJK-safe)
183	```
184	
185	Caption the result with a `{comment:}` naming the source and "published
186	arrangement — verify against the recording (capo/key may differ)". Not machine
187	ACR, so no `AUTO-GENERATED` header. Per-site extraction patterns, the site catalog
188	(91譜/Chord4/UG — many are JS-rendered or image-only 六线谱), simplified↔traditional
189	handling, and legality → read `references/chord-tab-sources.md`.
190	
191	## Generating from audio / links — the fallback when no chart exists
192	
193	This is the shakiest path — reach for it only when no existing chart is available.
194	
195	**Set expectations first**: open automatic chord recognition tops out around **78–80% on simple major/minor pop**
196	and drops sharply on 7ths, extended/jazz chords, key changes, and quiet or dense
197	mixes; inversions/slash chords are unreliable; and it cannot know the capo a
198	guitarist used. Treat the result as a **draft to correct**, not a transcription.
199	
200	```bash
201	# Best-effort turnkey: link or local file -> draft ChordPro
202	uv run scripts/audio-to-chords.py --dry-run "https://youtu.be/..."   # show the plan first
203	uv run scripts/audio-to-chords.py -o draft.cho "https://youtu.be/..."
204	```
205	
206	The script downloads audio with `yt-dlp` (YouTube/Bilibili/SoundCloud) and runs
207	`chord-extractor`/Chordino. Its output **must** carry the
208	`{comment: AUTO-GENERATED — verify chords/key/timing}` header. On macOS the
209	Chordino Vamp plugin often isn't installed; the script detects that and prints
210	exact install guidance + manual alternatives instead of crashing — relay that to
211	the user rather than silently failing. Tool comparison, beat/key detection, and
212	commercial escape hatches (Moises/Songsterr have APIs; Chordify/Chord AI/Ultimate
213	Guitar don't) → read `references/audio-to-chords.md`.
214	
215	**Legal**: only process content the user owns or has the right to use, for
216	personal use, locally; downloading copyrighted audio can violate a platform's
217	ToS. Surface this — don't bury it.
218	
219	## Lyrics sources
220	
221	Default to **LRCLIB** — free, no API key, returns time-synced `.lrc`:
222	
223	```bash
224	uv run scripts/fetch-lyrics.py --artist "Adele" --track "Hello" --duration 295
225	uv run scripts/fetch-lyrics.py --plain --artist "..." --track "..."   # plain text
226	```
227	
228	| Source | Access | Synced `.lrc`? |
229	|---|---|---|
230	| **LRCLIB** | free, no key | **yes** |
231	| Musixmatch | API key; full/synced is paid | yes (paid) |
232	| NetEase / QQ Music | unofficial community APIs | yes (Chinese catalog) |
233	| Genius (`lyricsgenius`) | API token; lyrics scraped from page | no (plain) |
234	| Mojim / 魔鏡 | scrape-only | no (plain) |
235	| KKBOX | partner-gated | n/a |
236	
237	Full comparison, legality, and the LRCLIB API → read `references/lyrics-sources.md`.
238	
239	## Available scripts
240	
241	- **`scripts/validate-cho.sh <file.cho>`** — verify a file parses cleanly
242	  (`chordpro --strict`); PASS/FAIL to stdout, warnings to stderr. Guides install
243	  if `chordpro` is missing. Flags: `--help`.
244	- **`scripts/render-cho.sh <file.cho>`** — render to PDF with a **CJK-safe** font
245	  (auto-detected) and glyph-check the result, so a Chinese song can't silently
246	  render as tofu. Flags: `-o/--output`, `--font`, `--keep-config`, `--help`.
247	- **`scripts/fetch-lyrics.py`** — fetch lyrics from LRCLIB (synced `.lrc` default,
248	  `--plain` for text). Auto-retries a CJK miss with a romanized/pinyin query.
249	  Self-contained via `uv run`. Flags: `--artist`, `--track`, `--duration`,
250	  `--album`, `--plain`, `-o/--output`, `--help`, `--dry-run`.
251	- **`scripts/audio-to-chords.py`** — best-effort link/audio → draft ChordPro
252	  (`yt-dlp` + `chord-extractor`). Degrades gracefully when the ACR backend is
253	  unavailable. Flags: `-o/--output`, `--lrc`, `--help`, `--dry-run`.
254	
255	## Bundled assets
256	
257	Ready-to-open examples + a template under `assets/` (all songs are **public
258	domain**; every `.cho` validates clean with `chordpro --strict`). Use them as
259	copy-paste starting points and few-shot references:
260	
261	- `assets/example-amazing-grace.cho` — simplest real song: metadata + inline chords.
262	- `assets/example-when-the-saints.cho` — chorus/verse structure + `{chorus}` recall.
263	- `assets/example-greensleeves.cho` — feature showcase: `{define}` diagrams, a
264	  `{sot}` tab block, chorus recall, transpose note.
265	- `assets/template-song.cho` — fill-in-the-blanks scaffold (renders as-is); the
266	  starting point for the interactive chord-fill flow.
267	- `assets/example-synced-lyrics.lrc` — sample time-synced `.lrc` (what
268	  `fetch-lyrics.py` returns; feed it to `audio-to-chords.py --lrc`).
269	- `assets/example-a2crd-input.txt` — chords-over-lyrics plain text; convert with
270	  `chordpro --a2crd assets/example-a2crd-input.txt`.
271	
272	## Reference files
273	
274	- `references/chordpro-format.md` — Read **when** hand-authoring or you need a
275	  directive beyond the cheat-sheet (`{define}` diagrams, `{transpose}`, markup,
276	  ABC/LilyPond, `x_` custom namespace).
277	- `references/chord-tab-sources.md` — Read **when** you need chords for a named
278	  song and have none: where to find existing charts (91譜/Chord4/Ultimate
279	  Guitar/…), how to adapt them, and the legality.
280	- `references/cli-and-rendering.md` — Read **when** installing, rendering,
281	  transposing, converting with `a2crd`, or validating/normalizing.
282	- `references/audio-to-chords.md` — Read **when** the user wants chords from an
283	  audio file or a link (ACR tool choice, beat/key, limits, escape hatches).
284	- `references/lyrics-sources.md` — Read **when** fetching lyrics (source table,
285	  synced-vs-plain, API-vs-scrape, legality, LRCLIB API).
286	
287	## Gotchas
288	
289	- **macOS has no official Homebrew `chordpro`** — install via CPAN
290	  (`brew install perl cpanminus && cpanm App::Music::ChordPro`). A signed `.dmg`
291	  GUI exists on GitHub Releases but the CLI is the CPAN route.
292	- **`Can't locate ChordPro.pm in @INC` after cpanm** — cpanm installed into a
293	  `local::lib` (`~/perl5`) that isn't on Perl's path. Activate it:
294	  `eval "$(perl -I"$HOME/perl5/lib/perl5" -Mlocal::lib)"` (persist in `~/.zshrc`).
295	- **No standalone `a2crd` in ChordPro 6.x** — use `chordpro --a2crd input.txt`.
296	  Its output needs a human pass (heuristic, column-based chord placement); always
297	  validate and eyeball before rendering.
298	- **Angle brackets `< >` are text markup in ChordPro v6.** Don't put `<...>`
299	  placeholders in lyrics/chords — the parser reads `<b>`/`<i>`-style markup and
300	  floods warnings. Use plain-text placeholders (see `assets/template-song.cho`).
301	- **No official online validator.** chordpro.org hosts docs + a desktop GUI, not
302	  a "try it online" box. Validate locally with the CLI (`validate-cho.sh`).
303	- **CJK renders as tofu by default — and passes validation.** `chordpro`'s default
304	  fonts have no Han/Kana/Hangul glyphs, so a Chinese/Japanese/Korean song produces
305	  a blank PDF that still exits 0 and passes `validate-cho.sh` (which only checks
306	  parsing). Render CJK with `scripts/render-cho.sh` (auto CJK font + glyph-check),
307	  or pass `--config` pointing `pdf.fonts.*` at a CJK font.
308	- **`a2crd` is Latin-only.** Its column heuristic assumes 1 char = 1 column, but
309	  full-width CJK occupies 2 display cells, so chords drift. For CJK, align chords to
310	  syllables/phrases by musical judgment — don't trust column arithmetic.
311	- **A strict "Unknown chord" warning ≠ a parse error.** `chordpro --strict` warns
312	  "Unknown chord" for a *valid* chord it has no built-in diagram for (e.g. `Em/C#`,
313	  `F#m7b5`); it still renders. Add a `{define}` (see the format reference) or ignore.
314	- **`{chorus}` recall is a trap with 2+ recurring sections.** It reprints only the
315	  most-recently-defined chorus, as a bare "Chorus" tag by default. Label distinct
316	  blocks (`{start_of_chorus: name}` / `{chorus: name}`) or expand repeats explicitly.
317	- **`WebFetch` strips copyrighted lyrics** (returns "[lyrics omitted]"), so the
318	  chart-fetch path needs raw `curl` + per-site parsing; and from an image-only chart
319	  `WebFetch` may *fabricate* chord placement — trust only an explicit chord list.
320	- **Chord accuracy from audio is ~80% at best** on simple pop, worse otherwise.
321	  Never present a machine-extracted sheet without the `AUTO-GENERATED` header and
322	  a "verify chords/key/timing" caveat.
323	- **Auto-generated chart sites are ACR in disguise.** Chordu / Chordify /
324	  GuitarTuna charts are machine-derived (~80%, same caveat) — treat them as drafts,
325	  unlike human-made charts on 91譜 / Chord4 / Ultimate Guitar.
326	- **Detected key is a suggestion.** ACR outputs absolute pitches; key detection
327	  confuses relative major/minor and keys a fifth apart, and enharmonic spelling
328	  (Gb vs F#) is ambiguous. Confirm with the user before committing `{key:}`.
329	- **Chords in `{sot}`…`{eot}` tab blocks are NOT parsed** — that's for ASCII tab.
330	  Use inline `[..]` in verses/choruses; reserve tab blocks for fret diagrams.
331	- **Lyrics/audio ToS.** Prefer LRCLIB (open); most other lyric sources are
332	  scrape-only or paid, and downloading audio has copyright/ToS limits. Keep it
333	  personal-use and local; surface the caveat rather than hiding it.
334
```

56	pipeline when the user already pasted chords (`a2crd` is faster and correct); and
57	for a **named/popular song, search for an existing human-made chart first** — it's
58	usually more accurate than audio ACR and sidesteps the download-ToS problem
59	entirely.
60	
61	**Before charting a named song, confirm it exists as described** — user-supplied
62	artist/album is sometimes wrong, and searching a bad artist can grab a mislabeled
63	chart; a quick Wikipedia/LRCLIB match prevents shipping a misattribution.
64	**Non-interactive/batch runs** can't use the "ask the user" rows — instead produce a
65	best-effort chart from the published chord vocabulary, caption every uncertainty in
66	a `{comment:}`, and omit unknown metadata rather than fabricate it.
67	
68	## ChordPro cheat-sheet + output template
69	
70	- **Extensions**: `.cho` (recommended), also `.crd` `.chopro` `.chord` `.pro`.
71	  Plain UTF-8. `#` starts a comment line; blank lines separate blocks.
72	- **Inline chords**: `[C]` immediately before the syllable it sits over —
73	  `Swing [G]low, sweet [C]chari[G]ot`. Annotations (non-chords): `[*softly]`.
74	- **Metadata**: `{title:}`/`{t:}`, `{subtitle:}`/`{st:}`, `{artist:}`,
75	  `{composer:}`, `{album:}`, `{year:}`, `{key:}`, `{tempo:}`, `{time:}`, `{capo:}`.
76	- **Environments** (long / short): chorus `{start_of_chorus}`/`{soc}` …
77	  `{end_of_chorus}`/`{eoc}`; verse `{sov}`…`{eov}`; bridge `{sob}`…`{eob}`;
78	  tab (monospaced, chords NOT parsed) `{sot}`…`{eot}`. Recall a chorus with
79	  `{chorus}`. Comments: `{comment:}`/`{c:}`.
80	- **Key vs capo**: `{key:}` is the *written/fingering* key of the shapes shown;
81	  `{capo:}` is the capo used. If charts disagree, prefer the one whose chord
82	  vocabulary is internally consistent, and caption the *sounding* pitch.
83	- **Chorus recall**: `{chorus}` reprints the most-recently-defined chorus (showing
84	  only a "Chorus" label by default). With 2+ distinct recurring sections, label
85	  them — `{start_of_chorus: name}` … `{chorus: name}` — or expand the repeat.
86	
87	Emit this shape — metadata block → environments/comments → verses/choruses:
88	
89	```
90	{title: Swing Low Sweet Chariot}
91	{artist: Traditional}
92	{key: G}
93	{tempo: 90}
94	{time: 4/4}
95	
96	{comment: Intro}
97	[G] [C] [G] [D]
98	
99	{start_of_chorus: Chorus}
100	Swing [G]low, sweet [C]chari[G]ot,
101	Comin' for to carry me [D]home.
102	{end_of_chorus}
103	
104	{start_of_verse: Verse 1}
105	I [G]looked over Jordan, and [C]what did I [G]see,
106	Comin' for to carry me [D]home.
107	{end_of_verse}
108	
109	{chorus}
110	```
111	
112	Full directive set (chord `{define}` diagrams, `{transpose}`, markup, ABC/LilyPond
113	blocks, `x_` custom namespace) → read `references/chordpro-format.md`.
114	
115	## The `chordpro` / `a2crd` CLI (essentials)
116	
117	The official tool is a Perl program (CPAN dist **`App::Music::ChordPro`**). Current
118	6.x releases install the **`chordpro`** command; the chords-over-lyrics importer
119	is `chordpro --a2crd` (a standalone `a2crd` binary shipped in older releases and
120	may be absent — prefer `chordpro --a2crd`).
121	
122	```bash
123	# Install (macOS — there is NO official Homebrew formula; use CPAN)
124	brew install perl cpanminus && cpanm App::Music::ChordPro
125	# If `chordpro` then errors "Can't locate ChordPro.pm", activate local::lib once:
126	eval "$(perl -I"$HOME/perl5/lib/perl5" -Mlocal::lib)"   # add to ~/.zshrc to persist
127	
128	# Render
129	chordpro -o song.pdf song.cho          # PDF (format inferred from extension)
130	chordpro --generate=HTML -o song.html song.cho
131	
132	# Transpose (N semitones; suffix s/f forces sharp/flat spelling)
133	chordpro -x 2  -o up.pdf   song.cho
134	chordpro -x -3f -o down.pdf song.cho
135	
136	# Convert chords-over-lyrics text -> ChordPro (the official importer)
137	chordpro --a2crd input.txt -o song.cho
138	```
139	
140	Install-per-platform, generators, config JSON, songbook `--toc`, and `a2crd`
141	heuristic tuning → read `references/cli-and-rendering.md`.
142	
143	## Verify loop — never hand back an unvalidated `.cho`
144	
145	Every generated or edited file goes through the parser before you present it:
146	
147	```bash
148	scripts/validate-cho.sh song.cho          # wraps the command below; PASS/FAIL + warnings
149	# equivalently:
150	chordpro --strict --generate=Text -o - song.cho   # exit 0 + no stderr warnings = valid
151	```
152	
153	To auto-normalize to canonical form (fix spacing, round-trip directives):
154	`chordpro --generate=ChordPro -o song.cho song.cho`. If `chordpro` isn't
155	installed, the script prints the install one-liner — say so and offer to proceed
156	without rendering (the format is still human-checkable).
157	
158	**Producing a PDF? Verify it *renders*, not just parses.** `validate-cho.sh` only
159	checks that the file parses — it can't see a broken PDF. `chordpro`'s default
160	fonts have **no CJK glyphs**, so a Chinese/Japanese/Korean song renders as blank
161	tofu while still exiting 0 and passing validation. Use `scripts/render-cho.sh
162	song.cho` — it auto-detects a CJK font, renders, and glyph-checks the PDF (fails
163	loudly on tofu).
164	
165	## Finding existing chord charts (the usual first move)
166	
167	For a named/popular song, a human-made chart almost always already exists online
168	and beats audio extraction on accuracy. The realistic recipe (WebFetch's
169	summarizer strips copyrighted lyrics, and `a2crd`'s column logic mis-aligns
170	full-width CJK — so neither is the happy path it looks like):
171	
172	```bash
173	# 1. search (中文: 吉他谱/和弦/弹唱谱; EN: chords / ultimate guitar)
174	# 2. fetch the RAW html (WebFetch drops the lyrics) and parse chords from the
175	#    site's markup — e.g. Chord4 parenthesized-syllable, UG js-store data-content.
176	curl -sL "<chart-url>" -o chart.html
177	# 3. lyrics come SEPARATELY from LRCLIB (reliable, synced):
178	uv run scripts/fetch-lyrics.py --artist "…" --track "…" -o song.lrc
179	# 4. align the chart's chords onto the lyric syllables by phrase, NOT by column
180	#    (CJK chars are 2 display cells). For pure-Latin chords-over-lyrics you can
181	#    still use:  chordpro --a2crd chart.txt -o song.cho
182	scripts/validate-cho.sh song.cho && scripts/render-cho.sh song.cho   # 5. validate + render (CJK-safe)
183	```
184	
185	Caption the result with a `{comment:}` naming the source and "published
186	arrangement — verify against the recording (capo/key may differ)". Not machine
187	ACR, so no `AUTO-GENERATED` header. Per-site extraction patterns, the site catalog
188	(91譜/Chord4/UG — many are JS-rendered or image-only 六线谱), simplified↔traditional
189	handling, and legality → read `references/chord-tab-sources.md`.
190	
191	## Generating from audio / links — the fallback when no chart exists
192	
193	This is the shakiest path — reach for it only when no existing chart is available.
194	
195	**Set expectations first**: open automatic chord recognition tops out around **78–80% on simple major/minor pop**
196	and drops sharply on 7ths, extended/jazz chords, key changes, and quiet or dense
197	mixes; inversions/slash chords are unreliable; and it cannot know the capo a
198	guitarist used. Treat the result as a **draft to correct**, not a transcription.
199	
200	```bash
201	# Best-effort turnkey: link or local file -> draft ChordPro
202	uv run scripts/audio-to-chords.py --dry-run "https://youtu.be/..."   # show the plan first
203	uv run scripts/audio-to-chords.py -o draft.cho "https://youtu.be/..."
204	```
205	
206	The script downloads audio with `yt-dlp` (YouTube/Bilibili/SoundCloud) and runs
207	`chord-extractor`/Chordino. Its output **must** carry the
208	`{comment: AUTO-GENERATED — verify chords/key/timing}` header. On macOS the
209	Chordino Vamp plugin often isn't installed; the script detects that and prints
210	exact install guidance + manual alternatives instead of crashing — relay that to
211	the user rather than silently failing. Tool comparison, beat/key detection, and
212	commercial escape hatches (Moises/Songsterr have APIs; Chordify/Chord AI/Ultimate
213	Guitar don't) → read `references/audio-to-chords.md`.
214	
215	**Legal**: only process content the user owns or has the right to use, for
216	personal use, locally; downloading copyrighted audio can violate a platform's
217	ToS. Surface this — don't bury it.
218	
219	## Lyrics sources
220	
221	Default to **LRCLIB** — free, no API key, returns time-synced `.lrc`:
222	
223	```bash
224	uv run scripts/fetch-lyrics.py --artist "Adele" --track "Hello" --duration 295
225	uv run scripts/fetch-lyrics.py --plain --artist "..." --track "..."   # plain text
226	```
227	
228	| Source | Access | Synced `.lrc`? |
229	|---|---|---|
230	| **LRCLIB** | free, no key | **yes** |
231	| Musixmatch | API key; full/synced is paid | yes (paid) |
232	| NetEase / QQ Music | unofficial community APIs | yes (Chinese catalog) |
233	| Genius (`lyricsgenius`) | API token; lyrics scraped from page | no (plain) |
234	| Mojim / 魔鏡 | scrape-only | no (plain) |
235	| KKBOX | partner-gated | n/a |
236	
237	Full comparison, legality, and the LRCLIB API → read `references/lyrics-sources.md`.
238	
239	## Available scripts
240	
241	- **`scripts/validate-cho.sh <file.cho>`** — verify a file parses cleanly
242	  (`chordpro --strict`); PASS/FAIL to stdout, warnings to stderr. Guides install
243	  if `chordpro` is missing. Flags: `--help`.
244	- **`scripts/render-cho.sh <file.cho>`** — render to PDF with a **CJK-safe** font
245	  (auto-detected) and glyph-check the result, so a Chinese song can't silently
246	  render as tofu. Flags: `-o/--output`, `--font`, `--keep-config`, `--help`.
247	- **`scripts/fetch-lyrics.py`** — fetch lyrics from LRCLIB (synced `.lrc` default,
248	  `--plain` for text). Auto-retries a CJK miss with a romanized/pinyin query.
249	  Self-contained via `uv run`. Flags: `--artist`, `--track`, `--duration`,
250	  `--album`, `--plain`, `-o/--output`, `--help`, `--dry-run`.
251	- **`scripts/audio-to-chords.py`** — best-effort link/audio → draft ChordPro
252	  (`yt-dlp` + `chord-extractor`). Degrades gracefully when the ACR backend is
253	  unavailable. Flags: `-o/--output`, `--lrc`, `--help`, `--dry-run`.
254	
255	## Bundled assets
256	
257	Ready-to-open examples + a template under `assets/` (all songs are **public
258	domain**; every `.cho` validates clean with `chordpro --strict`). Use them as
259	copy-paste starting points and few-shot references:
260	
261	- `assets/example-amazing-grace.cho` — simplest real song: metadata + inline chords.
262	- `assets/example-when-the-saints.cho` — chorus/verse structure + `{chorus}` recall.
263	- `assets/example-greensleeves.cho` — feature showcase: `{define}` diagrams, a
264	  `{sot}` tab block, chorus recall, transpose note.
265	- `assets/template-song.cho` — fill-in-the-blanks scaffold (renders as-is); the
266	  starting point for the interactive chord-fill flow.
267	- `assets/example-synced-lyrics.lrc` — sample time-synced `.lrc` (what
268	  `fetch-lyrics.py` returns; feed it to `audio-to-chords.py --lrc`).
269	- `assets/example-a2crd-input.txt` — chords-over-lyrics plain text; convert with
270	  `chordpro --a2crd assets/example-a2crd-input.txt`.
271	
272	## Reference files
273	
274	- `references/chordpro-format.md` — Read **when** hand-authoring or you need a
275	  directive beyond the cheat-sheet (`{define}` diagrams, `{transpose}`, markup,
276	  ABC/LilyPond, `x_` custom namespace).
277	- `references/chord-tab-sources.md` — Read **when** you need chords for a named
278	  song and have none: where to find existing charts (91譜/Chord4/Ultimate
279	  Guitar/…), how to adapt them, and the legality.
280	- `references/cli-and-rendering.md` — Read **when** installing, rendering,
281	  transposing, converting with `a2crd`, or validating/normalizing.
282	- `references/audio-to-chords.md` — Read **when** the user wants chords from an
283	  audio file or a link (ACR tool choice, beat/key, limits, escape hatches).
284	- `references/lyrics-sources.md` — Read **when** fetching lyrics (source table,
285	  synced-vs-plain, API-vs-scrape, legality, LRCLIB API).
286	
287	## Gotchas
288	
289	- **macOS has no official Homebrew `chordpro`** — install via CPAN
290	  (`brew install perl cpanminus && cpanm App::Music::ChordPro`). A signed `.dmg`
291	  GUI exists on GitHub Releases but the CLI is the CPAN route.
292	- **`Can't locate ChordPro.pm in @INC` after cpanm** — cpanm installed into a
293	  `local::lib` (`~/perl5`) that isn't on Perl's path. Activate it:
294	  `eval "$(perl -I"$HOME/perl5/lib/perl5" -Mlocal::lib)"` (persist in `~/.zshrc`).
295	- **No standalone `a2crd` in ChordPro 6.x** — use `chordpro --a2crd input.txt`.
296	  Its output needs a human pass (heuristic, column-based chord placement); always
297	  validate and eyeball before rendering.
298	- **Angle brackets `< >` are text markup in ChordPro v6.** Don't put `<...>`
299	  placeholders in lyrics/chords — the parser reads `<b>`/`<i>`-style markup and
300	  floods warnings. Use plain-text placeholders (see `assets/template-song.cho`).
301	- **No official online validator.** chordpro.org hosts docs + a desktop GUI, not
302	  a "try it online" box. Validate locally with the CLI (`validate-cho.sh`).
303	- **CJK renders as tofu by default — and passes validation.** `chordpro`'s default
304	  fonts have no Han/Kana/Hangul glyphs, so a Chinese/Japanese/Korean song produces
305	  a blank PDF that still exits 0 and passes `validate-cho.sh` (which only checks
306	  parsing). Render CJK with `scripts/render-cho.sh` (auto CJK font + glyph-check),
307	  or pass `--config` pointing `pdf.fonts.*` at a CJK font.
308	- **`a2crd` is Latin-only.** Its column heuristic assumes 1 char = 1 column, but
309	  full-width CJK occupies 2 display cells, so chords drift. For CJK, align chords to
310	  syllables/phrases by musical judgment — don't trust column arithmetic.
311	- **A strict "Unknown chord" warning ≠ a parse error.** `chordpro --strict` warns
312	  "Unknown chord" for a *valid* chord it has no built-in diagram for (e.g. `Em/C#`,
313	  `F#m7b5`); it still renders. Add a `{define}` (see the format reference) or ignore.
314	- **`{chorus}` recall is a trap with 2+ recurring sections.** It reprints only the
315	  most-recently-defined chorus, as a bare "Chorus" tag by default. Label distinct
316	  blocks (`{start_of_chorus: name}` / `{chorus: name}`) or expand repeats explicitly.
317	- **`WebFetch` strips copyrighted lyrics** (returns "[lyrics omitted]"), so the
318	  chart-fetch path needs raw `curl` + per-site parsing; and from an image-only chart
319	  `WebFetch` may *fabricate* chord placement — trust only an explicit chord list.
320	- **Chord accuracy from audio is ~80% at best** on simple pop, worse otherwise.
321	  Never present a machine-extracted sheet without the `AUTO-GENERATED` header and
322	  a "verify chords/key/timing" caveat.
323	- **Auto-generated chart sites are ACR in disguise.** Chordu / Chordify /
324	  GuitarTuna charts are machine-derived (~80%, same caveat) — treat them as drafts,
325	  unlike human-made charts on 91譜 / Chord4 / Ultimate Guitar.
326	- **Detected key is a suggestion.** ACR outputs absolute pitches; key detection
327	  confuses relative major/minor and keys a fifth apart, and enharmonic spelling
328	  (Gb vs F#) is ambiguous. Confirm with the user before committing `{key:}`.
329	- **Chords in `{sot}`…`{eot}` tab blocks are NOT parsed** — that's for ASCII tab.
330	  Use inline `[..]` in verses/choruses; reserve tab blocks for fret diagrams.
331	- **Lyrics/audio ToS.** Prefer LRCLIB (open); most other lyric sources are
332	  scrape-only or paid, and downloading audio has copyright/ToS limits. Keep it
333	  personal-use and local; surface the caveat rather than hiding it.
334

106	Comin' for to carry me [D]home.
107	{end_of_verse}
108	
109	{chorus}
110	```
111	
112	Full directive set (chord `{define}` diagrams, `{transpose}`, markup, ABC/LilyPond
113	blocks, `x_` custom namespace) → read `references/chordpro-format.md`.
114	
115	## The `chordpro` / `a2crd` CLI (essentials)
116	
117	The official tool is a Perl program (CPAN dist **`App::Music::ChordPro`**). Current
118	6.x releases install the **`chordpro`** command; the chords-over-lyrics importer
119	is `chordpro --a2crd` (a standalone `a2crd` binary shipped in older releases and
120	may be absent — prefer `chordpro --a2crd`).
121	
122	```bash
123	# Install (macOS — there is NO official Homebrew formula; use CPAN)
124	brew install perl cpanminus && cpanm App::Music::ChordPro
125	# If `chordpro` then errors "Can't locate ChordPro.pm", activate local::lib once:
126	eval "$(perl -I"$HOME/perl5/lib/perl5" -Mlocal::lib)"   # add to ~/.zshrc to persist
127	
128	# Render
129	chordpro -o song.pdf song.cho          # PDF (format inferred from extension)
130	chordpro --generate=HTML -o song.html song.cho
131	
132	# Transpose (N semitones; suffix s/f forces sharp/flat spelling)
133	chordpro -x 2  -o up.pdf   song.cho
134	chordpro -x -3f -o down.pdf song.cho
135	
136	# Convert chords-over-lyrics text -> ChordPro (the official importer)
137	chordpro --a2crd input.txt -o song.cho
138	```
139	
140	Install-per-platform, generators, config JSON, songbook `--toc`, and `a2crd`
141	heuristic tuning → read `references/cli-and-rendering.md`.
142	
143	## Verify loop — never hand back an unvalidated `.cho`
144	
145	Every generated or edited file goes through the parser before you present it:
146	
147	```bash
148	scripts/validate-cho.sh song.cho          # wraps the command below; PASS/FAIL + warnings
149	# equivalently:
150	chordpro --strict --generate=Text -o - song.cho   # exit 0 + no stderr warnings = valid
151	```
152	
153	To auto-normalize to canonical form (fix spacing, round-trip directives):
154	`chordpro --generate=ChordPro -o song.cho song.cho`. If `chordpro` isn't
155	installed, the script prints the install one-liner — say so and offer to proceed
156	without rendering (the format is still human-checkable).
157	
158	**Producing a PDF? Verify it *renders*, not just parses.** `validate-cho.sh` only
159	checks that the file parses — it can't see a broken PDF. `chordpro`'s default
160	fonts have **no CJK glyphs**, so a Chinese/Japanese/Korean song renders as blank
161	tofu while still exiting 0 and passing validation. Use `scripts/render-cho.sh
162	song.cho` — it auto-detects a CJK font, renders, and glyph-checks the PDF (fails
163	loudly on tofu).
164	
165	## Finding existing chord charts (the usual first move)
166	
167	For a named/popular song, a human-made chart almost always already exists online
168	and beats audio extraction on accuracy. The realistic recipe (WebFetch's
169	summarizer strips copyrighted lyrics, and `a2crd`'s column logic mis-aligns
170	full-width CJK — so neither is the happy path it looks like):
171	
172	```bash
173	# 1. search (中文: 吉他谱/和弦/弹唱谱; EN: chords / ultimate guitar)
174	# 2. fetch the RAW html (WebFetch drops the lyrics) and parse chords from the
175	#    site's markup — e.g. Chord4 parenthesized-syllable, UG js-store data-content.
176	curl -sL "<chart-url>" -o chart.html
177	# 3. lyrics come SEPARATELY from LRCLIB (reliable, synced):
178	uv run scripts/fetch-lyrics.py --artist "…" --track "…" -o song.lrc
179	# 4. align the chart's chords onto the lyric syllables by phrase, NOT by column
180	#    (CJK chars are 2 display cells). For pure-Latin chords-over-lyrics you can
181	#    still use:  chordpro --a2crd chart.txt -o song.cho
182	scripts/validate-cho.sh song.cho && scripts/render-cho.sh song.cho   # 5. validate + render (CJK-safe)
183	```
184	
185	Caption the result with a `{comment:}` naming the source and "published
186	arrangement — verify against the recording (capo/key may differ)". Not machine
187	ACR, so no `AUTO-GENERATED` header. Per-site extraction patterns, the site catalog
188	(91譜/Chord4/UG — many are JS-rendered or image-only 六线谱), simplified↔traditional
189	handling, and legality → read `references/chord-tab-sources.md`.
190	
191	## Generating from audio / links — the fallback when no chart exists
192	
193	This is the shakiest path — reach for it only when no existing chart is available.
194	
195	**Set expectations first**: open automatic chord recognition tops out around **78–80% on simple major/minor pop**
196	and drops sharply on 7ths, extended/jazz chords, key changes, and quiet or dense
197	mixes; inversions/slash chords are unreliable; and it cannot know the capo a
198	guitarist used. Treat the result as a **draft to correct**, not a transcription.
199	
200	```bash
201	# Best-effort turnkey: link or local file -> draft ChordPro
202	uv run scripts/audio-to-chords.py --dry-run "https://youtu.be/..."   # show the plan first
203	uv run scripts/audio-to-chords.py -o draft.cho "https://youtu.be/..."
204	```
205	
206	The script downloads audio with `yt-dlp` (YouTube/Bilibili/SoundCloud) and runs
207	`chord-extractor`/Chordino. Its output **must** carry the
208	`{comment: AUTO-GENERATED — verify chords/key/timing}` header. On macOS the
209	Chordino Vamp plugin often isn't installed; the script detects that and prints
210	exact install guidance + manual alternatives instead of crashing — relay that to
211	the user rather than silently failing. Tool comparison, beat/key detection, and
212	commercial escape hatches (Moises/Songsterr have APIs; Chordify/Chord AI/Ultimate
213	Guitar don't) → read `references/audio-to-chords.md`.
214	
215	**Legal**: only process content the user owns or has the right to use, for
216	personal use, locally; downloading copyrighted audio can violate a platform's
217	ToS. Surface this — don't bury it.
218	
219	## Lyrics sources
220	
221	Default to **LRCLIB** — free, no API key, returns time-synced `.lrc`:
222	
223	```bash
224	uv run scripts/fetch-lyrics.py --artist "Adele" --track "Hello" --duration 295
225	uv run scripts/fetch-lyrics.py --plain --artist "..." --track "..."   # plain text
226	```
227	
228	| Source | Access | Synced `.lrc`? |
229	|---|---|---|
230	| **LRCLIB** | free, no key | **yes** |
231	| Musixmatch | API key; full/synced is paid | yes (paid) |
232	| NetEase / QQ Music | unofficial community APIs | yes (Chinese catalog) |
233	| Genius (`lyricsgenius`) | API token; lyrics scraped from page | no (plain) |
234	| Mojim / 魔鏡 | scrape-only | no (plain) |
235	| KKBOX | partner-gated | n/a |
236	
237	Full comparison, legality, and the LRCLIB API → read `references/lyrics-sources.md`.
238	
239	## Available scripts
240	
241	- **`scripts/validate-cho.sh <file.cho>`** — verify a file parses cleanly
242	  (`chordpro --strict`); PASS/FAIL to stdout, warnings to stderr. Guides install
243	  if `chordpro` is missing. Flags: `--help`.
244	- **`scripts/render-cho.sh <file.cho>`** — render to PDF with a **CJK-safe** font
245	  (auto-detected) and glyph-check the result, so a Chinese song can't silently
246	  render as tofu. Flags: `-o/--output`, `--font`, `--keep-config`, `--help`.
247	- **`scripts/fetch-lyrics.py`** — fetch lyrics from LRCLIB (synced `.lrc` default,
248	  `--plain` for text). Auto-retries a CJK miss with a romanized/pinyin query.
249	  Self-contained via `uv run`. Flags: `--artist`, `--track`, `--duration`,
250	  `--album`, `--plain`, `-o/--output`, `--help`, `--dry-run`.
251	- **`scripts/audio-to-chords.py`** — best-effort link/audio → draft ChordPro
252	  (`yt-dlp` + `chord-extractor`). Degrades gracefully when the ACR backend is
253	  unavailable. Flags: `-o/--output`, `--lrc`, `--help`, `--dry-run`.
254	
255	## Bundled assets
256	
257	Ready-to-open examples + a template under `assets/` (all songs are **public
258	domain**; every `.cho` validates clean with `chordpro --strict`). Use them as
259	copy-paste starting points and few-shot references:
260	
261	- `assets/example-amazing-grace.cho` — simplest real song: metadata + inline chords.
262	- `assets/example-when-the-saints.cho` — chorus/verse structure + `{chorus}` recall.
263	- `assets/example-greensleeves.cho` — feature showcase: `{define}` diagrams, a
264	  `{sot}` tab block, chorus recall, transpose note.
265	- `assets/template-song.cho` — fill-in-the-blanks scaffold (renders as-is); the
266	  starting point for the interactive chord-fill flow.
267	- `assets/example-synced-lyrics.lrc` — sample time-synced `.lrc` (what
268	  `fetch-lyrics.py` returns; feed it to `audio-to-chords.py --lrc`).
269	- `assets/example-a2crd-input.txt` — chords-over-lyrics plain text; convert with
270	  `chordpro --a2crd assets/example-a2crd-input.txt`.
271	
272	## Reference files
273	
274	- `references/chordpro-format.md` — Read **when** hand-authoring or you need a
275	  directive beyond the cheat-sheet (`{define}` diagrams, `{transpose}`, markup,
276	  ABC/LilyPond, `x_` custom namespace).
277	- `references/chord-tab-sources.md` — Read **when** you need chords for a named
278	  song and have none: where to find existing charts (91譜/Chord4/Ultimate
279	  Guitar/…), how to adapt them, and the legality.
280	- `references/cli-and-rendering.md` — Read **when** installing, rendering,
281	  transposing, converting with `a2crd`, or validating/normalizing.
282	- `references/audio-to-chords.md` — Read **when** the user wants chords from an
283	  audio file or a link (ACR tool choice, beat/key, limits, escape hatches).
284	- `references/lyrics-sources.md` — Read **when** fetching lyrics (source table,
285	  synced-vs-plain, API-vs-scrape, legality, LRCLIB API).
286	
287	## Gotchas
288	
289	- **macOS has no official Homebrew `chordpro`** — install via CPAN
290	  (`brew install perl cpanminus && cpanm App::Music::ChordPro`). A signed `.dmg`
291	  GUI exists on GitHub Releases but the CLI is the CPAN route.
292	- **`Can't locate ChordPro.pm in @INC` after cpanm** — cpanm installed into a
293	  `local::lib` (`~/perl5`) that isn't on Perl's path. Activate it:
294	  `eval "$(perl -I"$HOME/perl5/lib/perl5" -Mlocal::lib)"` (persist in `~/.zshrc`).
295	- **No standalone `a2crd` in ChordPro 6.x** — use `chordpro --a2crd input.txt`.
296	  Its output needs a human pass (heuristic, column-based chord placement); always
297	  validate and eyeball before rendering.
298	- **Angle brackets `< >` are text markup in ChordPro v6.** Don't put `<...>`
299	  placeholders in lyrics/chords — the parser reads `<b>`/`<i>`-style markup and
300	  floods warnings. Use plain-text placeholders (see `assets/template-song.cho`).
301	- **No official online validator.** chordpro.org hosts docs + a desktop GUI, not
302	  a "try it online" box. Validate locally with the CLI (`validate-cho.sh`).
303	- **CJK renders as tofu by default — and passes validation.** `chordpro`'s default
304	  fonts have no Han/Kana/Hangul glyphs, so a Chinese/Japanese/Korean song produces
305	  a blank PDF that still exits 0 and passes `validate-cho.sh` (which only checks
306	  parsing). Render CJK with `scripts/render-cho.sh` (auto CJK font + glyph-check),
307	  or pass `--config` pointing `pdf.fonts.*` at a CJK font.
308	- **`a2crd` is Latin-only.** Its column heuristic assumes 1 char = 1 column, but
309	  full-width CJK occupies 2 display cells, so chords drift. For CJK, align chords to
310	  syllables/phrases by musical judgment — don't trust column arithmetic.
311	- **A strict "Unknown chord" warning ≠ a parse error.** `chordpro --strict` warns
312	  "Unknown chord" for a *valid* chord it has no built-in diagram for (e.g. `Em/C#`,
313	  `F#m7b5`); it still renders. Add a `{define}` (see the format reference) or ignore.
314	- **`{chorus}` recall is a trap with 2+ recurring sections.** It reprints only the
315	  most-recently-defined chorus, as a bare "Chorus" tag by default. Label distinct
316	  blocks (`{start_of_chorus: name}` / `{chorus: name}`) or expand repeats explicitly.
317	- **`WebFetch` strips copyrighted lyrics** (returns "[lyrics omitted]"), so the
318	  chart-fetch path needs raw `curl` + per-site parsing; and from an image-only chart
319	  `WebFetch` may *fabricate* chord placement — trust only an explicit chord list.
320	- **Chord accuracy from audio is ~80% at best** on simple pop, worse otherwise.
321	  Never present a machine-extracted sheet without the `AUTO-GENERATED` header and
322	  a "verify chords/key/timing" caveat.
323	- **Auto-generated chart sites are ACR in disguise.** Chordu / Chordify /
324	  GuitarTuna charts are machine-derived (~80%, same caveat) — treat them as drafts,
325	  unlike human-made charts on 91譜 / Chord4 / Ultimate Guitar.
326	- **Detected key is a suggestion.** ACR outputs absolute pitches; key detection
327	  confuses relative major/minor and keys a fifth apart, and enharmonic spelling
328	  (Gb vs F#) is ambiguous. Confirm with the user before committing `{key:}`.
329	- **Chords in `{sot}`…`{eot}` tab blocks are NOT parsed** — that's for ASCII tab.
330	  Use inline `[..]` in verses/choruses; reserve tab blocks for fret diagrams.
331	- **Lyrics/audio ToS.** Prefer LRCLIB (open); most other lyric sources are
332	  scrape-only or paid, and downloading audio has copyright/ToS limits. Keep it
333	  personal-use and local; surface the caveat rather than hiding it.
334

1	# Finding existing chord charts online
2	
3	Read this when the user wants chords for a **known/popular song** (by title, by
4	lyrics, or from a link) and hasn't pasted chords or supplied audio. For most
5	songs people ask about, **a human-made chart already exists on the web** — and it

7	~80%). So the reliable first move is: search chart sites → adapt the chart to
8	ChordPro → validate. Fall back to audio ACR or interactive fill only when no
9	chart is found.
10	
11	This is the router's highest-value path for "make me a chord sheet for `<song>`",
12	and it's what actually happens in practice — treat existing charts as the
13	default source of chords, not an afterthought.
14	
15	## The workflow
16	
17	Verified across a 7-song C-pop batch — the naive "WebFetch → a2crd" path breaks in
18	two ways (WebFetch's summarizer strips copyrighted lyrics; `a2crd` mis-aligns CJK),
19	so the real recipe is:
20	
21	1. **Search.** `WebSearch` for the song + a chart keyword in the right language:
22	   - EN: `"<artist> <title>" chords`, `... ultimate guitar`, `... chordpro`
23	   - 中文: `<歌手> <歌名> 吉他谱`, `... 和弦`, `... 弹唱谱`, `... 简谱`
24	2. **Fetch RAW, then parse the site's markup.** `WebFetch`'s LLM summary **strips the
25	   copyrighted lyrics** (returns "[歌词已移除]" / "[lyrics omitted]"), so you get chords
26	   with no alignment. Instead `curl -sL <url>` the raw HTML and parse the site markup:
27	   - **Chord4** (best for Mandarin): chords are parenthesized syllables like
28	     `你不是真正(的)快樂` (chord sits above the `(char)`), plus `data-chord` attrs,
29	     inside the `tabs_content` `<pre>` block.
30	   - **Ultimate Guitar**: JS-rendered — the chart is in the embedded **`js-store`
31	     `data-content` JSON** as `[ch]C[/ch] … [tab]…[/tab]`.
32	   - **Image-only 六线谱** (common for C-pop — jitahome/qinhun/guistudy…): there is NO
33	     text to parse. `WebFetch` will *confidently fabricate* per-line placement — trust
34	     only an explicit chord **list**, never fabricated alignment.
35	3. **Lyrics come SEPARATELY from LRCLIB** (`scripts/fetch-lyrics.py -o song.lrc`).
36	   Treat LRCLIB lyrics as ground truth (they arrive traditional or simplified —
37	   see below).
38	4. **Align by phrase, not by column.** `chordpro --a2crd` only works on **pure-Latin**
39	   chords-over-lyrics; for CJK its 1-char = 1-column heuristic drifts (full-width
40	   chars are 2 display cells). Place each chord over the syllable/phrase it belongs
41	   to by musical judgment. If the chart omits an intro/interlude, reuse the relevant
42	   verse loop labeled "verify against recording" — never fabricate a specific riff.
43	5. **Validate AND render.** `scripts/validate-cho.sh` (parse) **and**
44	   `scripts/render-cho.sh` (CJK-safe render + glyph-check — a bare `chordpro -o`
45	   renders Chinese as tofu yet passes validation). Caption a `{comment:}` naming the
46	   source + "published arrangement — verify against the recording (capo/key may
47	   differ)". Not machine ACR, so no `AUTO-GENERATED` header.
48	
49	## Where the charts live
50	
51	Coverage and format vary; try a couple, and **don't rely on any single site**
52	(the batch hit `kanpu8` HTTP 403 and `jitapai` expired-TLS). Auto-generated sites
53	are effectively ACR — same ~80% caveat.
54	
55	**Chinese / Taiwan (great for C-pop like the 落葉歸根 case):**
56	- **Chord4 / 和弦网** — `chord4.com` — **the repeat winner** (sourced chords in 6 of 7
57	  eval runs). Raw HTML exposes a parseable chords-over-lyrics block. Start here for Mandarin.
58	- **91譜 / 91pu** — `91pu.com.tw` — large Taiwan library, but **JS-rendered**; `curl`
59	  often returns only page chrome. Good to eyeball, awkward to parse.
60	- **弹唱谱 / 简谱 hubs** — `qupu123`, `中国曲谱网 (qupu.com)`, `17jita`, `jitaba/jitapu`,
61	  `jitahome`, `qinhun`, `guistudy` — **mostly image 六线谱** (manual transcription);
62	  simplified-character search finds more.
63	- **魔鏡歌詞 / Mojim** — `mojim.com` — mostly lyrics, some chords; good for confirming lyrics.
64	
65	**Western / global:**
66	- **Ultimate Guitar** — `ultimate-guitar.com` — largest, but **fully JS-rendered**;
67	  `WebFetch` returns no chords. Parse the `js-store` `data-content` JSON from raw HTML.
68	- **e-chords**, **Chordie**, **AZChords** — chords-over-lyrics, usually parseable.
69	- **Songsterr** — public API for tabs/chords (`songsterr.com/a/wsa/api-tabs-a26570`).
70	- **Chordu / Chordify / GuitarTuna** — **auto-generated from audio** → ACR-quality
71	  (~80%, verify), not human-checked. Use only to corroborate.
72	
73	## Format taxonomy (what you'll get back)
74	
75	| Format | How to use it | Reliability |
76	|---|---|---|
77	| Latin chords-over-lyrics text | `chordpro --a2crd` → clean up → validate | High (human-made) |
78	| CJK chords-over-lyrics text | hand-align by phrase (a2crd drifts on full-width) → validate | High |
79	| Inline / chord chart | transcribe into the ChordPro template | High |
80	| Guitar tab (6-line) | embed in a `{start_of_tab}` block; or use for riffs only | High for riffs |
81	| 简谱 (numbered) / image scan | manual transcription; no reliable OMR — trust only an explicit chord list | Low (tedious) |
82	| Auto-generated (chordu/chordify) | same as ACR — a draft to verify | ~80% |
83	
84	## Simplified vs traditional, and the metadata a chart won't give you
85	
86	- **Char-set mismatch is common**: a simplified-character chart vs traditional LRCLIB
87	  lyrics (or vice versa). Treat the **LRCLIB lyrics as ground truth** and map chords by
88	  position/meaning, not string equality. `opencc` can convert if you must reconcile.
89	- **capo / tempo / composer / year** are usually **absent from text charts**. Get them
90	  from a second source (Wikipedia/Baidu/SongBPM), but **tempo is unreliable** — beware
91	  the half-time trap (a song *felt* at 82 BPM is often listed as 164). Omit an unknown
92	  field or caption it "unverified"; never fabricate.
93	
94	## Legality (surface it, don't bury it)
95	
96	These charts are user-contributed arrangements; the underlying songs are usually
97	copyrighted. Keep it **personal-use and local**, don't redistribute the fetched
98	chart or lyrics commercially, and cite the source in a `{comment:}`. Prefer this
99	route over downloading audio — it avoids the platform-ToS problem entirely — but
100	the copyright of the song itself still applies to any lyrics you embed.

# Building LLM-Powered Applications with Claude

This skill helps you build LLM-powered applications with Claude. Choose the right surface based on your needs, detect the project language, then read the relevant language-specific documentation.

## Before You Start

Scan the target file (or, if no target file, the prompt and project) for non-Anthropic provider markers — `import openai`, `from openai`, `langchain_openai`, `OpenAI(`, `gpt-4`, `gpt-5`, file names like `agent-openai.py` or `*-generic.py`, or any explicit instruction to keep the code provider-neutral. If you find any, stop and tell the user that this skill produces Claude/Anthropic SDK code; ask whether they want to switch the file to Claude or want a non-Claude implementation. Do not edit a non-Anthropic file with Anthropic SDK calls.

## Output Requirement

When the user asks you to add, modify, or implement a Claude feature, your code must call Claude through one of:

1. **The official Anthropic SDK** for the project's language (`anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai/sdk`, `com.anthropic.*`, etc.). This is the default whenever a supported SDK exists for the project.
2. **Raw HTTP** (`curl`, `requests`, `fetch`, `httpx`, etc.) — only when the user explicitly asks for cURL/REST/raw HTTP, the project is a shell/cURL project, or the language has no official SDK.

Never mix the two — don't reach for `requests`/`fetch` in a Python or TypeScript project just because it feels lighter. Never fall back to OpenAI-compatible shims.

**Never guess SDK usage.** Function names, class names, namespaces, method signatures, and import paths must come from explicit documentation — either the `{lang}/` files in this skill or the official SDK repositories or documentation links listed in `shared/live-sources.md`. If the binding you need is not explicitly documented in the skill files, WebFetch the relevant SDK repo from `shared/live-sources.md` before writing code. Do not infer Ruby/Java/Go/PHP/C# APIs from cURL shapes or from another language's SDK.

**If WebFetch or repository access fails** (network restricted, timeouts, clone blocked): do not keep retrying — write code from the patterns and namespace/package tables in the `{lang}/` file, run the compiler or interpreter on it, and iterate on the error output. For statically-typed SDKs (C#, Java, Go) a compile-fix loop against local errors reaches working code faster than blocked network research.

## Defaults

Unless the user requests otherwise:

For the Claude model version, please use Claude Opus 4.8, which you can access via the exact model string `claude-opus-4-8`. Please default to using adaptive thinking (`thinking: {type: "adaptive"}`) for anything remotely complicated. And finally, please default to streaming for any request that may involve long input, long output, or high `max_tokens` — it prevents hitting request timeouts. Use the SDK's `.get_final_message()` / `.finalMessage()` helper to get the complete response if you don't need to handle individual stream events

## ⚠️ API Drift — Your Training Prior May Be Stale

Several common Claude API shapes changed in 2025–2026. If you recall a pattern from training, verify it against the `{lang}/` files in this skill before writing — the rows below are the most frequent drift points:

| Area | Stale prior | Current API |
|---|---|---|
| Extended thinking | `thinking: {type: "enabled", budget_tokens: N}` | On Claude 4.6+ models: `thinking: {type: "adaptive"}`. `budget_tokens` is deprecated on Opus 4.6 / Sonnet 4.6 and **rejected with a 400** on Fable 5 / Sonnet 5 / Opus 4.8 / 4.7. Pre-4.6 models still use `budget_tokens`. |
| Web search / web fetch tool type | `web_search_20250305`, `web_fetch_20250910` | `web_search_20260209`, `web_fetch_20260209` (dynamic filtering) on Opus 4.8/4.7/4.6, Sonnet 5, and Sonnet 4.6. Older models keep the basic variants; on Vertex AI only basic `web_search_20250305` is available (web fetch is not on Vertex) — see the Server Tools QR below. |
| PHP parameter names | snake_case wire names as named args (`max_tokens`) | Top-level named args are camelCase (`maxTokens`). Nested array keys vary by feature (e.g. `'taskBudget'`, `'skillID'`, `'mcp_server_name'`) — copy the exact key from the documented example; do not bulk-convert. |
| Managed Agents credentials | Keep secrets host-side via custom tools (the only option before vaults shipped) | Vault `environment_variable` credentials — stored by Anthropic, substituted at egress, never visible in the sandbox (`shared/managed-agents-tools.md` → Vaults). Host-side custom tools remain the fallback for self-hosted sandboxes. |

The `{lang}/` files in this skill are authoritative over recalled patterns.

## Language Detection

Before reading code examples, determine which language the user is working in:

1. **Look at project files** to infer the language:

   - `*.py`, `requirements.txt`, `pyproject.toml`, `setup.py`, `Pipfile` → **Python** — read from `python/`
   - `*.ts`, `*.tsx`, `package.json`, `tsconfig.json` → **TypeScript** — read from `typescript/`
   - `*.js`, `*.jsx` (no `.ts` files present) → **TypeScript** — JS uses the same SDK, read from `typescript/`
   - `*.java`, `pom.xml`, `build.gradle` → **Java** — read from `java/`
   - `*.kt`, `*.kts`, `build.gradle.kts` → **Java** — Kotlin uses the Java SDK, read from `java/`
   - `*.scala`, `build.sbt` → **Java** — Scala uses the Java SDK, read from `java/`
   - `*.go`, `go.mod` → **Go** — read from `go/`
   - `*.rb`, `Gemfile` → **Ruby** — read from `ruby/`
   - `*.cs`, `*.csproj` → **C#** — read from `csharp/`
   - `*.php`, `composer.json` → **PHP** — read from `php/`

2. **If multiple languages detected** (e.g., both Python and TypeScript files):

   - Check which language the user's current file or question relates to
   - If still ambiguous, ask: "I detected both Python and TypeScript files. Which language are you using for the Claude API integration?"

3. **If language can't be inferred** (empty project, no source files, or unsupported language):

   - Use AskUserQuestion with options: Python, TypeScript, Java, Go, Ruby, cURL/raw HTTP, C#, PHP
   - If AskUserQuestion is unavailable, default to Python examples and note: "Showing Python examples. Let me know if you need a different language."

4. **If unsupported language detected** (Rust, Swift, C++, Elixir, etc.):

   - Suggest cURL/raw HTTP examples from `curl/` and note that community SDKs may exist
   - Offer to show Python or TypeScript examples as reference implementations

5. **If user needs cURL/raw HTTP examples**, read from `curl/`.

### Language-Specific Feature Support

Every SDK language above supports both the beta Tool Runner and Managed Agents (beta) — Python (`@beta_tool` decorator), TypeScript (`betaZodTool` + Zod), Java (annotated classes), Go (`BetaToolRunner` in the `toolrunner` pkg), Ruby (`BaseTool` + `tool_runner`), C# (`BetaToolRunner` + raw JSON schema), PHP (`BetaRunnableTool` + `toolRunner()`); code entry points are in the Tool Use Patterns quick reference below. cURL is raw HTTP (no SDK features) and supports Managed Agents.

> **Managed Agents code examples**: see the reading guide in the `## Managed Agents (Beta)` section below.
