## Client-Side Tools: Computer Use

Computer use lets Claude interact with a desktop environment (screenshots, mouse, keyboard). It is a client-side tool — your application provides the environment and executes the actions Claude requests; Anthropic processes the screenshots and action requests in real time but does not host the environment or retain the data.

For full documentation, use WebFetch:

- URL: `https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/computer-use/overview`

---

## Context Editing

Context editing clears stale tool results and thinking blocks from the transcript as a long-running agent accumulates turns. Unlike compaction (which summarizes), context editing prunes — the cleared content is removed, not replaced. Use it when old tool outputs are no longer relevant and you want to keep the transcript lean without losing the conversation structure.

**Beta.** Use `client.beta.messages.*` with beta `context-management-2025-06-27`. Configure via `context_management.edits` with a strategy type of `clear_tool_uses_20250919` (clear old tool results; optional `clear_tool_inputs: true` also clears the tool_use params) or `clear_thinking_20251015` (clear thinking blocks). These are **not** the compaction types — `compact_20260112` with beta `compact-2026-01-12` is the separate compaction feature.

For full documentation, use WebFetch:

- URL: `https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/context-editing`

---

## Server-Side Tools: Advisor (Beta)

The advisor tool pairs a faster, lower-cost **executor** model (the top-level `model` on the request) with a higher-intelligence **advisor** model (the `model` field inside the tool definition) that provides strategic guidance mid-generation. The executor does most of the token generation; the advisor is consulted for planning. Availability: see `shared/platform-availability.md`.

### Tool Definition

```json
{
  "type": "advisor_20260301",
  "name": "advisor",
  "model": "claude-opus-4-8"
}
```

**The advisor model must be at least as capable as the executor.** An invalid pairing returns `400 invalid_request_error`. Valid pairs:

| Executor (request `model`) | Valid advisor (tool `model`) |
|---|---|
| `claude-haiku-4-5` / `claude-sonnet-4-6` / `claude-sonnet-5` / `claude-opus-4-6` / `claude-opus-4-7` | `claude-opus-4-8` or `claude-opus-4-7` |
| `claude-opus-4-8` | `claude-opus-4-8` only |

Call via `client.beta.messages.create(...)` with `betas=["advisor-tool-2026-03-01"]` (or the `anthropic-beta: advisor-tool-2026-03-01` header). In multi-turn conversations, append the full `response.content` — including any `advisor_tool_result` blocks — back to `messages` on the next turn. If you remove the advisor tool from `tools` on a later turn while the history still contains `advisor_tool_result` blocks, the API returns a 400.

---

## Client-Side Tools: Memory

The memory tool enables Claude to store and retrieve information across conversations through a memory file directory. Claude can create, read, update, and delete files that persist between sessions.

### Key Facts

- Client-side tool — you control storage via your implementation
- Supports commands: `view`, `create`, `str_replace`, `insert`, `delete`, `rename`
- Operates on files in a `/memories` directory
- The Python, TypeScript, and Java SDKs provide helper classes/functions for implementing the memory backend

> **Security:** Never store API keys, passwords, tokens, or other secrets in memory files. Be cautious with personally identifiable information (PII) — check data privacy regulations (GDPR, CCPA) before persisting user data. The reference implementations have no built-in access control; in multi-user systems, implement per-user memory directories and authentication in your tool handlers.

For full implementation examples, use WebFetch:

- Docs: `https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/memory-tool.md`

---

## Client-Side Tools: Bash and Text Editor

The bash and text editor tools are **Anthropic-defined, schema-less** tools. Declare them by `type` and `name` only — the input schema is built into the model and cannot be modified. **Do not pass an `input_schema`**, and do not define a custom tool that happens to be named `"bash"` — that creates a user-defined tool without the built-in behavior.

Both are **client-executed**: Claude returns a `tool_use` block, your code performs the action locally, and you send back a `tool_result`. The API is stateless; your application maintains the shell session or filesystem between turns.

### Bash tool declaration

```json
{"type": "bash_20250124", "name": "bash"}
```

| Language | Declaration |
|---|---|
| Python / TypeScript / Ruby / cURL | plain object `{"type": "bash_20250124", "name": "bash"}` |
| Go | `anthropic.ToolUnionParam{OfBashTool20250124: &anthropic.ToolBash20250124Param{}}` |
| Java | `.addTool(ToolBash20250124.builder().build())` from `com.anthropic.models.messages` |
| C# | `Tools = [new ToolBash20250124()]` from `Anthropic.Models.Messages` |
| PHP | `tools: [new \Anthropic\Messages\ToolBash20250124()]` |

Claude's `tool_use.input` contains either `{"command": "<string>"}` or `{"restart": true}`. Check for `restart` first (reset the session, return a confirmation string); otherwise run `command` and return combined stdout + stderr.

> **Security — commands are untrusted model output.** Run in an isolated environment (container, VM, or restricted user); apply an **allowlist** of permitted executables and reject shell operators (`&&`, `|`, `;`, `` ` ``, `$()`); set timeouts and resource limits; log every command. A blocklist is not sufficient.

### Text editor tool declaration

```json
{"type": "text_editor_20250728", "name": "str_replace_based_edit_tool"}
```

Optional field: `max_characters` to cap `view` output. Java exposes a typed `ToolTextEditor20250728` builder (`com.anthropic.models.messages`); other statically-typed SDKs follow the same naming pattern — see the Anthropic-Defined Tools section in `{lang}/claude-api/tool-use.md` for the exact class.

> **Security — `path` is untrusted model output. Confine every file operation to a fixed project root.** Before executing any command, resolve the model-supplied `path` to its canonical form and verify it remains within your project root; reject the request if it escapes (`..`, symlinks, absolute paths outside the root, URL-encoded traversal like `%2e%2e%2f`). Use your language's built-in path utilities (e.g., Python `pathlib.Path.resolve()` then check `.is_relative_to(root)`). Never call `open()` / `writeFile` / `unlink` directly on the raw `path` value.

`tool_use.input.command` is one of:

| `command` | Other inputs | Action |
|---|---|---|
| `view` | `path`, optional `view_range` | Return file contents or directory listing |
| `create` | `path`, `file_text` | Create/overwrite file with `file_text`. Create a backup if the file already exists. |
| `str_replace` | `path`, `old_str`, `new_str` | Replace exactly one occurrence; error if 0 or >1 matches |
| `insert` | `path`, `insert_line`, `insert_text` | Insert `insert_text` after line `insert_line` (0 = beginning of file) |

For both tools, on error return `{"type": "tool_result", "tool_use_id": "…", "content": "<error text>", "is_error": true}` so Claude can recover.

---

## Structured Outputs

Structured outputs constrain Claude's responses to follow a specific JSON schema, guaranteeing valid, parseable output. This is not a separate tool — it enhances the Messages API response format and/or tool parameter validation.

Two features are available:

- **JSON outputs** (`output_config.format`): Control Claude's response format
- **Strict tool use** (`strict: true`): Guarantee valid tool parameter schemas

**Supported models:** Claude Fable 5, Claude Opus 4.8, Claude Sonnet 5, and Claude Haiku 4.5. Legacy models (Claude Opus 4.5, Claude Opus 4.1) also support structured outputs.

> **Recommended:** Use `client.messages.parse()` which automatically validates responses against your schema. When using `messages.create()` directly, use `output_config: {format: {...}}`. The `output_format` convenience parameter is also accepted by some SDK methods (e.g., `.parse()`), but `output_config.format` is the canonical API-level parameter.

### JSON Schema Limitations

**Supported:**

- Basic types: object, array, string, integer, number, boolean, null
- `enum`, `const`, `anyOf`, `allOf`, `$ref`/`$def`
- String formats: `date-time`, `time`, `date`, `duration`, `email`, `hostname`, `uri`, `ipv4`, `ipv6`, `uuid`
- `additionalProperties: false` (required for all objects)

**Not supported:**

- Recursive schemas
- Numerical constraints (`minimum`, `maximum`, `multipleOf`)
- String constraints (`minLength`, `maxLength`)
- Complex array constraints
- `additionalProperties` set to anything other than `false`

The Python and TypeScript SDKs automatically handle unsupported constraints by removing them from the schema sent to the API and validating them client-side.

### Important Notes

- **First request latency**: New schemas incur a one-time compilation cost. Subsequent requests with the same schema use a 24-hour cache.
- **Refusals**: If Claude refuses for safety reasons (`stop_reason: "refusal"`), the output may not match your schema.
- **Token limits**: If `stop_reason: "max_tokens"`, output may be incomplete. Increase `max_tokens`.
- **Incompatible with**: Citations (returns 400 error), message prefilling.
- **Works with**: Batches API, streaming, token counting, extended thinking.

## Tips for Effective Tool Use

1. **Provide detailed descriptions**: Claude relies heavily on descriptions to understand when and how to use tools
2. **Use specific tool names**: `get_current_weather` is better than `weather`
3. **Validate inputs**: Always validate tool inputs before execution
4. **Handle errors gracefully**: Return informative error messages so Claude can adapt
5. **Limit tool count**: Too many tools can confuse the model — keep the set focused
6. **Test tool interactions**: Verify Claude uses tools correctly in various scenarios

For detailed tool use documentation, use WebFetch:

- URL: `https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/overview`
</doc>

## When to Use WebFetch

Use WebFetch to get the latest documentation when:

- User asks for "latest" or "current" information
- Cached data seems incorrect
- User asks about features not covered here

Live documentation URLs are in `shared/live-sources.md`.

## Common Pitfalls

- Don't truncate inputs when passing files or content to the API. If the content is too long to fit in the context window, notify the user and discuss options (chunking, summarization, etc.) rather than silently truncating.
- **Prefill removed (Fable 5 and the 4.6/4.7/4.8 family):** Assistant message prefills (last-assistant-turn prefills) return a 400 error on Fable 5, Opus 4.6, Opus 4.7, Opus 4.8, and Sonnet 4.6. Use structured outputs (`output_config.format`) or system prompt instructions to control response format instead. (One exception: the fallback-credit prefill claim — when redeeming a credit with `fallback_has_prefill_claim: true`, the server accepts the echoed assistant message; see the migration guide's refusal section.)
- **Confirm migration scope before editing:** When a user asks to migrate code to a newer Claude model without naming a specific file, directory, or file list, **ask which scope to apply first** — the entire working directory, a specific subdirectory, or a specific set of files. Do not start editing until the user confirms. Imperative phrasings like "migrate my codebase", "move my project to X", "upgrade to Sonnet 4.6", or bare "migrate to Opus 4.8" are **still ambiguous** — they tell you what to do but not where, so ask. Proceed without asking only when the prompt names an exact file, a specific directory, or an explicit file list ("migrate `app.py`", "migrate everything under `services/`", "update `a.py` and `b.py`"). See `shared/model-migration.md` Step 0.
- **`max_tokens` defaults:** Don't lowball `max_tokens` — hitting the cap truncates output mid-thought and requires a retry. For non-streaming requests, default to `~16000` (keeps responses under SDK HTTP timeouts). For streaming requests, default to `~64000` (timeouts aren't a concern, so give the model room). Only go lower when you have a hard reason: classification (`~256`), cost caps, deliberately short outputs, or **`max_tokens: 0`** for cache pre-warming (see `shared/prompt-caching.md` → Pre-warming).
- **128K output tokens:** Fable 5, Opus 4.6, Opus 4.7, Opus 4.8, Sonnet 5, and Sonnet 4.6 support up to 128K `max_tokens`, but the SDKs require streaming for values that large to avoid HTTP timeouts. Use `.stream()` with `.get_final_message()` / `.finalMessage()`.
- **Tool call JSON parsing (Fable 5 and the 4.6/4.7/4.8 family):** Fable 5, Opus 4.6, Opus 4.7, Opus 4.8, and Sonnet 4.6 may produce different JSON string escaping in tool call `input` fields (e.g., Unicode or forward-slash escaping). Always parse tool inputs with `json.loads()` / `JSON.parse()` — never do raw string matching on the serialized input.
- **Structured outputs (all models):** Use `output_config: {format: {...}}` instead of the deprecated `output_format` parameter on `messages.create()`. This is a general API change, not 4.6-specific.
- **Don't reimplement SDK functionality:** The SDK provides high-level helpers — use them instead of building from scratch. Specifically: use `stream.finalMessage()` instead of wrapping `.on()` events in `new Promise()`; use typed exception classes (`Anthropic.RateLimitError`, etc.) instead of string-matching error messages; use SDK types (`Anthropic.MessageParam`, `Anthropic.Tool`, `Anthropic.Message`, etc.) instead of redefining equivalent interfaces.
- **Error handling — catch a chain, not one broad class.** A single `except APIStatusError` / `catch (AnthropicServiceException)` / `rescue APIError` loses the distinction between retryable (429, ≥500, network) and non-retryable (400/404) failures. Write a most-specific-first chain — e.g. `NotFoundError` → `RateLimitError` → `APIStatusError` → `APIConnectionError` (or the Go equivalent: `errors.As` into `*anthropic.Error` then `switch apierr.StatusCode { case 404: …; case 429: …; default: … }`). Per-language class names and namespaces are in `shared/error-codes.md`.
- **Don't research SDK types — write first.** If a type name isn't shown in the documentation included in this skill, write the code file from the namespace/package tables in the language-specific doc and let the compiler's error point you to the right name. Do not spend turns on WebFetch, SDK-repo clones, or compiling-and-running a separate reflection program to discover type names before writing — produce the source file first, then fix what the compiler reports. A quick `strings` / `jar tf` / `javap` against the installed SDK is acceptable for locating names (it returns in seconds), but don't escalate beyond that. A file with a wrong type name is recoverable; a session spent on discovery with no file written is not.
- **Bash and text editor tools are Anthropic-defined, schema-less.** Declare `{"type": "bash_20250124", "name": "bash"}` / `{"type": "text_editor_20250728", "name": "str_replace_based_edit_tool"}` — no `input_schema`. A custom tool with your own schema named `"bash"` is a different tool. Handler paths and security checks are in `shared/tool-use-concepts.md` § Client-Side Tools.
- **Advisor tool model pairing.** The advisor tool's `model` must be at least as capable as the request's top-level `model` — e.g. executor `claude-sonnet-5` → advisor `claude-opus-4-8` or `claude-opus-4-7`. An invalid pair returns 400. Pairing table in `shared/tool-use-concepts.md` § Advisor. Availability: `shared/platform-availability.md`.
- **Agent Skills ≠ Managed Agents.** To have Claude generate a `.pptx`/`.xlsx`/etc. via Agent Skills, call `client.beta.messages.create` with `container={"skills": [...]}`, the `code_execution_20260521` tool, and both `code-execution-2025-08-25` + `skills-2025-10-02` betas. Do not use `client.beta.agents` / `sessions` / `environments` here — those are the Managed Agents surface, not Agent Skills.
- **MCP connector needs both halves.** `mcp_servers=[{type:"url", url, name}]` alone is rejected as a validation error — also add `tools=[{type:"mcp_toolset", mcp_server_name:<same name>}]` with beta `mcp-client-2025-11-20`. Availability: `shared/platform-availability.md`.
- **`inference_geo` is a direct top-level request parameter** — `client.messages.create(..., inference_geo="us")` / `.inferenceGeo("us")`. Do not put it in `extra_body` / `putAdditionalBodyProperty`. Supported on Opus 4.6 / Sonnet 4.6 and later; availability: `shared/platform-availability.md`. `response.usage.inference_geo` reports where inference ran.
- **Fine-grained tool streaming is not a beta feature.** Set `eager_input_streaming: true` on the tool definition and call the regular `client.messages.stream(...)`. There is no beta header and no `client.beta.*` path.
- **Cache diagnostics is beta.** Use `client.beta.messages.*` with beta `cache-diagnosis-2026-04-07`. Pass `diagnostics: {previous_message_id: null}` on the first turn and `diagnostics: {previous_message_id: <previous response id>}` on subsequent turns; the result is on `response.diagnostics`. Availability: `shared/platform-availability.md`.
- **Memory tool type is `memory_20250818`.** Declare `{"type": "memory_20250818", "name": "memory"}`. Go uses the beta-namespace type `{OfMemoryTool20250818: &anthropic.BetaMemoryTool20250818Param{}}` on `client.Beta.Messages.New`; Python/TypeScript/Ruby/PHP/C# use the non-beta `client.messages.create`; Java has both a non-beta `MemoryTool20250818` and a beta tool-runner path. Python/TypeScript provide `BetaAbstractMemoryTool` / `betaMemoryTool` helpers for implementing the backend.
- **Use a model the feature actually supports.** Some features are restricted to specific model tiers — fast mode is Opus 4.8 / 4.7 only, task budgets are Fable 5 / Sonnet 5 / Opus 4.8 / 4.7 only, and the advisor tool requires a valid executor↔advisor pair. If the user's prompt names a model that the feature doesn't support, use a supported model instead and note the substitution in the output.
- **Don't define custom types for SDK data structures:** The SDK exports types for all API objects. Use `Anthropic.MessageParam` for messages, `Anthropic.Tool` for tool definitions, `Anthropic.ToolUseBlock` / `Anthropic.ToolResultBlockParam` for tool results, `Anthropic.Message` for responses. Defining your own `interface ChatMessage { role: string; content: unknown }` duplicates what the SDK already provides and loses type safety.
- **Report and document output:** For tasks that produce reports, documents, or visualizations, the code execution sandbox has `python-docx`, `python-pptx`, `matplotlib`, `pillow`, and `pypdf` pre-installed. Claude can generate formatted files (DOCX, PDF, charts) and return them via the Files API — consider this for "report" or "document" type requests instead of plain stdout text.
- **Server-tool errors don't raise.** Web search and web fetch errors return HTTP 200 with a `web_search_tool_result` / `web_fetch_tool_result` block whose `content` is a single error object (e.g. `{error_code: "max_uses_exceeded"}`) — not a raised exception. For web search, a success `content` is a *list*; an error `content` is an *object* — branch on that before indexing.
- **Code execution output block type:** `code_execution_20260521` returns `bash_code_execution_tool_result` (with `.content.stdout`), **not** the legacy bare `code_execution_tool_result`. Iterate `response.content` and match on the correct type.
- **Tool search: never defer everything.** The search tool itself must not have `defer_loading: true`, and at least one tool in `tools` must be non-deferred, or the API returns 400 `All tools have defer_loading set`.

4	lyrics, or from a link) and hasn't pasted chords or supplied audio. For most
5	songs people ask about, **a human-made chart already exists on the web** — and it
6	is usually *more accurate* than machine audio→chord extraction (`audio-to-chords.py`,
7	~80%). So the reliable first move is: search chart sites → adapt the chart to
8	ChordPro → validate. Fall back to audio ACR or interactive fill only when no
9	chart is found.
10	
11	This is the router's highest-value path for "make me a chord sheet for `<song>`",
12	and it's what actually happens in practice — treat existing charts as the
13	default source of chords, not an afterthought.
14	
15	## The workflow
16	
17	Verified across a 7-song C-pop batch — the naive "WebFetch → a2crd" path breaks in
18	two ways (WebFetch's summarizer strips copyrighted lyrics; `a2crd` mis-aligns CJK),
19	so the real recipe is:
20	
21	1. **Search.** `WebSearch` for the song + a chart keyword in the right language:
22	   - EN: `"<artist> <title>" chords`, `... ultimate guitar`, `... chordpro`
23	   - 中文: `<歌手> <歌名> 吉他谱`, `... 和弦`, `... 弹唱谱`, `... 简谱`
24	2. **Fetch RAW, then parse the site's markup.** `WebFetch`'s LLM summary **strips the
25	   copyrighted lyrics** (returns "[歌词已移除]" / "[lyrics omitted]"), so you get chords
26	   with no alignment. Instead `curl -sL <url>` the raw HTML and parse the site markup:
27	   - **Chord4** (best for Mandarin): chords are parenthesized syllables like
28	     `你不是真正(的)快樂` (chord sits above the `(char)`), plus `data-chord` attrs,
29	     inside the `tabs_content` `<pre>` block.
30	   - **Ultimate Guitar**: JS-rendered — the chart is in the embedded **`js-store`
31	     `data-content` JSON** as `[ch]C[/ch] … [tab]…[/tab]`.
32	   - **Image-only 六线谱** (common for C-pop — jitahome/qinhun/guistudy…): there is NO
33	     text to parse. `WebFetch` will *confidently fabricate* per-line placement — trust
34	     only an explicit chord **list**, never fabricated alignment.
35	3. **Lyrics come SEPARATELY from LRCLIB** (`scripts/fetch-lyrics.py -o song.lrc`).
36	   Treat LRCLIB lyrics as ground truth (they arrive traditional or simplified —
37	   see below).
38	4. **Align by phrase, not by column.** `chordpro --a2crd` only works on **pure-Latin**
39	   chords-over-lyrics; for CJK its 1-char = 1-column heuristic drifts (full-width
40	   chars are 2 display cells). Place each chord over the syllable/phrase it belongs
41	   to by musical judgment. If the chart omits an intro/interlude, reuse the relevant
42	   verse loop labeled "verify against recording" — never fabricate a specific riff.
43	5. **Validate AND render.** `scripts/validate-cho.sh` (parse) **and**
44	   `scripts/render-cho.sh` (CJK-safe render + glyph-check — a bare `chordpro -o`
45	   renders Chinese as tofu yet passes validation). Caption a `{comment:}` naming the
46	   source + "published arrangement — verify against the recording (capo/key may
47	   differ)". Not machine ACR, so no `AUTO-GENERATED` header.
48	
49	## Where the charts live
50	
51	Coverage and format vary; try a couple, and **don't rely on any single site**
52	(the batch hit `kanpu8` HTTP 403 and `jitapai` expired-TLS). Auto-generated sites
53	are effectively ACR — same ~80% caveat.
54	
55	**Chinese / Taiwan (great for C-pop like the 落葉歸根 case):**
56	- **Chord4 / 和弦网** — `chord4.com` — **the repeat winner** (sourced chords in 6 of 7
57	  eval runs). Raw HTML exposes a parseable chords-over-lyrics block. Start here for Mandarin.
58	- **91譜 / 91pu** — `91pu.com.tw` — large Taiwan library, but **JS-rendered**; `curl`
59	  often returns only page chrome. Good to eyeball, awkward to parse.
60	- **弹唱谱 / 简谱 hubs** — `qupu123`, `中国曲谱网 (qupu.com)`, `17jita`, `jitaba/jitapu`,
61	  `jitahome`, `qinhun`, `guistudy` — **mostly image 六线谱** (manual transcription);
62	  simplified-character search finds more.
63	- **魔鏡歌詞 / Mojim** — `mojim.com` — mostly lyrics, some chords; good for confirming lyrics.
64	
65	**Western / global:**
66	- **Ultimate Guitar** — `ultimate-guitar.com` — largest, but **fully JS-rendered**;
67	  `WebFetch` returns no chords. Parse the `js-store` `data-content` JSON from raw HTML.
68	- **e-chords**, **Chordie**, **AZChords** — chords-over-lyrics, usually parseable.
69	- **Songsterr** — public API for tabs/chords (`songsterr.com/a/wsa/api-tabs-a26570`).
70	- **Chordu / Chordify / GuitarTuna** — **auto-generated from audio** → ACR-quality
71	  (~80%, verify), not human-checked. Use only to corroborate.
72	
73	## Format taxonomy (what you'll get back)
74	
75	| Format | How to use it | Reliability |
76	|---|---|---|
77	| Latin chords-over-lyrics text | `chordpro --a2crd` → clean up → validate | High (human-made) |
78	| CJK chords-over-lyrics text | hand-align by phrase (a2crd drifts on full-width) → validate | High |
79	| Inline / chord chart | transcribe into the ChordPro template | High |
80	| Guitar tab (6-line) | embed in a `{start_of_tab}` block; or use for riffs only | High for riffs |
81	| 简谱 (numbered) / image scan | manual transcription; no reliable OMR — trust only an explicit chord list | Low (tedious) |
82	| Auto-generated (chordu/chordify) | same as ACR — a draft to verify | ~80% |
83	
84	## Simplified vs traditional, and the metadata a chart won't give you
85	
86	- **Char-set mismatch is common**: a simplified-character chart vs traditional LRCLIB
87	  lyrics (or vice versa). Treat the **LRCLIB lyrics as ground truth** and map chords by
88	  position/meaning, not string equality. `opencc` can convert if you must reconcile.
89	- **capo / tempo / composer / year** are usually **absent from text charts**. Get them
90	  from a second source (Wikipedia/Baidu/SongBPM), but **tempo is unreliable** — beware
91	  the half-time trap (a song *felt* at 82 BPM is often listed as 164). Omit an unknown
92	  field or caption it "unverified"; never fabricate.
93	
94	## Legality (surface it, don't bury it)
95	
96	These charts are user-contributed arrangements; the underlying songs are usually
97	copyrighted. Keep it **personal-use and local**, don't redistribute the fetched
98	chart or lyrics commercially, and cite the source in a `{comment:}`. Prefer this
99	route over downloading audio — it avoids the platform-ToS problem entirely — but
100	the copyright of the song itself still applies to any lyrics you embed.
101
```

```text
1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# render-cho.sh — Render a ChordPro file to PDF with correct fonts, then prove the
3	# glyphs actually made it into the PDF.
4	#
5	# Why this exists: `chordpro`'s default fonts (GNU FreeFont) contain NO CJK glyphs,
6	# so a bare `chordpro -o song.pdf song.cho` on a Chinese/Japanese/Korean song exits
7	# 0, emits no warning, and passes `validate-cho.sh` — while silently dropping every
8	# non-Latin character (tofu / blank). Parse-validity is not render-fidelity. This
9	# script auto-detects a CJK-capable font, renders through it, and then round-trips
10	# the PDF to confirm the expected script is visible. It closes the verify loop for
11	# non-Latin songs.
12	#
13	# Bash 3.2 compatible (works on stock macOS).
14	
15	set -euo pipefail
16	
17	usage() {
18	  cat <<'EOF'
19	Usage: render-cho.sh [OPTIONS] <file.cho>
20	
21	Render a ChordPro file to PDF and verify the glyphs rendered (not tofu).
22	If the .cho contains CJK, a CJK-capable font is auto-detected and injected via a
23	temporary `--config`; the output PDF is then glyph-checked.
24	
25	Options:
26	  -o, --output FILE   Output PDF path (default: <file>.pdf next to the input).
27	  --font PATH         Force a specific font file (overrides auto-detection).
28	  --keep-config       Write the font --config next to the PDF instead of a temp file.
29	  --help, -h          Show this help and exit.
30	
31	Auto-detected CJK fonts (first that exists wins):
32	  macOS: /System/Library/Fonts/Supplemental/Arial Unicode.ttf, PingFang.ttc, STHeiti
33	  Linux: Noto Sans CJK (Noto*CJK*.ttc), wqy-* — install fonts-noto-cjk if missing.
34	
35	Verdict (stdout, JSON):
36	  {"file":"song.cho","pdf":"song.pdf","cjk":true,"font":"…/Arial Unicode.ttf","glyphs_ok":true}
37	
38	Exit codes:
39	  0  rendered and (if CJK) glyphs verified present
40	  1  invalid arguments
41	  2  input not found / chordpro not installed
42	  3  render failed, OR CJK song rendered as tofu (no CJK glyphs in the PDF)
43	EOF
44	}
45	
46	log() { printf '%s\n' "$*" >&2; }
47	die() { printf 'error: %s\n' "$*" >&2; exit "${2:-1}"; }
48	
49	FILE=""; OUT=""; FONT=""; KEEP_CONFIG=0
50	while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
51	  case "$1" in
52	    -o|--output) OUT="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
53	    --font) FONT="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
54	    --keep-config) KEEP_CONFIG=1; shift ;;
55	    --help|-h) usage; exit 0 ;;
56	    -*) die "unknown flag: $1 (try --help)" 1 ;;
57	    *) [ -n "$FILE" ] && die "only one file allowed" 1; FILE="$1"; shift ;;
58	  esac
59	done
60	
61	[ -n "$FILE" ] || die "missing <file.cho> (try --help)" 1
62	[ -f "$FILE" ] || die "file not found: $FILE" 2
63	command -v chordpro >/dev/null 2>&1 || die "chordpro not on PATH. Install: brew install perl cpanminus && cpanm App::Music::ChordPro (then activate local::lib; see references/cli-and-rendering.md)" 2
64	[ -n "$OUT" ] || OUT="${FILE%.*}.pdf"
65	
66	# Does the input contain CJK (CJK Unified Ideographs, Hiragana, Katakana, Hangul)?
67	has_cjk() {
68	  python3 - "$1" <<'PY' 2>/dev/null
69	import sys
70	t=open(sys.argv[1],encoding="utf-8",errors="ignore").read()
71	def cjk(c):
72	    o=ord(c)
73	    return (0x4E00<=o<=0x9FFF) or (0x3040<=o<=0x30FF) or (0xAC00<=o<=0xD7AF) or (0x3400<=o<=0x4DBF)
74	sys.exit(0 if any(cjk(c) for c in t) else 1)
75	PY
76	}
77	
78	detect_font() {
79	  local c
80	  for c in \
81	    "$HOME/Library/Fonts/Arial Unicode.ttf" \
82	    "/System/Library/Fonts/Supplemental/Arial Unicode.ttf" \
83	    "/Library/Fonts/Arial Unicode.ttf" \
84	    "/System/Library/Fonts/PingFang.ttc" \
85	    "/System/Library/Fonts/STHeiti Light.ttc" \
86	    /usr/share/fonts/opentype/noto/NotoSansCJK-Regular.ttc \
87	    /usr/share/fonts/truetype/noto/NotoSansCJK-Regular.ttc \
88	    /usr/share/fonts/noto-cjk/NotoSansCJK-Regular.ttc \
89	    /usr/share/fonts/opentype/noto/NotoSerifCJK-Regular.ttc \
90	    /usr/share/fonts/truetype/wqy/wqy-microhei.ttc ; do
91	    if [ -f "$c" ]; then printf '%s' "$c"; return 0; fi
92	  done
93	  return 1
94	}
95	
96	CJK=0; FONT_USED=""; CONFIG=""
97	if has_cjk "$FILE"; then
98	  CJK=1
99	  if [ -z "$FONT" ]; then
100	    FONT="$(detect_font || true)"
101	    [ -n "$FONT" ] || die "input has CJK but no CJK font found. Install one (macOS ships 'Arial Unicode.ttf'; Linux: fonts-noto-cjk) or pass --font PATH." 3
102	  fi
103	  FONT_USED="$FONT"
104	  if [ "$KEEP_CONFIG" = "1" ]; then CONFIG="$(dirname "$OUT")/.chordpro-fonts.json"; else CONFIG="$(mktemp -t chordpro-fonts).json"; fi
105	  # Point every text-bearing PDF font role at the CJK font (chords stay Latin but
106	  # sharing the font is harmless and keeps annotations legible).
107	  python3 - "$FONT" > "$CONFIG" <<'PY'
108	import json,sys
109	f=sys.argv[1]
110	roles=["title","subtitle","text","chord","comment","comment_italic","comment_box","tab","grid","toc","footer"]
111	print(json.dumps({"pdf":{"fonts":{r:{"file":f} for r in roles}}}, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2))
112	PY
113	  [ "$KEEP_CONFIG" = "1" ] || trap 'rm -f "$CONFIG"' EXIT
114	fi
115	
116	# Render
117	if [ "$CJK" = "1" ]; then
118	  chordpro --config "$CONFIG" -o "$OUT" "$FILE" 2>/tmp/render.$$ || { cat /tmp/render.$$ >&2; rm -f /tmp/render.$$; die "chordpro render failed" 3; }
119	else
120	  chordpro -o "$OUT" "$FILE" 2>/tmp/render.$$ || { cat /tmp/render.$$ >&2; rm -f /tmp/render.$$; die "chordpro render failed" 3; }
121	fi
122	rm -f /tmp/render.$$
123	[ -f "$OUT" ] || die "no PDF produced at $OUT" 3
124	
125	# Glyph-check: for a CJK song, confirm CJK actually made it into the PDF text layer.
126	GLYPHS_OK=true
127	if [ "$CJK" = "1" ]; then

129	    if pdftotext "$OUT" - 2>/dev/null | python3 -c 'import sys; t=sys.stdin.read(); sys.exit(0 if any(0x4E00<=ord(c)<=0x9FFF or 0x3040<=ord(c)<=0x30FF or 0xAC00<=ord(c)<=0xD7AF for c in t) else 1)'; then
130	      GLYPHS_OK=true
131	    else
132	      GLYPHS_OK=false
133	      log "GLYPH CHECK FAILED: no CJK glyphs found in $OUT — the PDF is tofu."
134	      log "The chosen font ($FONT_USED) may lack the needed glyphs; try --font with a fuller CJK font."
135	    fi
136	  else
137	    log "note: pdftotext not found (poppler) — skipping glyph verification. Install poppler to enable it."
138	  fi
139	fi
140	
141	printf '{"file":"%s","pdf":"%s","cjk":%s,"font":"%s","glyphs_ok":%s}\n' \
142	  "$FILE" "$OUT" "$( [ "$CJK" = 1 ] && echo true || echo false )" "$FONT_USED" "$GLYPHS_OK"
143	
144	if [ "$GLYPHS_OK" = "false" ]; then exit 3; fi
145	log "OK: rendered $OUT$( [ "$CJK" = 1 ] && echo ' (CJK glyphs verified)')"

9	"""fetch-lyrics.py — Fetch lyrics from LRCLIB (free, no API key).
10	
11	LRCLIB is the default lyrics source for this skill: open, key-less,
12	cross-platform, and it returns time-synced .lrc when available. Lyrics (the
13	data) go to stdout or --output; diagnostics go to stderr.
14	
15	Run with uv (self-contained via PEP 723 inline metadata):
16	
17	    uv run fetch-lyrics.py --artist "Adele" --track "Hello" --duration 295
18	    uv run fetch-lyrics.py --plain --artist "..." --track "..." -o out.txt
19

21	references/lyrics-sources.md — this script intentionally ships only the open
22	LRCLIB path and does not scrape.
23	
24	Exit codes:
25	  0  lyrics found and emitted
26	  1  invalid arguments
27	  3  no matching lyrics found
28	  4  network / API error
29	"""
30	from __future__ import annotations
31	
32	import argparse
33	import sys
34	
35	import httpx
36	
37	LRCLIB = "https://lrclib.net/api"
38	UA = "chordpro-skill/1.0 (agent-skills; +https://github.com/daviddwlee84/agent-skills)"
39	
40	
41	def log(msg: str) -> None:
42	    """Diagnostics -> stderr."""
43	    print(msg, file=sys.stderr)
44	
45	
46	def make_parser() -> argparse.ArgumentParser:
47	    p = argparse.ArgumentParser(
48	        prog="fetch-lyrics.py",
49	        description="Fetch lyrics from LRCLIB (synced .lrc by default, --plain for text).",
50	        epilog=(
51	            "Examples:\n"
52	            '  uv run fetch-lyrics.py --artist "Adele" --track "Hello" --duration 295\n'
53	            '  uv run fetch-lyrics.py --plain --artist "周杰倫" --track "晴天"\n'
54	        ),
55	        formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter,
56	    )
57	    p.add_argument("--artist", required=True, help="Artist / performer name.")
58	    p.add_argument("--track", required=True, help="Track / song title.")
59	    p.add_argument("--album", help="Album name (improves exact-match on /get).")
60	    p.add_argument(
61	        "--duration",
62	        type=int,
63	        help="Track duration in seconds (helps disambiguate on /get and /search).",
64	    )
65	    p.add_argument(
66	        "--plain",
67	        action="store_true",
68	        help="Return plain text instead of the synced .lrc.",
69	    )
70	    p.add_argument("-o", "--output", help="Write lyrics to this file instead of stdout.")
71	    p.add_argument(
72	        "--dry-run",
73	        action="store_true",
74	        help="Print the requests that would be made, then exit.",
75	    )
76	    return p
77	
78	
79	def _emit(text: str, output: str | None) -> None:
80	    if output:
81	        with open(output, "w", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
82	            fh.write(text.rstrip("\n") + "\n")
83	        log(f"wrote {output} ({len(text.splitlines())} lines)")
84	    else:
85	        sys.stdout.write(text.rstrip("\n") + "\n")
86	
87	
88	def _has_cjk(s: str) -> bool:
89	    return any(
90	        0x4E00 <= ord(c) <= 0x9FFF
91	        or 0x3040 <= ord(c) <= 0x30FF
92	        or 0xAC00 <= ord(c) <= 0xD7AF
93	        for c in s
94	    )
95	
96	
97	def _romanize_variants(s: str) -> list[str]:
98	    """Romanization candidates for CJK text. LRCLIB indexes names the conventional
99	    way (surname + concatenated given name, e.g. 李榮浩 -> 'Li Ronghao'), so try that
100	    plus a per-syllable form ('Li Rong Hao')."""
101	    try:
102	        from pypinyin import lazy_pinyin
103	    except ImportError:
104	        return [s]
105	    sylls = [w for w in lazy_pinyin(s) if w]
106	    if not sylls:
107	        return [s]
108	    per_syllable = " ".join(w.capitalize() for w in sylls)  # Li Rong Hao / Li Bai
109	    name = sylls[0].capitalize()
110	    if len(sylls) > 1:
111	        name += " " + "".join(sylls[1:]).capitalize()  # Li Ronghao / Li Bai
112	    out: list[str] = []
113	    for v in (name, per_syllable):
114	        if v and v not in out:
115	            out.append(v)
116	    return out
117	
118	
119	def _lookup(client, artist, track, album, duration):
120	    """Try LRCLIB /get then /search; return the best record or None."""
121	    params: dict[str, object] = {"artist_name": artist, "track_name": track}
122	    if album:
123	        params["album_name"] = album
124	    if duration:
125	        params["duration"] = duration
126	    resp = client.get(f"{LRCLIB}/get", params=params)
127	    if resp.status_code == 200:
128	        rec = resp.json()
129	        log(f"exact match: {rec.get('artistName')} – {rec.get('trackName')}")
130	        return rec
131	    if resp.status_code != 404:
132	        resp.raise_for_status()
133	    log("exact /get miss; trying /search…")
134	    sresp = client.get(
135	        f"{LRCLIB}/search", params={"artist_name": artist, "track_name": track}
136	    )
137	    sresp.raise_for_status()
138	    results = sresp.json() or []
139	    if not results:
140	        return None
141	    if duration:
142	        results.sort(key=lambda r: abs((r.get("duration") or 0) - duration))
143	    rec = results[0]
144	    log(
145	        f"best search match: {rec.get('artistName')} – "
146	        f"{rec.get('trackName')} ({rec.get('duration')}s)"
147	    )
148	    return rec
149	
150	
151	def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
152	    args = make_parser().parse_args(argv)
153	
154	    get_params: dict[str, object] = {
155	        "artist_name": args.artist,
156	        "track_name": args.track,
157	    }
158	    if args.album:
159	        get_params["album_name"] = args.album
160	    if args.duration:
161	        get_params["duration"] = args.duration
162	
163	    if args.dry_run:
164	        log(f"[dry-run] GET {LRCLIB}/get params={get_params}")
165	        log(
166	            f"[dry-run] fallback GET {LRCLIB}/search "
167	            f"params={{'artist_name': {args.artist!r}, 'track_name': {args.track!r}}}"
168	        )
169	        return 0
170	
171	    try:
172	        with httpx.Client(headers={"User-Agent": UA}, timeout=20.0) as client:
173	            rec = _lookup(client, args.artist, args.track, args.album, args.duration)
174	            if rec is None and (_has_cjk(args.artist) or _has_cjk(args.track)):
175	                for a in _romanize_variants(args.artist):
176	                    for t in _romanize_variants(args.track):
177	                        if (a, t) == (args.artist, args.track):
178	                            continue
179	                        log(f"CJK miss; retrying romanized: {a!r} / {t!r}")
180	                        rec = _lookup(client, a, t, args.album, args.duration)
181	                        if rec is not None:
182	                            break
183	                    if rec is not None:
184	                        break
185	    except httpx.HTTPError as exc:
186	        log(f"LRCLIB request failed: {exc}")
187	        return 4
188	
189	    if rec is None:
190	        log("no matching lyrics found")
191	        return 3
192	    if rec.get("instrumental"):
193	        log("LRCLIB marks this track as instrumental — no lyrics available.")
194	        return 3
195	
196	    synced = rec.get("syncedLyrics")
197	    plain = rec.get("plainLyrics")
198	
199	    if args.plain:
200	        text = plain or ""
201	        if not text:
202	            log("no plain lyrics available for this track")
203	            return 3
204	    else:
205	        text = synced or ""
206	        if not text:
207	            log("no synced .lrc available; falling back to plain text (--plain)")
208	            text = plain or ""
209	        if not text:
210	            log("no lyrics (synced or plain) available for this track")
211	            return 3
212	
213	    _emit(text, args.output)
214	    return 0
215	
216

218	    sys.exit(main())

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# render-cho.sh — Render a ChordPro file to PDF with correct fonts, then prove the
3	# glyphs actually made it into the PDF.
4	#
5	# Why this exists: `chordpro`'s default fonts (GNU FreeFont) contain NO CJK glyphs,
6	# so a bare `chordpro -o song.pdf song.cho` on a Chinese/Japanese/Korean song exits
7	# 0, emits no warning, and passes `validate-cho.sh` — while silently dropping every
8	# non-Latin character (tofu / blank). Parse-validity is not render-fidelity. This
9	# script auto-detects a CJK-capable font, renders through it, and then round-trips
10	# the PDF to confirm the expected script is visible. It closes the verify loop for
11	# non-Latin songs.
12	#
13	# Bash 3.2 compatible (works on stock macOS).
14	
15	set -euo pipefail
16	
17	usage() {
18	  cat <<'EOF'
19	Usage: render-cho.sh [OPTIONS] <file.cho>
20	
21	Render a ChordPro file to PDF and verify the glyphs rendered (not tofu).
22	If the .cho contains CJK, a CJK-capable font is auto-detected and injected via a
23	temporary `--config`; the output PDF is then glyph-checked.
24	
25	Options:
26	  -o, --output FILE   Output PDF path (default: <file>.pdf next to the input).
27	  --font PATH         Force a specific font file (overrides auto-detection).
28	  --keep-config       Write the font --config next to the PDF instead of a temp file.
29	  --help, -h          Show this help and exit.
30	
31	Auto-detected CJK fonts (first that exists wins):
32	  macOS: /System/Library/Fonts/Supplemental/Arial Unicode.ttf, PingFang.ttc, STHeiti
33	  Linux: Noto Sans CJK (Noto*CJK*.ttc), wqy-* — install fonts-noto-cjk if missing.
34	
35	Verdict (stdout, JSON):
36	  {"file":"song.cho","pdf":"song.pdf","cjk":true,"font":"…/Arial Unicode.ttf","glyphs_ok":true}
37	
38	Exit codes:
39	  0  rendered and (if CJK) glyphs verified present
40	  1  invalid arguments
41	  2  input not found / chordpro not installed
42	  3  render failed, OR CJK song rendered as tofu (no CJK glyphs in the PDF)
43	EOF
44	}
45	
46	log() { printf '%s\n' "$*" >&2; }
47	die() { printf 'error: %s\n' "$*" >&2; exit "${2:-1}"; }
48	
49	FILE=""; OUT=""; FONT=""; KEEP_CONFIG=0
50	while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
51	  case "$1" in
52	    -o|--output) OUT="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
53	    --font) FONT="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
54	    --keep-config) KEEP_CONFIG=1; shift ;;
55	    --help|-h) usage; exit 0 ;;
56	    -*) die "unknown flag: $1 (try --help)" 1 ;;
57	    *) [ -n "$FILE" ] && die "only one file allowed" 1; FILE="$1"; shift ;;
58	  esac
59	done
60	
61	[ -n "$FILE" ] || die "missing <file.cho> (try --help)" 1
62	[ -f "$FILE" ] || die "file not found: $FILE" 2
63	command -v chordpro >/dev/null 2>&1 || die "chordpro not on PATH. Install: brew install perl cpanminus && cpanm App::Music::ChordPro (then activate local::lib; see references/cli-and-rendering.md)" 2
64	[ -n "$OUT" ] || OUT="${FILE%.*}.pdf"
65	
66	# Does the input contain CJK (CJK Unified Ideographs, Hiragana, Katakana, Hangul)?
67	has_cjk() {
68	  python3 - "$1" <<'PY' 2>/dev/null
69	import sys
70	t=open(sys.argv[1],encoding="utf-8",errors="ignore").read()
71	def cjk(c):
72	    o=ord(c)
73	    return (0x4E00<=o<=0x9FFF) or (0x3040<=o<=0x30FF) or (0xAC00<=o<=0xD7AF) or (0x3400<=o<=0x4DBF)
74	sys.exit(0 if any(cjk(c) for c in t) else 1)
75	PY
76	}

87	    /usr/share/fonts/truetype/noto/NotoSansCJK-Regular.ttc \
88	    /usr/share/fonts/noto-cjk/NotoSansCJK-Regular.ttc \
89	    /usr/share/fonts/opentype/noto/NotoSerifCJK-Regular.ttc \

92	  done

111	print(json.dumps({"pdf":{"fonts":{r:{"file":f} for r in roles}}}, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2))

9	"""fetch-lyrics.py — Fetch lyrics from LRCLIB (free, no API key).
10	
11	LRCLIB is the default lyrics source for this skill: open, key-less,
12	cross-platform, and it returns time-synced .lrc when available. Lyrics (the
13	data) go to stdout or --output; diagnostics go to stderr.
14	
15	Run with uv (self-contained via PEP 723 inline metadata):
16	
17	    uv run fetch-lyrics.py --artist "Adele" --track "Hello" --duration 295
18	    uv run fetch-lyrics.py --plain --artist "..." --track "..." -o out.txt
19	
20	Other sources (Musixmatch, NetEase, QQ, Genius, Mojim) are documented in
21	references/lyrics-sources.md — this script intentionally ships only the open
22	LRCLIB path and does not scrape.
23	
24	Exit codes:
25	  0  lyrics found and emitted
26	  1  invalid arguments
27	  3  no matching lyrics found
28	  4  network / API error
29	"""
30	from __future__ import annotations
31	
32	import argparse
33	import sys
34	
35	import httpx
36	
37	LRCLIB = "https://lrclib.net/api"
38	UA = "chordpro-skill/1.0 (agent-skills; +https://github.com/daviddwlee84/agent-skills)"
39	
40	
41	def log(msg: str) -> None:
42	    """Diagnostics -> stderr."""
43	    print(msg, file=sys.stderr)
44	
45	
46	def make_parser() -> argparse.ArgumentParser:
47	    p = argparse.ArgumentParser(
48	        prog="fetch-lyrics.py",
49	        description="Fetch lyrics from LRCLIB (synced .lrc by default, --plain for text).",
50	        epilog=(
51	            "Examples:\n"
52	            '  uv run fetch-lyrics.py --artist "Adele" --track "Hello" --duration 295\n'
53	            '  uv run fetch-lyrics.py --plain --artist "周杰倫" --track "晴天"\n'
54	        ),
55	        formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter,
56	    )
57	    p.add_argument("--artist", required=True, help="Artist / performer name.")
58	    p.add_argument("--track", required=True, help="Track / song title.")
59	    p.add_argument("--album", help="Album name (improves exact-match on /get).")
60	    p.add_argument(
61	        "--duration",
62	        type=int,
63	        help="Track duration in seconds (helps disambiguate on /get and /search).",
64	    )
65	    p.add_argument(
66	        "--plain",
67	        action="store_true",
68	        help="Return plain text instead of the synced .lrc.",
69	    )
70	    p.add_argument("-o", "--output", help="Write lyrics to this file instead of stdout.")
71	    p.add_argument(
72	        "--dry-run",
73	        action="store_true",
74	        help="Print the requests that would be made, then exit.",
75	    )
76	    return p
77	
78	
79	def _emit(text: str, output: str | None) -> None:
80	    if output:
81	        with open(output, "w", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
82	            fh.write(text.rstrip("\n") + "\n")
83	        log(f"wrote {output} ({len(text.splitlines())} lines)")
84	    else:
85	        sys.stdout.write(text.rstrip("\n") + "\n")
86	
87	
88	def _has_cjk(s: str) -> bool:
89	    return any(
90	        0x4E00 <= ord(c) <= 0x9FFF
91	        or 0x3040 <= ord(c) <= 0x30FF
92	        or 0xAC00 <= ord(c) <= 0xD7AF
93	        for c in s
94	    )
95	
96	
97	def _romanize_variants(s: str) -> list[str]:
98	    """Romanization candidates for CJK text. LRCLIB indexes names the conventional
99	    way (surname + concatenated given name, e.g. 李榮浩 -> 'Li Ronghao'), so try that
100	    plus a per-syllable form ('Li Rong Hao')."""
101	    try:
102	        from pypinyin import lazy_pinyin
103	    except ImportError:
104	        return [s]
105	    sylls = [w for w in lazy_pinyin(s) if w]
106	    if not sylls:
107	        return [s]
108	    per_syllable = " ".join(w.capitalize() for w in sylls)  # Li Rong Hao / Li Bai
109	    name = sylls[0].capitalize()
110	    if len(sylls) > 1:
111	        name += " " + "".join(sylls[1:]).capitalize()  # Li Ronghao / Li Bai
112	    out: list[str] = []
113	    for v in (name, per_syllable):
114	        if v and v not in out:
115	            out.append(v)
116	    return out
117	
118	
119	def _lookup(client, artist, track, album, duration):
120	    """Try LRCLIB /get then /search; return the best record or None."""
121	    params: dict[str, object] = {"artist_name": artist, "track_name": track}
122	    if album:
123	        params["album_name"] = album
124	    if duration:
125	        params["duration"] = duration
126	    resp = client.get(f"{LRCLIB}/get", params=params)
127	    if resp.status_code == 200:
128	        rec = resp.json()
129	        log(f"exact match: {rec.get('artistName')} – {rec.get('trackName')}")
130	        return rec
131	    if resp.status_code != 404:
132	        resp.raise_for_status()
133	    log("exact /get miss; trying /search…")
134	    sresp = client.get(
135	        f"{LRCLIB}/search", params={"artist_name": artist, "track_name": track}
136	    )
137	    sresp.raise_for_status()
138	    results = sresp.json() or []
139	    if not results:
140	        return None
141	    if duration:
142	        results.sort(key=lambda r: abs((r.get("duration") or 0) - duration))
143	    rec = results[0]
144	    log(
145	        f"best search match: {rec.get('artistName')} – "
146	        f"{rec.get('trackName')} ({rec.get('duration')}s)"
147	    )
148	    return rec

151	def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
152	    args = make_parser().parse_args(argv)
153	
154	    get_params: dict[str, object] = {
155	        "artist_name": args.artist,
156	        "track_name": args.track,
157	    }
158	    if args.album:
159	        get_params["album_name"] = args.album
160	    if args.duration:

162	
163	    if args.dry_run:
164	        log(f"[dry-run] GET {LRCLIB}/get params={get_params}")
165	        log(
166	            f"[dry-run] fallback GET {LRCLIB}/search "
167	            f"params={{'artist_name': {args.artist!r}, 'track_name': {args.track!r}}}"
168	        )
169	        return 0
170	
171	    try:
172	        with httpx.Client(headers={"User-Agent": UA}, timeout=20.0) as client:
173	            rec = _lookup(client, args.artist, args.track, args.album, args.duration)
174	            if rec is None and (_has_cjk(args.artist) or _has_cjk(args.track)):
175	                for a in _romanize_variants(args.artist):

179	                        log(f"CJK miss; retrying romanized: {a!r} / {t!r}")
180	                        rec = _lookup(client, a, t, args.album, args.duration)
181	                        if rec is not None:
182	                            break
183	                    if rec is not None:
184	                        break
185	    except httpx.HTTPError as exc:
186	        log(f"LRCLIB request failed: {exc}")
187	        return 4
188	
189	    if rec is None:
190	        log("no matching lyrics found")
191	        return 3

```text
1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# validate-cho.sh — Validate a ChordPro file by strict-parsing it with the chordpro CLI.
3	#
4	# The verify loop for this skill: never hand back an unvalidated .cho. Runs
5	# `chordpro --strict` and reports whether the file parses cleanly. Data (a JSON
6	# verdict) goes to stdout; human notes and parser warnings go to stderr.
7	#
8	# Bash 3.2 compatible (works on stock macOS).
9	
10	set -euo pipefail
11	
12	usage() {
13	  cat <<'EOF'
14	Usage: validate-cho.sh [OPTIONS] <file.cho>
15	
16	Strict-parse a ChordPro file and report validity. Emits a JSON verdict on stdout
17	and any parser warnings on stderr.
18	
19	Options:
20	  --help, -h         Show this help and exit.
21	
22	Examples:
23	  validate-cho.sh song.cho
24	
25	Verdict (stdout):
26	  {"file":"song.cho","valid":true,"warnings":0}
27	
28	Exit codes:
29	  0  file parses (valid; warnings may still be present — see stderr)
30	  1  invalid arguments
31	  2  file not found
32	  3  file failed to parse, OR chordpro is not installed (see stderr for guidance)
33	EOF
34	}
35	
36	log() { printf '%s\n' "$*" >&2; }
37	die() { printf 'error: %s\n' "$*" >&2; exit "${2:-1}"; }
38	
39	FILE=""
40	while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
41	  case "$1" in
42	    --help|-h) usage; exit 0 ;;
43	    --) shift; [ $# -gt 0 ] && FILE="$1"; break ;;
44	    -*) die "unknown flag: $1 (try --help)" 1 ;;
45	    *)
46	      if [ -n "$FILE" ]; then die "only one file allowed (got '$FILE' and '$1')" 1; fi
47	      FILE="$1"; shift ;;
48	  esac
49	done
50	
51	[ -n "$FILE" ] || die "missing <file.cho> (try --help)" 1
52	[ -f "$FILE" ] || die "file not found: $FILE" 2
53	
54	if ! command -v chordpro >/dev/null 2>&1; then
55	  log "chordpro CLI not found on PATH. Install it (macOS has no Homebrew formula):"
56	  log "  brew install perl cpanminus && cpanm App::Music::ChordPro"
57	  log "Then re-run. The file was not validated; the ChordPro format is still"
58	  log "human-checkable by eye (see references/chordpro-format.md)."
59	  printf '{"file":"%s","valid":null,"error":"chordpro-not-installed"}\n' "$FILE"
60	  exit 3
61	fi
62	
63	tmperr="$(mktemp)"
64	trap 'rm -f "$tmperr"' EXIT
65	
66	# --generate=Text -o /dev/null discards the render so stdout stays clean; strict
67	# mode surfaces malformed/unknown directives as stderr warnings.
68	set +e
69	chordpro --strict --generate=Text -o /dev/null "$FILE" 2>"$tmperr"
70	rc=$?
71	set -e
72	
73	warncount="$(grep -c . "$tmperr" 2>/dev/null || true)"
74	[ -n "$warncount" ] || warncount=0
75	
76	# Demystify the most common false-alarm: strict mode warns "Unknown chord" for a
77	# valid chord it has no built-in diagram for (e.g. Em/C#, F#m7b5). It renders fine.
78	if grep -q "Unknown chord" "$tmperr" 2>/dev/null; then
79	  log 'note: "Unknown chord" = no built-in diagram for a valid chord — add a {define} or ignore (not a parse error).'
80	fi
81	
82	if [ "$rc" -eq 0 ]; then
83	  if [ "$warncount" -gt 0 ]; then
84	    log "PASS (with $warncount warning line(s) — review below): $FILE"
85	    cat "$tmperr" >&2
86	  else
87	    log "PASS: $FILE parses cleanly"
88	  fi
89	  printf '{"file":"%s","valid":true,"warnings":%s}\n' "$FILE" "$warncount"
90	  exit 0
91	else
92	  log "FAIL: $FILE did not parse (chordpro exit=$rc)"
93	  cat "$tmperr" >&2
94	  printf '{"file":"%s","valid":false,"warnings":%s}\n' "$FILE" "$warncount"
95	  exit 3
96	fi
97
```

这涉及两个具体的问题：一是和弦变化的时间标记相对于歌词音节的位置精准度，二是选择的和弦本身的准确性。

我在思考这个技能的工作流程中这两个问题的根源。目前的技能有多条路线：在线搜索现有的和弦谱、将带和弦的歌词文本转换、音频转和弦的识别、以及从歌词库加上交互式填充。用户主要是通过歌曲名称来查找C-pop歌曲的和弦，目前的主要路线是搜索在线和弦谱并获取相关数据。

问题的根源在于数据源的不匹配：和弦进行来自一个来源（已经有自己的歌词对齐方式），而歌词文本来自另一个来源（干净的文本，可能有不同的换行或版本）。当合并这两个来源时，原始的对齐信息就丢失了，系统需要重新猜测对齐方式，而中文的音节歧义性使这个问题更加复杂。至于和弦进行的准确性，则取决于找到的和弦谱本身的质量。

让我思考一些具体的改进方法。这个问题的关键在于源数据的合并过程——当前的工作流程从一个地方获取和弦，从另一个地方获取歌词，然后由代理重新合并，这本质上破坏了原始的对齐信息。

最好的解决方案是保留源数据本身的对齐方式。如果找到的和弦图表已经有对齐的标记，那就直接转录它，而不是用LRCLIB的歌词去"改进"它。只有在完全没有对齐图表的情况下，才应该从头开始填充和弦。

另一个问题是不同来源使用的标记格式差异——比如Chord4使用带括号的音节标记，这需要特殊处理。

而LRCLIB只能提供行级别的时间戳，不是字级别的，所以要获得更精细的对齐，需要依赖其他资源，比如强制对齐工具或者图表网站本身已有的标记。

音频提取的和弦进行准确度大约在80%左右，对于大小调还可以，但对于七和弦、扩展和弦、转位和弦这些就不太行了。中文流行音乐里这类复杂和弦很常见，所以需要用更好的模型或者加入音乐理论的后处理，比如用维特比算法在调性约束下平滑和弦序列，或者让和弦变化与节拍对齐。

和弦变化几乎总是发生在节拍上，通常是在小节线或强拍处。如果逐帧提取和弦而不对齐到节拍网格，变化点会很嘈杂。用节拍同步的和弦识别方法能大幅清理"和弦何时变化"这个问题。

现在我来整理一下真正能提升效果的改进方案，按投入产出比排序。最关键的是停止重新合并，保留源对齐——这是单一最有影响力的改变，而且不需要新的依赖。当一个谱子已经有和弦-歌词对齐时，应该直接保留这个信息。

只有在没有对齐谱子的情况下才去找LRCLIB的歌词。

282	- `references/audio-to-chords.md` — Read **when** the user wants chords from an
283	  audio file or a link (ACR tool choice, beat/key, limits, escape hatches).
284	- `references/lyrics-sources.md` — Read **when** fetching lyrics (source table,
285	  synced-vs-plain, API-vs-scrape, legality, LRCLIB API).

287	## Gotchas
288	
289	- **macOS has no official Homebrew `chordpro`** — install via CPAN
290	  (`brew install perl cpanminus && cpanm App::Music::ChordPro`). A signed `.dmg`
291	  GUI exists on GitHub Releases but the CLI is the CPAN route.
292	- **`Can't locate ChordPro.pm in @INC` after cpanm** — cpanm installed into a
293	  `local::lib` (`~/perl5`) that isn't on Perl's path. Activate it:
294	  `eval "$(perl -I"$HOME/perl5/lib/perl5" -Mlocal::lib)"` (persist in `~/.zshrc`).
295	- **No standalone `a2crd` in ChordPro 6.x** — use `chordpro --a2crd input.txt`.
296	  Its output needs a human pass (heuristic, column-based chord placement); always
297	  validate and eyeball before rendering.
298	- **Angle brackets `< >` are text markup in ChordPro v6.** Don't put `<...>`
299	  placeholders in lyrics/chords — the parser reads `<b>`/`<i>`-style markup and
300	  floods warnings. Use plain-text placeholders (see `assets/template-song.cho`).
301	- **No official online validator.** chordpro.org hosts docs + a desktop GUI, not
302	  a "try it online" box. Validate locally with the CLI (`validate-cho.sh`).
303	- **CJK renders as tofu by default — and passes validation.** `chordpro`'s default
304	  fonts have no Han/Kana/Hangul glyphs, so a Chinese/Japanese/Korean song produces
305	  a blank PDF that still exits 0 and passes `validate-cho.sh` (which only checks
306	  parsing). Render CJK with `scripts/render-cho.sh` (auto CJK font + glyph-check),
307	  or pass `--config` pointing `pdf.fonts.*` at a CJK font.
308	- **`a2crd` is Latin-only.** Its column heuristic assumes 1 char = 1 column, but
309	  full-width CJK occupies 2 display cells, so chords drift. For CJK, align chords to
310	  syllables/phrases by musical judgment — don't trust column arithmetic.
311	- **A strict "Unknown chord" warning ≠ a parse error.** `chordpro --strict` warns
312	  "Unknown chord" for a *valid* chord it has no built-in diagram for (e.g. `Em/C#`,
313	  `F#m7b5`); it still renders. Add a `{define}` (see the format reference) or ignore.
314	- **`{chorus}` recall is a trap with 2+ recurring sections.** It reprints only the
315	  most-recently-defined chorus, as a bare "Chorus" tag by default. Label distinct
316	  blocks (`{start_of_chorus: name}` / `{chorus: name}`) or expand repeats explicitly.
317	- **`WebFetch` strips copyrighted lyrics** (returns "[lyrics omitted]"), so the
318	  chart-fetch path needs raw `curl` + per-site parsing; and from an image-only chart
319	  `WebFetch` may *fabricate* chord placement — trust only an explicit chord list.
320	- **Chord accuracy from audio is ~80% at best** on simple pop, worse otherwise.
321	  Never present a machine-extracted sheet without the `AUTO-GENERATED` header and
322	  a "verify chords/key/timing" caveat.
323	- **Auto-generated chart sites are ACR in disguise.** Chordu / Chordify /
324	  GuitarTuna charts are machine-derived (~80%, same caveat) — treat them as drafts,
325	  unlike human-made charts on 91譜 / Chord4 / Ultimate Guitar.
326	- **Detected key is a suggestion.** ACR outputs absolute pitches; key detection
327	  confuses relative major/minor and keys a fifth apart, and enharmonic spelling
328	  (Gb vs F#) is ambiguous. Confirm with the user before committing `{key:}`.
329	- **Chords in `{sot}`…`{eot}` tab blocks are NOT parsed** — that's for ASCII tab.
330	  Use inline `[..]` in verses/choruses; reserve tab blocks for fret diagrams.
331	- **Lyrics/audio ToS.** Prefer LRCLIB (open); most other lyric sources are
332	  scrape-only or paid, and downloading audio has copyright/ToS limits. Keep it
333	  personal-use and local; surface the caveat rather than hiding it.
334

9	chart is found.
10	
11	This is the router's highest-value path for "make me a chord sheet for `<song>`",
12	and it's what actually happens in practice — treat existing charts as the
13	default source of chords, not an afterthought.
14	
15	## The workflow
16	
17	Verified across a 7-song C-pop batch — the naive "WebFetch → a2crd" path breaks in
18	two ways (WebFetch's summarizer strips copyrighted lyrics; `a2crd` mis-aligns CJK),
19	so the real recipe is:
20	
21	1. **Search.** `WebSearch` for the song + a chart keyword in the right language:
22	   - EN: `"<artist> <title>" chords`, `... ultimate guitar`, `... chordpro`
23	   - 中文: `<歌手> <歌名> 吉他谱`, `... 和弦`, `... 弹唱谱`, `... 简谱`
24	2. **Fetch RAW, then parse the site's markup.** `WebFetch`'s LLM summary **strips the
25	   copyrighted lyrics** (returns "[歌词已移除]" / "[lyrics omitted]"), so you get chords
26	   with no alignment. Instead `curl -sL <url>` the raw HTML and parse the site markup:
27	   - **Chord4** (best for Mandarin): chords are parenthesized syllables like
28	     `你不是真正(的)快樂` (chord sits above the `(char)`), plus `data-chord` attrs,
29	     inside the `tabs_content` `<pre>` block.
30	   - **Ultimate Guitar**: JS-rendered — the chart is in the embedded **`js-store`
31	     `data-content` JSON** as `[ch]C[/ch] … [tab]…[/tab]`.
32	   - **Image-only 六线谱** (common for C-pop — jitahome/qinhun/guistudy…): there is NO
33	     text to parse. `WebFetch` will *confidently fabricate* per-line placement — trust
34	     only an explicit chord **list**, never fabricated alignment.
35	3. **Lyrics come SEPARATELY from LRCLIB** (`scripts/fetch-lyrics.py -o song.lrc`).
36	   Treat LRCLIB lyrics as ground truth (they arrive traditional or simplified —
37	   see below).
38	4. **Align by phrase, not by column.** `chordpro --a2crd` only works on **pure-Latin**
39	   chords-over-lyrics; for CJK its 1-char = 1-column heuristic drifts (full-width
40	   chars are 2 display cells). Place each chord over the syllable/phrase it belongs
41	   to by musical judgment. If the chart omits an intro/interlude, reuse the relevant
42	   verse loop labeled "verify against recording" — never fabricate a specific riff.
43	5. **Validate AND render.** `scripts/validate-cho.sh` (parse) **and**
44	   `scripts/render-cho.sh` (CJK-safe render + glyph-check — a bare `chordpro -o`
45	   renders Chinese as tofu yet passes validation). Caption a `{comment:}` naming the
46	   source + "published arrangement — verify against the recording (capo/key may
47	   differ)". Not machine ACR, so no `AUTO-GENERATED` header.
48	
49	## Where the charts live
50	
51	Coverage and format vary; try a couple, and **don't rely on any single site**
52	(the batch hit `kanpu8` HTTP 403 and `jitapai` expired-TLS). Auto-generated sites
53	are effectively ACR — same ~80% caveat.
54	
55	**Chinese / Taiwan (great for C-pop like the 落葉歸根 case):**
56	- **Chord4 / 和弦网** — `chord4.com` — **the repeat winner** (sourced chords in 6 of 7
57	  eval runs). Raw HTML exposes a parseable chords-over-lyrics block. Start here for Mandarin.
58	- **91譜 / 91pu** — `91pu.com.tw` — large Taiwan library, but **JS-rendered**; `curl`
59	  often returns only page chrome. Good to eyeball, awkward to parse.
60	- **弹唱谱 / 简谱 hubs** — `qupu123`, `中国曲谱网 (qupu.com)`, `17jita`, `jitaba/jitapu`,
61	  `jitahome`, `qinhun`, `guistudy` — **mostly image 六线谱** (manual transcription);
62	  simplified-character search finds more.
63	- **魔鏡歌詞 / Mojim** — `mojim.com` — mostly lyrics, some chords; good for confirming lyrics.
64	
65	**Western / global:**
66	- **Ultimate Guitar** — `ultimate-guitar.com` — largest, but **fully JS-rendered**;
67	  `WebFetch` returns no chords. Parse the `js-store` `data-content` JSON from raw HTML.
68	- **e-chords**, **Chordie**, **AZChords** — chords-over-lyrics, usually parseable.
69	- **Songsterr** — public API for tabs/chords (`songsterr.com/a/wsa/api-tabs-a26570`).
70	- **Chordu / Chordify / GuitarTuna** — **auto-generated from audio** → ACR-quality
71	  (~80%, verify), not human-checked. Use only to corroborate.
72	
73	## Format taxonomy (what you'll get back)
74	
75	| Format | How to use it | Reliability |
76	|---|---|---|
77	| Latin chords-over-lyrics text | `chordpro --a2crd` → clean up → validate | High (human-made) |
78	| CJK chords-over-lyrics text | hand-align by phrase (a2crd drifts on full-width) → validate | High |
79	| Inline / chord chart | transcribe into the ChordPro template | High |
80	| Guitar tab (6-line) | embed in a `{start_of_tab}` block; or use for riffs only | High for riffs |
81	| 简谱 (numbered) / image scan | manual transcription; no reliable OMR — trust only an explicit chord list | Low (tedious) |
82	| Auto-generated (chordu/chordify) | same as ACR — a draft to verify | ~80% |
83	
84	## Simplified vs traditional, and the metadata a chart won't give you
85	
86	- **Char-set mismatch is common**: a simplified-character chart vs traditional LRCLIB
87	  lyrics (or vice versa). Treat the **LRCLIB lyrics as ground truth** and map chords by
88	  position/meaning, not string equality. `opencc` can convert if you must reconcile.
89	- **capo / tempo / composer / year** are usually **absent from text charts**. Get them
90	  from a second source (Wikipedia/Baidu/SongBPM), but **tempo is unreliable** — beware
91	  the half-time trap (a song *felt* at 82 BPM is often listed as 164). Omit an unknown
92	  field or caption it "unverified"; never fabricate.
93	
94	## Legality (surface it, don't bury it)
95	
96	These charts are user-contributed arrangements; the underlying songs are usually
97	copyrighted. Keep it **personal-use and local**, don't redistribute the fetched
98	chart or lyrics commercially, and cite the source in a `{comment:}`. Prefer this
99	route over downloading audio — it avoids the platform-ToS problem entirely — but
100	the copyright of the song itself still applies to any lyrics you embed.
101
```
</details></tool-use>

 `./skills/local/chordpro/references/audio-to-chords.md`

```text
1	# Audio / link → chords: feasibility, tools, and honest limits
2	
3	Read this when the user wants chords from an audio file or a
4	YouTube/Bilibili/SoundCloud link. **The headline: this is a draft generator,
5	not a transcriber.** Set that expectation before running anything.
6	
7	## Accuracy reality — say this out loud
8	
9	Open automatic chord recognition (ACR) at the current state of the art (MIREX
10	2024/2025 Audio Chord Estimation) tops out around **78–80% WCSR on major/minor**,
11	dropping to the **mid-60s% for sevenths**. Models "excel on frequent major/minor
12	chords but underperform on rare seventh and extended chords." So even on simple
13	pop, roughly **1 second in 5 is mislabeled**; jazz, modulations, quiet intros,
14	and dense mixes are much worse, and **inversions / slash chords are unreliable**.
15	The tool also outputs *absolute* pitches — it cannot know the capo a guitarist
16	used. Every machine-extracted sheet ships with a
17	`{comment: AUTO-GENERATED — verify chords/key/timing}` header.
18	
19	## The pipeline
20	
21	```
22	link ─▶ yt-dlp (→ wav)
23	        └▶ [optional] Demucs stem separation (isolate harmonic content — can help ACR)
24	        ─▶ ACR (chord-extractor/Chordino | madmom CNN | Omnizart) ─▶ chord timeline (.lab)
25	        ─▶ beats/downbeats (madmom) + key (Essentia/librosa) ─▶ bar grid + key/tempo
26	lyrics ─▶ LRCLIB (synced) ─first── else ─▶ Musixmatch ─ else ─▶ scrape/plain
27	        └▶ if PLAIN only: forced alignment (WhisperX) to recover line timing
28	merge  ─▶ snap chord onsets to beats; place [Chord] at nearest change per lyric line
29	output ─▶ ChordPro draft with AUTO-GENERATED header + {key}/{tempo}
30	```
31	
32	`scripts/audio-to-chords.py` automates the download → ACR → skeleton portion and
33	degrades gracefully when the ACR backend is missing.
34	
35	## Getting audio: `yt-dlp`
36	
37	Supports **YouTube, SoundCloud, AND Bilibili** (1000+ sites). Needs **ffmpeg**
38	for `-x` audio extraction.
39	
40	```bash
41	# best audio -> wav (best for analysis); swap wav->mp3 for MP3
42	yt-dlp -x --audio-format wav --audio-quality 0 -o "%(title)s.%(ext)s" "URL"
43	```
44	
45	- **Bilibili**: public videos work; higher-res/member content needs
46	  `--cookies-from-browser chrome`.
47	- **SoundCloud**: public tracks work; some are download-disabled/private.
48	- **Legal/ToS**: downloading copyrighted audio generally violates the platform's
49	  ToS and can infringe copyright. Frame as **personal-use, user-owns-or-has-rights**,
50	  process **locally**, **don't redistribute**. Surface this to the user.
51	
52	## ACR tools (audio → time-stamped chords)
53	
54	| Tool | Status (2026) | Invoke | Vocab | When to pick |
55	|---|---|---|---|---|
56	| **chord-extractor** (ohollo) | Maintained (v0.1.3, Aug 2025); wraps **Chordino** | `pip install chord-extractor`; `Chordino(roll_on=1).extract('song.wav')` | maj/min + some 7ths | **Default.** Turnkey on Linux; on macOS/Windows needs a Vamp plugin pack + `VAMP_PATH` (the friction point) |
57	| **madmom** CNN | NN models are best-in-class but install is painful (classifiers cap at Py 3.7; use 3.8–3.9 or the `imcmurray/madmom-modern` fork) | `CNNChordFeatureProcessor` + `CRFChordRecognitionProcessor` | maj/min | Higher accuracy when you can pin the env; also gives **beats/downbeats** |
58	| **Omnizart** | Actively maintained; Docker; Py ≥3.8; heavy (TF + fluidsynth) | `omnizart download-checkpoints` → `omnizart chord transcribe in.wav` | richer | Heavyweight multitask toolbox (also drums/melody/vocal) |
59	| **Chordino / NNLS-Chroma** (Vamp) | Mature C++; the engine under the above | `sonic-annotator -d vamp:nnls-chroma:chordino:simplechord in.wav -w csv` | maj/min + basic 7ths | Cross-platform CLI baseline without Python glue |
60	| **autochord** | Effectively frozen (last release 2021; TF-1.x rot) | `pip install autochord`; `autochord.recognize('a.wav','chords.lab')` | **25: 12 maj + 12 min + N only** | Only if others fail; major/minor only |
61	| **Hugging Face** | Research/demo-grade; **no stable plug-and-play audio→chord model** | Spaces like `tigorsinaga/AI_CHORD_RECOGNITION`; repos `chord-engine`, `Audio-Chord-Recognition` | varies | Mention as "cutting edge", don't depend on it. (`musiclang` is *symbolic* generation, not audio→chord) |
62	
63	**macOS note**: `chord-extractor`'s bundled Chordino binary is Linux-only. On
64	macOS you must install the NNLS-Chroma Vamp plugin and set `VAMP_PATH`, OR fall
65	back to `sonic-annotator` with the plugin, OR run in a Linux container. The
66	script detects the missing plugin and prints this guidance.
67	
68	## Beat / downbeat + key (complements chords)
69	
70	- **madmom** — best NN **beat/downbeat** (`RNNDownBeatProcessor` +
71	  `DBNDownBeatTrackingProcessor`); downbeats give the bar grid to snap chords to.
72	- **librosa** — pure-Python, trivial install: `librosa.beat.beat_track` (tempo +
73	  beats); chroma for a hand-rolled Krumhansl-Schmuckler key estimate.
74	- **Essentia** — `KeyExtractor` (key+scale), `RhythmExtractor2013`; heavier install.
75	- **KeyFinder** — desktop GUI, not a library (`libKeyFinder` C++ if binding).
76	
77	**Key caveat**: detection is ~70–90% and confuses relative major/minor and
78	keys a fifth apart. Treat detected key as a *suggestion*; confirm with the user.
79	
80	## Where it breaks (tell the user)
81	
82	1. Chord accuracy (~80% simple pop; worse on 7ths/jazz/modulation/quiet/dense).
83	2. Chord↔lyric alignment — chords are timestamped; mapping to the exact *syllable*
84	   needs word-level lyric timing (rare — Musixmatch richsync / QQ KRC). Most
85	   drafts land chords at **line** granularity; a human nudges them.
86	3. Capo/key ambiguity + enharmonic spelling.
87	4. Vocabulary mismatch (maj/min-only tools oversimplify sus/add/7 songs).
88	5. Lyrics coverage gaps for niche/Chinese/live tracks → scrape or ASR fallback.
89	
90	## Commercial / reference escape hatches (name-drop only)
91	
92	- **Moises** — real developer/extensions platform (`extensions.moises.ai`,
93	  request access): stems, chords, beat. The one with genuine API access.
94	- **Songsterr** — public API for tabs/chords (CORS-restricted → server-side).
95	- **Chordify** — no official public API.
96	- **Chord AI** — explicitly no API.
97	- **Ultimate Guitar** — no official public API (third-party scrapers only).
98	
99	## Selected sources
100	
101	- chord-extractor: https://github.com/ohollo/chord-extractor
102	- madmom chords: https://madmom.readthedocs.io/en/v0.16/modules/features/chords.html ·
103	  modern fork https://github.com/imcmurray/madmom-modern
104	- Omnizart: https://github.com/Music-and-Culture-Technology-Lab/omnizart
105	- NNLS-Chroma / Chordino: https://isophonics.net/nnls-chroma.html
106	- MIREX ACE results: https://www.music-ir.org/mirex/wiki/2025:Audio_Chord_Estimation_Results
107	- yt-dlp: https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp
108	- Moises API: https://extensions.moises.ai/api-reference · Songsterr API:
109	  https://www.songsterr.com/a/wsa/api-tabs-a26570
